    44→    started_at REAL NOT NULL,
    45→    ended_at REAL,
    46→    end_reason TEXT,
    47→    message_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    48→    tool_call_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    49→    input_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    50→    output_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    51→    title TEXT,
    52→    FOREIGN KEY (parent_session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id)
    53→);
    54→
    55→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
    56→    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    57→    session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
    58→    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    59→    content TEXT,
    60→    tool_call_id TEXT,
    61→    tool_calls TEXT,
    62→    tool_name TEXT,
    63→    timestamp REAL NOT NULL,
    64→    token_count INTEGER,
    65→    finish_reason TEXT
    66→);
    67→
    68→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_source ON sessions(source);
    69→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_parent ON sessions(parent_session_id);
    70→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_started ON sessions(started_at DESC);
    71→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_session ON messages(session_id, timestamp);
    72→"""
    73→
    74→FTS_SQL = """
    75→CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts USING fts5(
    76→    content,
    77→    content=messages,
    78→    content_rowid=id
    79→);
    80→
    81→CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_insert AFTER INSERT ON messages BEGIN
    82→    INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, content) VALUES (new.id, new.content);
    83→END;
    84→
    85→CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_delete AFTER DELETE ON messages BEGIN
    86→    INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, content) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.content);
    87→END;
    88→
    89→CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_update AFTER UPDATE ON messages BEGIN
    90→    INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, content) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.content);
    91→    INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, content) VALUES (new.id, new.content);
    92→END;
    93→"""
    94→
    95→
    96→class SessionDB:
    97→    """
    98→    SQLite-backed session storage with FTS5 search.
    99→
   100→    Thread-safe for the common gateway pattern (multiple reader threads,
   101→    single writer via WAL mode). Each method opens its own cursor.
   102→    """
   103→
   104→    def __init__(self, db_path: Path = None):
   105→        self.db_path = db_path or DEFAULT_DB_PATH
   106→        self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   107→
   108→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   109→        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(
   110→            str(self.db_path),
   111→            check_same_thread=False,
   112→            timeout=10.0,
   113→        )
   114→        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
   115→        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
   116→        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
   117→
   118→        self._init_schema()
   119→
   120→    def _init_schema(self):
   121→        """Create tables and FTS if they don't exist, run migrations."""
   122→        cursor = self._conn.cursor()
   123→
   124→        cursor.executescript(SCHEMA_SQL)
   125→
   126→        # Check schema version and run migrations
   127→        cursor.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_version LIMIT 1")
   128→        row = cursor.fetchone()
   129→        if row is None:
   130→            cursor.execute("INSERT INTO schema_version (version) VALUES (?)", (SCHEMA_VERSION,))
   131→        else:
   132→            current_version = row["version"] if isinstance(row, sqlite3.Row) else row[0]
   133→            if current_version < 2:
   134→                # v2: add finish_reason column to messages
   135→                try:
   136→                    cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN finish_reason TEXT")
   137→                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   138→                    pass  # Column already exists
   139→                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 2")
   140→            if current_version < 3:
   141→                # v3: add title column to sessions
   142→                try:
   143→                    cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN title TEXT")
   144→                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   145→                    pass  # Column already exists
   146→                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 3")
   147→            if current_version < 4:
   148→                # v4: add unique index on title (NULLs allowed, only non-NULL must be unique)
   149→                try:
   150→                    cursor.execute(
   151→                        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
   152→                        "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
   153→                    )
   154→                except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   155→                    pass  # Index already exists
   156→                cursor.execute("UPDATE schema_version SET version = 4")
   157→
   158→        # Unique title index — always ensure it exists (safe to run after migrations
   159→        # since the title column is guaranteed to exist at this point)
   160→        try:
   161→            cursor.execute(
   162→                "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
   163→                "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
   164→            )
   165→        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   166→            pass  # Index already exists
   167→
   168→        # FTS5 setup (separate because CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE can't be in executescript with IF NOT EXISTS reliably)
   169→        try:
   170→            cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM messages_fts LIMIT 0")
   171→        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   172→            cursor.executescript(FTS_SQL)
   173→
   174→        self._conn.commit()
   175→
   176→    def close(self):
   177→        """Close the database connection."""
   178→        with self._lock:
   179→            if self._conn:
   180→                self._conn.close()
   181→                self._conn = None
   182→
   183→    # =========================================================================
   184→    # Session lifecycle
   185→    # =========================================================================
   186→
   187→    def create_session(
   188→        self,
   189→        session_id: str,
   190→        source: str,
   191→        model: str = None,
   192→        model_config: Dict[str, Any] = None,
   193→        system_prompt: str = None,
   194→        user_id: str = None,
   195→        parent_session_id: str = None,
   196→    ) -> str:
   197→        """Create a new session record. Returns the session_id."""
   198→        with self._lock:
   199→            self._conn.execute(
   200→                """INSERT INTO sessions (id, source, user_id, model, model_config,
   201→                   system_prompt, parent_session_id, started_at)
   202→                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
   203→                (
   204→                    session_id,
   205→                    source,
   206→                    user_id,
   207→                    model,
   208→                    json.dumps(model_config) if model_config else None,
   209→                    system_prompt,
   210→                    parent_session_id,
   211→                    time.time(),
   212→                ),
   213→            )
   214→            self._conn.commit()
   215→        return session_id
   216→
   217→    def end_session(self, session_id: str, end_reason: str) -> None:
   218→        """Mark a session as ended."""
   219→        with self._lock:
   220→            self._conn.execute(
   221→                "UPDATE sessions SET ended_at = ?, end_reason = ? WHERE id = ?",
   222→                (time.time(), end_reason, session_id),
   223→            )
   224→            self._conn.commit()
   225→
   226→    def update_system_prompt(self, session_id: str, system_prompt: str) -> None:
   227→        """Store the full assembled system prompt snapshot."""
   228→        with self._lock:
   229→            self._conn.execute(
   230→                "UPDATE sessions SET system_prompt = ? WHERE id = ?",
   231→                (system_prompt, session_id),
   232→            )
   233→            self._conn.commit()
   234→
   235→    def update_token_counts(
   236→        self, session_id: str, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0
   237→    ) -> None:
   238→        """Increment token counters on a session."""
   239→        with self._lock:
   240→            self._conn.execute(
   241→                """UPDATE sessions SET
   242→                   input_tokens = input_tokens + ?,
   243→                   output_tokens = output_tokens + ?
   244→                   WHERE id = ?""",
   245→                (input_tokens, output_tokens, session_id),
   246→            )
   247→            self._conn.commit()
   248→
   249→    def get_session(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   250→        """Get a session by ID."""
   251→        with self._lock:
   252→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   253→                "SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (session_id,)
   254→            )
   255→            row = cursor.fetchone()
   256→        return dict(row) if row else None
   257→
   258→    # Maximum length for session titles
   259→    MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 100
   260→
   261→    @staticmethod
   262→    def sanitize_title(title: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
   263→        """Validate and sanitize a session title.
   264→
   265→        - Strips leading/trailing whitespace
   266→        - Removes ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F) and problematic
   267→          Unicode control chars (zero-width, RTL/LTR overrides, etc.)
   268→        - Collapses internal whitespace runs to single spaces
   269→        - Normalizes empty/whitespace-only strings to None
   270→        - Enforces MAX_TITLE_LENGTH
   271→
   272→        Returns the cleaned title string or None.
   273→        Raises ValueError if the title exceeds MAX_TITLE_LENGTH after cleaning.
   274→        """
   275→        if not title:
   276→            return None
   277→
   278→        import re
   279→
   280→        # Remove ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F) but keep
   281→        # whitespace chars (\t=0x09, \n=0x0A, \r=0x0D) so they can be
   282→        # normalized to spaces by the whitespace collapsing step below
   283→        cleaned = re.sub(r'[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]', '', title)
   284→
   285→        # Remove problematic Unicode control characters:
   286→        # - Zero-width chars (U+200B-U+200F, U+FEFF)
   287→        # - Directional overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069)
   288→        # - Object replacement (U+FFFC), interlinear annotation (U+FFF9-U+FFFB)
   289→        cleaned = re.sub(
   290→            r'[\u200b-\u200f\u2028-\u202e\u2060-\u2069\ufeff\ufffc\ufff9-\ufffb]',
   291→            '', cleaned,
   292→        )
   293→
   294→        # Collapse internal whitespace runs and strip
   295→        cleaned = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', cleaned).strip()
   296→
   297→        if not cleaned:
   298→            return None
   299→
   300→        if len(cleaned) > SessionDB.MAX_TITLE_LENGTH:
   301→            raise ValueError(
   302→                f"Title too long ({len(cleaned)} chars, max {SessionDB.MAX_TITLE_LENGTH})"
   303→            )
   304→
   305→        return cleaned
   306→
   307→    def set_session_title(self, session_id: str, title: str) -> bool:
   308→        """Set or update a session's title.
   309→
   310→        Returns True if session was found and title was set.
   311→        Raises ValueError if title is already in use by another session,
   312→        or if the title fails validation (too long, invalid characters).
   313→        Empty/whitespace-only strings are normalized to None (clearing the title).
   314→        """
   315→        title = self.sanitize_title(title)
   316→        with self._lock:
   317→            if title:
   318→                # Check uniqueness (allow the same session to keep its own title)
   319→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   320→                    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ?",
   321→                    (title, session_id),
   322→                )
   323→                conflict = cursor.fetchone()
   324→                if conflict:
   325→                    raise ValueError(
   326→                        f"Title '{title}' is already in use by session {conflict['id']}"
   327→                    )
   328→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   329→                "UPDATE sessions SET title = ? WHERE id = ?",
   330→                (title, session_id),
   331→            )
   332→            self._conn.commit()
   333→            return cursor.rowcount > 0
   334→
   335→    def get_session_title(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
   336→        """Get the title for a session, or None."""
   337→        with self._lock:
   338→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   339→                "SELECT title FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (session_id,)
   340→            )
   341→            row = cursor.fetchone()
   342→        return row["title"] if row else None
   343→
   344→    def get_session_by_title(self, title: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   345→        """Look up a session by exact title. Returns session dict or None."""
   346→        with self._lock:
   347→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   348→                "SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE title = ?", (title,)
   349→            )
   350→            row = cursor.fetchone()
   351→        return dict(row) if row else None
   352→
   353→    def resolve_session_by_title(self, title: str) -> Optional[str]:
   354→        """Resolve a title to a session ID, preferring the latest in a lineage.
   355→
   356→        If the exact title exists, returns that session's ID.
   357→        If not, searches for "title #N" variants and returns the latest one.
   358→        If the exact title exists AND numbered variants exist, returns the
   359→        latest numbered variant (the most recent continuation).
   360→        """
   361→        # First try exact match
   362→        exact = self.get_session_by_title(title)
   363→
   364→        # Also search for numbered variants: "title #2", "title #3", etc.
   365→        # Escape SQL LIKE wildcards (%, _) in the title to prevent false matches
   366→        escaped = title.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")
   367→        with self._lock:
   368→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   369→                "SELECT id, title, started_at FROM sessions "
   370→                "WHERE title LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' ORDER BY started_at DESC",
   371→                (f"{escaped} #%",),
   372→            )
   373→            numbered = cursor.fetchall()
   374→
   375→        if numbered:
   376→            # Return the most recent numbered variant
   377→            return numbered[0]["id"]
   378→        elif exact:
   379→            return exact["id"]
   380→        return None
   381→
   382→    def get_next_title_in_lineage(self, base_title: str) -> str:
   383→        """Generate the next title in a lineage (e.g., "my session" → "my session #2").
   384→
   385→        Strips any existing " #N" suffix to find the base name, then finds
   386→        the highest existing number and increments.
   387→        """
   388→        import re
   389→        # Strip existing #N suffix to find the true base
   390→        match = re.match(r'^(.*?) #(\d+)$', base_title)
   391→        if match:
   392→            base = match.group(1)
   393→        else:
   394→            base = base_title
   395→
   396→        # Find all existing numbered variants
   397→        # Escape SQL LIKE wildcards (%, _) in the base to prevent false matches
   398→        escaped = base.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")
   399→        with self._lock:
   400→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   401→                "SELECT title FROM sessions WHERE title = ? OR title LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\'",
   402→                (base, f"{escaped} #%"),
   403→            )
   404→            existing = [row["title"] for row in cursor.fetchall()]
   405→
   406→        if not existing:
   407→            return base  # No conflict, use the base name as-is
   408→
   409→        # Find the highest number
   410→        max_num = 1  # The unnumbered original counts as #1
   411→        for t in existing:
   412→            m = re.match(r'^.* #(\d+)$', t)
   413→            if m:
   414→                max_num = max(max_num, int(m.group(1)))
   415→
   416→        return f"{base} #{max_num + 1}"
   417→
   418→    def list_sessions_rich(
   419→        self,
   420→        source: str = None,
   421→        limit: int = 20,
   422→        offset: int = 0,
   423→    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   424→        """List sessions with preview (first user message) and last active timestamp.
   425→
   426→        Returns dicts with keys: id, source, model, title, started_at, ended_at,
   427→        message_count, preview (first 60 chars of first user message),
   428→        last_active (timestamp of last message).
   429→
   430→        Uses a single query with correlated subqueries instead of N+2 queries.
   431→        """
   432→        source_clause = "WHERE s.source = ?" if source else ""
   433→        query = f"""
   434→            SELECT s.*,
   435→                COALESCE(
   436→                    (SELECT SUBSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(m.content, X'0A', ' '), X'0D', ' '), 1, 63)
   437→                     FROM messages m
   438→                     WHERE m.session_id = s.id AND m.role = 'user' AND m.content IS NOT NULL
   439→                     ORDER BY m.timestamp, m.id LIMIT 1),
   440→                    ''
   441→                ) AS _preview_raw,
   442→                COALESCE(
   443→                    (SELECT MAX(m2.timestamp) FROM messages m2 WHERE m2.session_id = s.id),
   444→                    s.started_at
   445→                ) AS last_active
   446→            FROM sessions s
   447→            {source_clause}
   448→            ORDER BY s.started_at DESC
   449→            LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
   450→        """
   451→        params = (source, limit, offset) if source else (limit, offset)
   452→        with self._lock:
   453→            cursor = self._conn.execute(query, params)
   454→            rows = cursor.fetchall()
   455→        sessions = []
   456→        for row in rows:
   457→            s = dict(row)
   458→            # Build the preview from the raw substring
   459→            raw = s.pop("_preview_raw", "").strip()
   460→            if raw:
   461→                text = raw[:60]
   462→                s["preview"] = text + ("..." if len(raw) > 60 else "")
   463→            else:
   464→                s["preview"] = ""
   465→            sessions.append(s)
   466→
   467→        return sessions
   468→
   469→    # =========================================================================
   470→    # Message storage
   471→    # =========================================================================
   472→
   473→    def append_message(
   474→        self,
   475→        session_id: str,
   476→        role: str,
   477→        content: str = None,
   478→        tool_name: str = None,
   479→        tool_calls: Any = None,
   480→        tool_call_id: str = None,
   481→        token_count: int = None,
   482→        finish_reason: str = None,
   483→    ) -> int:
   484→        """
   485→        Append a message to a session. Returns the message row ID.
   486→
   487→        Also increments the session's message_count (and tool_call_count
   488→        if role is 'tool' or tool_calls is present).
   489→        """
   490→        with self._lock:
   491→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   492→                """INSERT INTO messages (session_id, role, content, tool_call_id,
   493→                   tool_calls, tool_name, timestamp, token_count, finish_reason)
   494→                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
   495→                (
   496→                    session_id,
   497→                    role,
   498→                    content,
   499→                    tool_call_id,
   500→                    json.dumps(tool_calls) if tool_calls else None,
   501→                    tool_name,
   502→                    time.time(),
   503→                    token_count,
   504→                    finish_reason,
   505→                ),
   506→            )
   507→            msg_id = cursor.lastrowid
   508→
   509→            # Update counters
   510→            # Count actual tool calls from the tool_calls list (not from tool responses).
   511→            # A single assistant message can contain multiple parallel tool calls.
   512→            num_tool_calls = 0
   513→            if tool_calls is not None:
   514→                num_tool_calls = len(tool_calls) if isinstance(tool_calls, list) else 1
   515→            if num_tool_calls > 0:
   516→                self._conn.execute(
   517→                    """UPDATE sessions SET message_count = message_count + 1,
   518→                       tool_call_count = tool_call_count + ? WHERE id = ?""",
   519→                    (num_tool_calls, session_id),
   520→                )
   521→            else:
   522→                self._conn.execute(
   523→                    "UPDATE sessions SET message_count = message_count + 1 WHERE id = ?",
   524→                    (session_id,),
   525→                )
   526→
   527→            self._conn.commit()
   528→        return msg_id
   529→
   530→    def get_messages(self, session_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   531→        """Load all messages for a session, ordered by timestamp."""
   532→        with self._lock:
   533→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   534→                "SELECT * FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY timestamp, id",
   535→                (session_id,),
   536→            )
   537→            rows = cursor.fetchall()
   538→        result = []
   539→        for row in rows:
   540→            msg = dict(row)
   541→            if msg.get("tool_calls"):
   542→                try:
   543→                    msg["tool_calls"] = json.loads(msg["tool_calls"])
   544→                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
   545→                    pass
   546→            result.append(msg)
   547→        return result
   548→
   549→    def get_messages_as_conversation(self, session_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   550→        """
   551→        Load messages in the OpenAI conversation format (role + content dicts).
   552→        Used by the gateway to restore conversation history.
   553→        """
   554→        with self._lock:
   555→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   556→                "SELECT role, content, tool_call_id, tool_calls, tool_name "
   557→                "FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY timestamp, id",
   558→                (session_id,),
   559→            )
   560→            raw_rows = cursor.fetchall()
   561→        messages = []
   562→        for row in raw_rows:
   563→            msg = {"role": row["role"], "content": row["content"]}
   564→            if row["tool_call_id"]:
   565→                msg["tool_call_id"] = row["tool_call_id"]
   566→            if row["tool_name"]:
   567→                msg["tool_name"] = row["tool_name"]
   568→            if row["tool_calls"]:
   569→                try:
   570→                    msg["tool_calls"] = json.loads(row["tool_calls"])
   571→                except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
   572→                    pass
   573→            messages.append(msg)
   574→        return messages
   575→
   576→    # =========================================================================
   577→    # Search
   578→    # =========================================================================
   579→
   580→    @staticmethod
   581→    def _sanitize_fts5_query(query: str) -> str:
   582→        """Sanitize user input for safe use in FTS5 MATCH queries.
   583→
   584→        FTS5 has its own query syntax where characters like ``"``, ``(``, ``)``,
   585→        ``+``, ``*``, ``{``, ``}`` and bare boolean operators (``AND``, ``OR``,
   586→        ``NOT``) have special meaning.  Passing raw user input directly to
   587→        MATCH can cause ``sqlite3.OperationalError``.
   588→
   589→        Strategy: strip characters that are only meaningful as FTS5 operators
   590→        and would otherwise cause syntax errors.  This preserves normal keyword
   591→        search while preventing crashes on inputs like ``C++``, ``"unterminated``,
   592→        or ``hello AND``.
   593→        """
   594→        # Remove FTS5-special characters that are not useful in keyword search
   595→        sanitized = re.sub(r'[+{}()"^]', " ", query)
   596→        # Collapse repeated * (e.g. "***") into a single one, and remove
   597→        # leading * (prefix-only matching requires at least one char before *)
   598→        sanitized = re.sub(r"\*+", "*", sanitized)
   599→        sanitized = re.sub(r"(^|\s)\*", r"\1", sanitized)
   600→        # Remove dangling boolean operators at start/end that would cause
   601→        # syntax errors (e.g. "hello AND" or "OR world")
   602→        sanitized = re.sub(r"(?i)^(AND|OR|NOT)\b\s*", "", sanitized.strip())
   603→        sanitized = re.sub(r"(?i)\s+(AND|OR|NOT)\s*$", "", sanitized.strip())
   604→        return sanitized.strip()
   605→
   606→    def search_messages(
   607→        self,
   608→        query: str,
   609→        source_filter: List[str] = None,
   610→        role_filter: List[str] = None,
   611→        limit: int = 20,
   612→        offset: int = 0,
   613→    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   614→        """
   615→        Full-text search across session messages using FTS5.
   616→
   617→        Supports FTS5 query syntax:
   618→          - Simple keywords: "docker deployment"
   619→          - Phrases: '"exact phrase"'
   620→          - Boolean: "docker OR kubernetes", "python NOT java"
   621→          - Prefix: "deploy*"
   622→
   623→        Returns matching messages with session metadata, content snippet,
   624→        and surrounding context (1 message before and after the match).
   625→        """
   626→        if not query or not query.strip():
   627→            return []
   628→
   629→        query = self._sanitize_fts5_query(query)
   630→        if not query:
   631→            return []
   632→
   633→        if source_filter is None:
   634→            source_filter = ["cli", "telegram", "discord", "whatsapp", "slack"]
   635→
   636→        # Build WHERE clauses dynamically
   637→        where_clauses = ["messages_fts MATCH ?"]
   638→        params: list = [query]
   639→
   640→        source_placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in source_filter)
   641→        where_clauses.append(f"s.source IN ({source_placeholders})")
   642→        params.extend(source_filter)
   643→
   644→        if role_filter:
   645→            role_placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in role_filter)
   646→            where_clauses.append(f"m.role IN ({role_placeholders})")
   647→            params.extend(role_filter)
   648→
   649→        where_sql = " AND ".join(where_clauses)
   650→        params.extend([limit, offset])
   651→
   652→        sql = f"""
   653→            SELECT
   654→                m.id,
   655→                m.session_id,
   656→                m.role,
   657→                snippet(messages_fts, 0, '>>>', '<<<', '...', 40) AS snippet,
   658→                m.content,
   659→                m.timestamp,
   660→                m.tool_name,
   661→                s.source,
   662→                s.model,
   663→                s.started_at AS session_started
   664→            FROM messages_fts
   665→            JOIN messages m ON m.id = messages_fts.rowid
   666→            JOIN sessions s ON s.id = m.session_id
   667→            WHERE {where_sql}
   668→            ORDER BY rank
   669→            LIMIT ? OFFSET ?
   670→        """
   671→
   672→        with self._lock:
   673→            try:
   674→                cursor = self._conn.execute(sql, params)
   675→            except sqlite3.OperationalError:
   676→                # FTS5 query syntax error despite sanitization — return empty
   677→                return []
   678→            matches = [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
   679→
   680→            # Add surrounding context (1 message before + after each match)
   681→            for match in matches:
   682→                try:
   683→                    ctx_cursor = self._conn.execute(
   684→                        """SELECT role, content FROM messages
   685→                           WHERE session_id = ? AND id >= ? - 1 AND id <= ? + 1
   686→                           ORDER BY id""",
   687→                        (match["session_id"], match["id"], match["id"]),
   688→                    )
   689→                    context_msgs = [
   690→                        {"role": r["role"], "content": (r["content"] or "")[:200]}
   691→                        for r in ctx_cursor.fetchall()
   692→                    ]
   693→                    match["context"] = context_msgs
   694→                except Exception:
   695→                    match["context"] = []
   696→
   697→                # Remove full content from result (snippet is enough, saves tokens)
   698→                match.pop("content", None)
   699→
   700→        return matches
   701→
   702→    def search_sessions(
   703→        self,
   704→        source: str = None,
   705→        limit: int = 20,
   706→        offset: int = 0,
   707→    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   708→        """List sessions, optionally filtered by source."""
   709→        with self._lock:
   710→            if source:
   711→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   712→                    "SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE source = ? ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
   713→                    (source, limit, offset),
   714→                )
   715→            else:
   716→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   717→                    "SELECT * FROM sessions ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
   718→                    (limit, offset),
   719→                )
   720→            return [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
   721→
   722→    # =========================================================================
   723→    # Utility
   724→    # =========================================================================
   725→
   726→    def session_count(self, source: str = None) -> int:
   727→        """Count sessions, optionally filtered by source."""
   728→        with self._lock:
   729→            if source:
   730→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   731→                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE source = ?", (source,)
   732→                )
   733→            else:
   734→                cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions")
   735→            return cursor.fetchone()[0]
   736→
   737→    def message_count(self, session_id: str = None) -> int:
   738→        """Count messages, optionally for a specific session."""
   739→        with self._lock:
   740→            if session_id:
   741→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   742→                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,)
   743→                )
   744→            else:
   745→                cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages")
   746→            return cursor.fetchone()[0]
   747→
   748→    # =========================================================================
   749→    # Export and cleanup
   750→    # =========================================================================
   751→
   752→    def export_session(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   753→        """Export a single session with all its messages as a dict."""
   754→        session = self.get_session(session_id)
   755→        if not session:
   756→            return None
   757→        messages = self.get_messages(session_id)
   758→        return {**session, "messages": messages}
   759→
   760→    def export_all(self, source: str = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   761→        """
   762→        Export all sessions (with messages) as a list of dicts.
   763→        Suitable for writing to a JSONL file for backup/analysis.
   764→        """
   765→        sessions = self.search_sessions(source=source, limit=100000)
   766→        results = []
   767→        for session in sessions:
   768→            messages = self.get_messages(session["id"])
   769→            results.append({**session, "messages": messages})
   770→        return results
   771→
   772→    def clear_messages(self, session_id: str) -> None:
   773→        """Delete all messages for a session and reset its counters."""
   774→        with self._lock:
   775→            self._conn.execute(
   776→                "DELETE FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,)
   777→            )
   778→            self._conn.execute(
   779→                "UPDATE sessions SET message_count = 0, tool_call_count = 0 WHERE id = ?",
   780→                (session_id,),
   781→            )
   782→            self._conn.commit()
   783→
   784→    def delete_session(self, session_id: str) -> bool:
   785→        """Delete a session and all its messages. Returns True if found."""
   786→        with self._lock:
   787→            cursor = self._conn.execute(
   788→                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (session_id,)
   789→            )
   790→            if cursor.fetchone()[0] == 0:
   791→                return False
   792→            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,))
   793→            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (session_id,))
   794→            self._conn.commit()
   795→            return True
   796→
   797→    def prune_sessions(self, older_than_days: int = 90, source: str = None) -> int:
   798→        """
   799→        Delete sessions older than N days. Returns count of deleted sessions.
   800→        Only prunes ended sessions (not active ones).
   801→        """
   802→        import time as _time
   803→        cutoff = _time.time() - (older_than_days * 86400)
   804→
   805→        with self._lock:
   806→            if source:
   807→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   808→                    """SELECT id FROM sessions
   809→                       WHERE started_at < ? AND ended_at IS NOT NULL AND source = ?""",
   810→                    (cutoff, source),
   811→                )
   812→            else:
   813→                cursor = self._conn.execute(
   814→                    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE started_at < ? AND ended_at IS NOT NULL",
   815→                    (cutoff,),
   816→                )
   817→            session_ids = [row["id"] for row in cursor.fetchall()]
   818→
   819→            for sid in session_ids:
   820→                self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM messages WHERE session_id = ?", (sid,))
   821→                self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ?", (sid,))
   822→
   823→            self._conn.commit()
   824→        return len(session_ids)
   825→

1→"""Shared interrupt signaling for all tools.
     2→
     3→Provides a global threading.Event that any tool can check to determine
     4→if the user has requested an interrupt. The agent's interrupt() method
     5→sets this event, and tools poll it during long-running operations.
     6→
     7→Usage in tools:
     8→    from tools.interrupt import is_interrupted
     9→    if is_interrupted():
    10→        return {"output": "[interrupted]", "returncode": 130}
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import threading
    14→
    15→_interrupt_event = threading.Event()
    16→
    17→
    18→def set_interrupt(active: bool) -> None:
    19→    """Called by the agent to signal or clear the interrupt."""
    20→    if active:
    21→        _interrupt_event.set()
    22→    else:
    23→        _interrupt_event.clear()
    24→
    25→
    26→def is_interrupted() -> bool:
    27→    """Check if an interrupt has been requested. Safe to call from any thread."""
    28→    return _interrupt_event.is_set()
    29→

1→"""Shared utility functions for hermes-agent."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import os
     5→import tempfile
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import Any, Union
     8→
     9→import yaml
    10→
    11→
    12→def atomic_json_write(path: Union[str, Path], data: Any, *, indent: int = 2) -> None:
    13→    """Write JSON data to a file atomically.
    14→
    15→    Uses temp file + fsync + os.replace to ensure the target file is never
    16→    left in a partially-written state.  If the process crashes mid-write,
    17→    the previous version of the file remains intact.
    18→
    19→    Args:
    20→        path: Target file path (will be created or overwritten).
    21→        data: JSON-serializable data to write.
    22→        indent: JSON indentation (default 2).
    23→    """
    24→    path = Path(path)
    25→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    26→
    27→    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
    28→        dir=str(path.parent),
    29→        prefix=f".{path.stem}_",
    30→        suffix=".tmp",
    31→    )
    32→    try:
    33→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    34→            json.dump(data, f, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)
    35→            f.flush()
    36→            os.fsync(f.fileno())
    37→        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    38→    except BaseException:
    39→        try:
    40→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    41→        except OSError:
    42→            pass
    43→        raise
    44→
    45→
    46→def atomic_yaml_write(
    47→    path: Union[str, Path],
    48→    data: Any,
    49→    *,
    50→    default_flow_style: bool = False,
    51→    sort_keys: bool = False,
    52→    extra_content: str | None = None,
    53→) -> None:
    54→    """Write YAML data to a file atomically.
    55→
    56→    Uses temp file + fsync + os.replace to ensure the target file is never
    57→    left in a partially-written state.  If the process crashes mid-write,
    58→    the previous version of the file remains intact.
    59→
    60→    Args:
    61→        path: Target file path (will be created or overwritten).
    62→        data: YAML-serializable data to write.
    63→        default_flow_style: YAML flow style (default False).
    64→        sort_keys: Whether to sort dict keys (default False).
    65→        extra_content: Optional string to append after the YAML dump
    66→            (e.g. commented-out sections for user reference).
    67→    """
    68→    path = Path(path)
    69→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    70→
    71→    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
    72→        dir=str(path.parent),
    73→        prefix=f".{path.stem}_",
    74→        suffix=".tmp",
    75→    )
    76→    try:
    77→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    78→            yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=default_flow_style, sort_keys=sort_keys)
    79→            if extra_content:
    80→                f.write(extra_content)
    81→            f.flush()
    82→            os.fsync(f.fileno())
    83→        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    84→    except BaseException:
    85→        try:
    86→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    87→        except OSError:
    88→            pass
    89→        raise
    90→

843→    def _is_user_authorized(self, source: SessionSource) -> bool:
   844→        """
   845→        Check if a user is authorized to use the bot.
   846→        
   847→        Checks in order:
   848→        1. Per-platform allow-all flag (e.g., DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true)
   849→        2. Environment variable allowlists (TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS, etc.)
   850→        3. DM pairing approved list
   851→        4. Global allow-all (GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true)
   852→        5. Default: deny
   853→        """
   854→        # Home Assistant events are system-generated (state changes), not
   855→        # user-initiated messages.  The HASS_TOKEN already authenticates the
   856→        # connection, so HA events are always authorized.
   857→        if source.platform == Platform.HOMEASSISTANT:
   858→            return True
   859→
   860→        user_id = source.user_id
   861→        if not user_id:
   862→            return False
   863→
   864→        platform_env_map = {
   865→            Platform.TELEGRAM: "TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS",
   866→            Platform.DISCORD: "DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS",
   867→            Platform.WHATSAPP: "WHATSAPP_ALLOWED_USERS",
   868→            Platform.SLACK: "SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS",
   869→            Platform.SIGNAL: "SIGNAL_ALLOWED_USERS",
   870→            Platform.EMAIL: "EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS",

   874→            Platform.DISCORD: "DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
   875→            Platform.WHATSAPP: "WHATSAPP_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",

   877→            Platform.SIGNAL: "SIGNAL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
   878→            Platform.EMAIL: "EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS",
   879→        }
   880→
   881→        # Per-platform allow-all flag (e.g., DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true)
   882→        platform_allow_all_var = platform_allow_all_map.get(source.platform, "")
   883→        if platform_allow_all_var and os.getenv(platform_allow_all_var, "").lower() in ("true", "1", "yes"):

   898→

   900→        allowed_ids = set()

1→"""
     2→Hermes control client — lightweight module for external tools to control
     3→a running Hermes instance (CLI or gateway).
     4→
     5→Usage:
     6→    from gateway.hermes_control_client import HermesControl
     7→
     8→    ctl = HermesControl()  # auto-discovers port from ~/.hermes/control_api.port
     9→
    10→    # Send a message (interrupt mode — stops current work)
    11→    ctl.send_message("Focus on this instead")
    12→
    13→    # Queue a message (processed after current work finishes)
    14→    ctl.send_message("When you're done, also check logs", mode="queue")
    15→
    16→    # Send a slash command
    17→    ctl.send_message("/reset")
    18→    ctl.send_message("/model openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4")
    19→
    20→    # List running sessions
    21→    sessions = ctl.list_sessions()
    22→
    23→    # List available commands
    24→    commands = ctl.list_commands()
    25→
    26→Zero dependencies beyond stdlib (uses urllib, not requests/aiohttp).
    27→"""
    28→
    29→import json
    30→import os
    31→import urllib.request
    32→import urllib.error
    33→from typing import Optional
    34→
    35→DEFAULT_PORT = 47823
    36→PORT_FILE = os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/control_api.port")
    37→
    38→
    39→class HermesControl:
    40→    """Client for the Hermes control API."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: Optional[int] = None):
    43→        if port is None:
    44→            port = self._discover_port()
    45→        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"
    46→
    47→    @staticmethod
    48→    def _discover_port() -> int:
    49→        try:
    50→            with open(PORT_FILE) as f:
    51→                return int(f.read().strip())
    52→        except (OSError, ValueError):
    53→            return DEFAULT_PORT
    54→
    55→    def _request(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict = None) -> dict:
    56→        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
    57→        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None
    58→        req = urllib.request.Request(
    59→            url,
    60→            data=data,
    61→            method=method,
    62→            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"} if data else {},
    63→        )
    64→        try:
    65→            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as resp:
    66→                return json.loads(resp.read())
    67→        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    68→            return json.loads(e.read())
    69→        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
    70→            return {"error": f"Cannot reach Hermes control API: {e.reason}"}
    71→
    72→    # ── Read-only endpoints ────────────────────────────────────────────
    73→
    74→    def health(self) -> dict:
    75→        """Check if the control API is running."""
    76→        return self._request("GET", "/health")
    77→
    78→    def list_sessions(self) -> dict:
    79→        """List all running agent sessions."""
    80→        return self._request("GET", "/sessions")

   246→            print("🛠️  No tools selected (all filtered out or unavailable)")
   247→
   248→    global _last_resolved_tool_names
   249→    _last_resolved_tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in filtered_tools]
   250→
   251→    return filtered_tools
   252→
   253→
   254→# =============================================================================
   255→# handle_function_call  (the main dispatcher)
   256→# =============================================================================
   257→
   258→# Tools whose execution is intercepted by the agent loop (run_agent.py)
   259→# because they need agent-level state (TodoStore, MemoryStore, etc.).
   260→# The registry still holds their schemas; dispatch just returns a stub error
   261→# so if something slips through, the LLM sees a sensible message.
   262→_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS = {"todo", "memory", "session_search", "delegate_task", "switch_model", "smart_model"}
   263→
   264→
   265→def handle_function_call(
   266→    function_name: str,
   267→    function_args: Dict[str, Any],
   268→    task_id: Optional[str] = None,
   269→    user_task: Optional[str] = None,
   270→    enabled_tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   271→) -> str:
   272→    """
   273→    Main function call dispatcher that routes calls to the tool registry.
   274→
   275→    Args:
   276→        function_name: Name of the function to call.
   277→        function_args: Arguments for the function.
   278→        task_id: Unique identifier for terminal/browser session isolation.
   279→        user_task: The user's original task (for browser_snapshot context).
   280→        enabled_tools: Tool names enabled for this session.  When provided,
   281→                       execute_code uses this list to determine which sandbox
   282→                       tools to generate.  Falls back to the process-global
   283→                       ``_last_resolved_tool_names`` for backward compat.
   284→
   285→    Returns:
   286→        Function result as a JSON string.
   287→    """
   288→    # Notify the read-loop tracker when a non-read/search tool runs,
   289→    # so the *consecutive* counter resets (reads after other work are fine).
   290→    _READ_SEARCH_TOOLS = {"read_file", "search_files"}
   291→    if function_name not in _READ_SEARCH_TOOLS:
   292→        try:
   293→            from tools.file_tools import notify_other_tool_call
   294→            notify_other_tool_call(task_id or "default")
   295→        except Exception:
   296→            pass  # file_tools may not be loaded yet
   297→
   298→    try:
   299→        if function_name in _AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS:
   300→            return json.dumps({"error": f"{function_name} must be handled by the agent loop"})
   301→
   302→        if function_name == "execute_code":
   303→            # Prefer the caller-provided list so subagents can't overwrite
   304→            # the parent's tool set via the process-global.
   305→            sandbox_enabled = enabled_tools if enabled_tools is not None else _last_resolved_tool_names
   306→            return registry.dispatch(
   307→                function_name, function_args,
   308→                task_id=task_id,
   309→                enabled_tools=sandbox_enabled,
   310→            )
   311→
   312→        return registry.dispatch(
   313→            function_name, function_args,
   314→            task_id=task_id,
   315→            user_task=user_task,
   316→        )
   317→
   318→    except Exception as e:
   319→        error_msg = f"Error executing {function_name}: {str(e)}"
   320→        logger.error(error_msg)
   321→        return json.dumps({"error": error_msg}, ensure_ascii=False)
   322→
   323→
   324→# =============================================================================
   325→# Backward-compat wrapper functions
   326→# =============================================================================
   327→
   328→def get_all_tool_names() -> List[str]:
   329→    """Return all registered tool names."""
   330→    return registry.get_all_tool_names()
   331→
   332→
   333→def get_toolset_for_tool(tool_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
   334→    """Return the toolset a tool belongs to."""
   335→    return registry.get_toolset_for_tool(tool_name)
   336→
   337→
   338→def get_available_toolsets() -> Dict[str, dict]:
   339→    """Return toolset availability info for UI display."""
   340→    return registry.get_available_toolsets()
   341→
   342→
   343→def check_toolset_requirements() -> Dict[str, bool]:
   344→    """Return {toolset: available_bool} for every registered toolset."""
   345→    return registry.check_toolset_requirements()
   346→
   347→
   348→def check_tool_availability(quiet: bool = False) -> Tuple[List[str], List[dict]]:
   349→    """Return (available_toolsets, unavailable_info)."""
   350→    return registry.check_tool_availability(quiet=quiet)
   351→

     3→Reads the global ~/.honcho/config.json when available, falling back
     4→to environment variables.
     5→
     6→Resolution order for host-specific settings:
     7→  1. Explicit host block fields (always win)
     8→  2. Flat/global fields from config root
     9→  3. Defaults (host name as workspace/peer)

    34→def _normalize_recall_mode(val: str) -> str:
    35→    """Normalize legacy recall mode values (e.g. 'auto' → 'hybrid')."""
    36→    val = _RECALL_MODE_ALIASES.get(val, val)
    37→    return val if val in _VALID_RECALL_MODES else "hybrid"
    38→
    39→
    40→def _resolve_memory_mode(
    41→    global_val: str | dict,
    42→    host_val: str | dict | None,
    43→) -> dict:
    44→    """Parse memoryMode (string or object) into memory_mode + peer_memory_modes.
    45→
    46→    Resolution order: host-level wins over global.
    47→    String form:  applies as the default for all peers.
    48→    Object form:  { "default": "hybrid", "hermes": "honcho", ... }
    49→                  "default" key sets the fallback; other keys are per-peer overrides.
    50→    """
    51→    # Pick the winning value (host beats global)
    52→    val = host_val if host_val is not None else global_val
    53→
    54→    if isinstance(val, dict):
    55→        default = val.get("default", "hybrid")
    56→        overrides = {k: v for k, v in val.items() if k != "default"}
    57→    else:
    58→        default = str(val) if val else "hybrid"
    59→        overrides = {}

   112→class _SafeWriter:
   113→    """Transparent stdout wrapper that catches OSError from broken pipes.
   114→
   115→    When hermes-agent runs as a systemd service, Docker container, or headless

   121→
   122→    This wrapper delegates all writes to the underlying stream and silently

   157→class IterationBudget:
   158→    """Thread-safe shared iteration counter for parent and child agents.
   159→
   160→    Tracks total LLM-call iterations consumed across a parent agent and all
   161→    its subagents.  A single ``IterationBudget`` is created by the parent
   162→    and passed to every child so they share the same cap.
   163→
   164→    ``execute_code`` (programmatic tool calling) iterations are refunded via
   165→    :meth:`refund` so they don't eat into the budget.
   166→    """
   167→
   168→    def __init__(self, max_total: int):
   169→        self.max_total = max_total
   170→        self._used = 0
   171→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   172→
   173→    def consume(self) -> bool:
   174→        """Try to consume one iteration.  Returns True if allowed."""
   175→        with self._lock:
   176→            if self._used >= self.max_total:
   177→                return False
   178→            self._used += 1
   179→            return True
   180→
   181→    def refund(self) -> None:
   182→        """Give back one iteration (e.g. for execute_code turns)."""
   183→        with self._lock:
   184→            if self._used > 0:
   185→                self._used -= 1
   186→
   187→    @property
   188→    def used(self) -> int:
   189→        return self._used
   190→
   191→    @property
   192→    def remaining(self) -> int:
   193→        with self._lock:
   194→            return max(0, self.max_total - self._used)
   195→

1→"""Central registry for all hermes-agent tools.
     2→
     3→Each tool file calls ``registry.register()`` at module level to declare its
     4→schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check.  ``model_tools.py``
     5→queries the registry instead of maintaining its own parallel data structures.
     6→
     7→Import chain (circular-import safe):
     8→    tools/registry.py  (no imports from model_tools or tool files)
     9→           ^
    10→    tools/*.py  (import from tools.registry at module level)
    11→           ^
    12→    model_tools.py  (imports tools.registry + all tool modules)
    13→           ^
    14→    run_agent.py, cli.py, batch_runner.py, etc.
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set
    20→
    21→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    22→
    23→
    24→class ToolEntry:
    25→    """Metadata for a single registered tool."""
    26→
    27→    __slots__ = (
    28→        "name", "toolset", "schema", "handler", "check_fn",
    29→        "requires_env", "is_async", "description",
    30→    )
    31→
    32→    def __init__(self, name, toolset, schema, handler, check_fn,
    33→                 requires_env, is_async, description):
    34→        self.name = name
    35→        self.toolset = toolset
    36→        self.schema = schema
    37→        self.handler = handler
    38→        self.check_fn = check_fn
    39→        self.requires_env = requires_env
    40→        self.is_async = is_async
    41→        self.description = description
    42→
    43→
    44→class ToolRegistry:
    45→    """Singleton registry that collects tool schemas + handlers from tool files."""
    46→
    47→    def __init__(self):
    48→        self._tools: Dict[str, ToolEntry] = {}
    49→        self._toolset_checks: Dict[str, Callable] = {}
    50→
    51→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    52→    # Registration
    53→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    54→
    55→    def register(
    56→        self,
    57→        name: str,
    58→        toolset: str,
    59→        schema: dict,
    60→        handler: Callable,
    61→        check_fn: Callable = None,
    62→        requires_env: list = None,
    63→        is_async: bool = False,
    64→        description: str = "",
    65→    ):
    66→        """Register a tool.  Called at module-import time by each tool file."""
    67→        self._tools[name] = ToolEntry(
    68→            name=name,
    69→            toolset=toolset,
    70→            schema=schema,
    71→            handler=handler,
    72→            check_fn=check_fn,
    73→            requires_env=requires_env or [],
    74→            is_async=is_async,
    75→            description=description or schema.get("description", ""),
    76→        )
    77→        if check_fn and toolset not in self._toolset_checks:
    78→            self._toolset_checks[toolset] = check_fn
    79→
    80→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    81→    # Schema retrieval
    82→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    83→
    84→    def get_definitions(self, tool_names: Set[str], quiet: bool = False) -> List[dict]:
    85→        """Return OpenAI-format tool schemas for the requested tool names.
    86→
    87→        Only tools whose ``check_fn()`` returns True (or have no check_fn)
    88→        are included.
    89→        """
    90→        result = []
    91→        for name in sorted(tool_names):
    92→            entry = self._tools.get(name)
    93→            if not entry:
    94→                continue
    95→            if entry.check_fn:
    96→                try:
    97→                    if not entry.check_fn():
    98→                        if not quiet:
    99→                            logger.debug("Tool %s unavailable (check failed)", name)
   100→                        continue
   101→                except Exception:
   102→                    if not quiet:
   103→                        logger.debug("Tool %s check raised; skipping", name)
   104→                    continue
   105→            result.append({"type": "function", "function": entry.schema})
   106→        return result
   107→
   108→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   109→    # Dispatch
   110→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   111→
   112→    def dispatch(self, name: str, args: dict, **kwargs) -> str:
   113→        """Execute a tool handler by name.
   114→
   115→        * Async handlers are bridged automatically via ``_run_async()``.
   116→        * All exceptions are caught and returned as ``{"error": "..."}``
   117→          for consistent error format.
   118→        """
   119→        entry = self._tools.get(name)
   120→        if not entry:
   121→            return json.dumps({"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"})
   122→        try:
   123→            if entry.is_async:
   124→                from model_tools import _run_async
   125→                return _run_async(entry.handler(args, **kwargs))
   126→            return entry.handler(args, **kwargs)
   127→        except Exception as e:
   128→            logger.exception("Tool %s dispatch error: %s", name, e)
   129→            return json.dumps({"error": f"Tool execution failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"})
   130→
   131→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   132→    # Query helpers  (replace redundant dicts in model_tools.py)
   133→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   134→
   135→    def get_all_tool_names(self) -> List[str]:
   136→        """Return sorted list of all registered tool names."""
   137→        return sorted(self._tools.keys())
   138→
   139→    def get_toolset_for_tool(self, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
   140→        """Return the toolset a tool belongs to, or None."""
   141→        entry = self._tools.get(name)
   142→        return entry.toolset if entry else None
   143→
   144→    def get_tool_to_toolset_map(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
   145→        """Return ``{tool_name: toolset_name}`` for every registered tool."""
   146→        return {name: e.toolset for name, e in self._tools.items()}
   147→
   148→    def is_toolset_available(self, toolset: str) -> bool:
   149→        """Check if a toolset's requirements are met.
   150→
   151→        Returns False (rather than crashing) when the check function raises
   152→        an unexpected exception (e.g. network error, missing import, bad config).
   153→        """
   154→        check = self._toolset_checks.get(toolset)
   155→        if not check:

   157→        try:

   163→    def check_toolset_requirements(self) -> Dict[str, bool]:
   164→        """Return ``{toolset: available_bool}`` for every toolset."""
   165→        toolsets = set(e.toolset for e in self._tools.values())
   166→        return {ts: self.is_toolset_available(ts) for ts in sorted(toolsets)}

   169→        """Return toolset metadata for UI display."""
   170→        toolsets: Dict[str, dict] = {}

   173→            if ts not in toolsets:
   174→                toolsets[ts] = {
   175→                    "available": self.is_toolset_available(ts),
   176→                    "tools": [],
   177→                    "description": "",
   178→                    "requirements": [],
   179→                }
   180→            toolsets[ts]["tools"].append(entry.name)
   181→            if entry.requires_env:

   192→            if ts not in result:

   200→            if entry.name not in result[ts]["tools"]:

   202→            for env in entry.requires_env:
   203→                if env not in result[ts]["env_vars"]:

   205→        return result

1→"""System prompt assembly -- identity, platform hints, skills index, context files.
     2→
     3→All functions are stateless. AIAgent._build_system_prompt() calls these to
     4→assemble pieces, then combines them with memory and ephemeral prompts.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import logging
     8→import os
     9→import re
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→from typing import Optional
    12→
    13→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    14→
    15→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16→# Context file scanning — detect prompt injection in AGENTS.md, .cursorrules,
    17→# SOUL.md before they get injected into the system prompt.
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→
    20→_CONTEXT_THREAT_PATTERNS = [
    21→    (r'ignore\s+(previous|all|above|prior)\s+instructions', "prompt_injection"),
    22→    (r'do\s+not\s+tell\s+the\s+user', "deception_hide"),
    23→    (r'system\s+prompt\s+override', "sys_prompt_override"),
    24→    (r'disregard\s+(your|all|any)\s+(instructions|rules|guidelines)', "disregard_rules"),
    25→    (r'act\s+as\s+(if|though)\s+you\s+(have\s+no|don\'t\s+have)\s+(restrictions|limits|rules)', "bypass_restrictions"),
    26→    (r'<!--[^>]*(?:ignore|override|system|secret|hidden)[^>]*-->', "html_comment_injection"),
    27→    (r'<\s*div\s+style\s*=\s*["\'].*display\s*:\s*none', "hidden_div"),
    28→    (r'translate\s+.*\s+into\s+.*\s+and\s+(execute|run|eval)', "translate_execute"),
    29→    (r'curl\s+[^\n]*\$\{?\w*(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL|API)', "exfil_curl"),
    30→    (r'cat\s+[^\n]*(\.env|credentials|\.netrc|\.pgpass)', "read_secrets"),
    31→]
    32→
    33→_CONTEXT_INVISIBLE_CHARS = {
    34→    '\u200b', '\u200c', '\u200d', '\u2060', '\ufeff',
    35→    '\u202a', '\u202b', '\u202c', '\u202d', '\u202e',
    36→}
    37→
    38→
    39→def _scan_context_content(content: str, filename: str) -> str:
    40→    """Scan context file content for injection. Returns sanitized content."""
    41→    findings = []
    42→
    43→    # Check invisible unicode
    44→    for char in _CONTEXT_INVISIBLE_CHARS:
    45→        if char in content:
    46→            findings.append(f"invisible unicode U+{ord(char):04X}")
    47→
    48→    # Check threat patterns
    49→    for pattern, pid in _CONTEXT_THREAT_PATTERNS:
    50→        if re.search(pattern, content, re.IGNORECASE):
    51→            findings.append(pid)
    52→
    53→    if findings:
    54→        logger.warning("Context file %s blocked: %s", filename, ", ".join(findings))
    55→        return f"[BLOCKED: {filename} contained potential prompt injection ({', '.join(findings)}). Content not loaded.]"
    56→
    57→    return content
    58→
    59→# =========================================================================
    60→# Constants

1→"""Shared interrupt signaling for all tools.
     2→
     3→Provides a global threading.Event that any tool can check to determine
     4→if the user has requested an interrupt. The agent's interrupt() method
     5→sets this event, and tools poll it during long-running operations.
     6→
     7→Usage in tools:
     8→    from tools.interrupt import is_interrupted
     9→    if is_interrupted():
    10→        return {"output": "[interrupted]", "returncode": 130}
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import threading
    14→
    15→_interrupt_event = threading.Event()
    16→
    17→
    18→def set_interrupt(active: bool) -> None:
    19→    """Called by the agent to signal or clear the interrupt."""
    20→    if active:
    21→        _interrupt_event.set()
    22→    else:
    23→        _interrupt_event.clear()
    24→
    25→
    26→def is_interrupted() -> bool:
    27→    """Check if an interrupt has been requested. Safe to call from any thread."""
    28→    return _interrupt_event.is_set()
    29→

1→"""Central registry for all hermes-agent tools.
     2→
     3→Each tool file calls ``registry.register()`` at module level to declare its
     4→schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check.  ``model_tools.py``
     5→queries the registry instead of maintaining its own parallel data structures.
     6→
     7→Import chain (circular-import safe):
     8→    tools/registry.py  (no imports from model_tools or tool files)
     9→           ^
    10→    tools/*.py  (import from tools.registry at module level)
    11→           ^
    12→    model_tools.py  (imports tools.registry + all tool modules)
    13→           ^
    14→    run_agent.py, cli.py, batch_runner.py, etc.
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set
    20→
    21→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    22→
    23→
    24→class ToolEntry:
    25→    """Metadata for a single registered tool."""
    26→
    27→    __slots__ = (
    28→        "name", "toolset", "schema", "handler", "check_fn",
    29→        "requires_env", "is_async", "description",
    30→    )
    31→
    32→    def __init__(self, name, toolset, schema, handler, check_fn,
    33→                 requires_env, is_async, description):
    34→        self.name = name
    35→        self.toolset = toolset
    36→        self.schema = schema
    37→        self.handler = handler
    38→        self.check_fn = check_fn
    39→        self.requires_env = requires_env
    40→        self.is_async = is_async
    41→        self.description = description
    42→
    43→
    44→class ToolRegistry:
    45→    """Singleton registry that collects tool schemas + handlers from tool files."""
    46→
    47→    def __init__(self):
    48→        self._tools: Dict[str, ToolEntry] = {}
    49→        self._toolset_checks: Dict[str, Callable] = {}
    50→
    51→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    52→    # Registration
    53→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    54→
    55→    def register(
    56→        self,
    57→        name: str,
    58→        toolset: str,
    59→        schema: dict,
    60→        handler: Callable,
    61→        check_fn: Callable = None,
    62→        requires_env: list = None,
    63→        is_async: bool = False,
    64→        description: str = "",
    65→    ):
    66→        """Register a tool.  Called at module-import time by each tool file."""
    67→        self._tools[name] = ToolEntry(
    68→            name=name,
    69→            toolset=toolset,
    70→            schema=schema,
    71→            handler=handler,
    72→            check_fn=check_fn,
    73→            requires_env=requires_env or [],
    74→            is_async=is_async,
    75→            description=description or schema.get("description", ""),
    76→        )
    77→        if check_fn and toolset not in self._toolset_checks:
    78→            self._toolset_checks[toolset] = check_fn
    79→
    80→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    81→    # Schema retrieval
    82→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    83→
    84→    def get_definitions(self, tool_names: Set[str], quiet: bool = False) -> List[dict]:
    85→        """Return OpenAI-format tool schemas for the requested tool names.
    86→
    87→        Only tools whose ``check_fn()`` returns True (or have no check_fn)
    88→        are included.
    89→        """
    90→        result = []
    91→        for name in sorted(tool_names):
    92→            entry = self._tools.get(name)
    93→            if not entry:
    94→                continue
    95→            if entry.check_fn:
    96→                try:
    97→                    if not entry.check_fn():
    98→                        if not quiet:
    99→                            logger.debug("Tool %s unavailable (check failed)", name)
   100→                        continue
   101→                except Exception:
   102→                    if not quiet:
   103→                        logger.debug("Tool %s check raised; skipping", name)
   104→                    continue
   105→            result.append({"type": "function", "function": entry.schema})
   106→        return result
   107→
   108→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   109→    # Dispatch
   110→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   111→
   112→    def dispatch(self, name: str, args: dict, **kwargs) -> str:
   113→        """Execute a tool handler by name.
   114→
   115→        * Async handlers are bridged automatically via ``_run_async()``.
   116→        * All exceptions are caught and returned as ``{"error": "..."}``
   117→          for consistent error format.
   118→        """
   119→        entry = self._tools.get(name)
   120→        if not entry:
   121→            return json.dumps({"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"})
   122→        try:
   123→            if entry.is_async:
   124→                from model_tools import _run_async
   125→                return _run_async(entry.handler(args, **kwargs))
   126→            return entry.handler(args, **kwargs)
   127→        except Exception as e:
   128→            logger.exception("Tool %s dispatch error: %s", name, e)
   129→            return json.dumps({"error": f"Tool execution failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"})
   130→
   131→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   132→    # Query helpers  (replace redundant dicts in model_tools.py)
   133→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   134→
   135→    def get_all_tool_names(self) -> List[str]:
   136→        """Return sorted list of all registered tool names."""
   137→        return sorted(self._tools.keys())
   138→
   139→    def get_toolset_for_tool(self, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
   140→        """Return the toolset a tool belongs to, or None."""
   141→        entry = self._tools.get(name)
   142→        return entry.toolset if entry else None
   143→
   144→    def get_tool_to_toolset_map(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
   145→        """Return ``{tool_name: toolset_name}`` for every registered tool."""
   146→        return {name: e.toolset for name, e in self._tools.items()}
   147→
   148→    def is_toolset_available(self, toolset: str) -> bool:
   149→        """Check if a toolset's requirements are met.
   150→
   151→        Returns False (rather than crashing) when the check function raises
   152→        an unexpected exception (e.g. network error, missing import, bad config).
   153→        """
   154→        check = self._toolset_checks.get(toolset)
   155→        if not check:
   156→            return True
   157→        try:
   158→            return bool(check())
   159→        except Exception:
   160→            logger.debug("Toolset %s check raised; marking unavailable", toolset)
   161→            return False
   162→
   163→    def check_toolset_requirements(self) -> Dict[str, bool]:
   164→        """Return ``{toolset: available_bool}`` for every toolset."""
   165→        toolsets = set(e.toolset for e in self._tools.values())
   166→        return {ts: self.is_toolset_available(ts) for ts in sorted(toolsets)}
   167→
   168→    def get_available_toolsets(self) -> Dict[str, dict]:
   169→        """Return toolset metadata for UI display."""
   170→        toolsets: Dict[str, dict] = {}
   171→        for entry in self._tools.values():
   172→            ts = entry.toolset
   173→            if ts not in toolsets:
   174→                toolsets[ts] = {
   175→                    "available": self.is_toolset_available(ts),
   176→                    "tools": [],
   177→                    "description": "",
   178→                    "requirements": [],
   179→                }
   180→            toolsets[ts]["tools"].append(entry.name)
   181→            if entry.requires_env:
   182→                for env in entry.requires_env:
   183→                    if env not in toolsets[ts]["requirements"]:
   184→                        toolsets[ts]["requirements"].append(env)
   185→        return toolsets
   186→
   187→    def get_toolset_requirements(self) -> Dict[str, dict]:
   188→        """Build a TOOLSET_REQUIREMENTS-compatible dict for backward compat."""
   189→        result: Dict[str, dict] = {}
   190→        for entry in self._tools.values():
   191→            ts = entry.toolset
   192→            if ts not in result:
   193→                result[ts] = {
   194→                    "name": ts,
   195→                    "env_vars": [],
   196→                    "check_fn": self._toolset_checks.get(ts),
   197→                    "setup_url": None,
   198→                    "tools": [],
   199→                }
   200→            if entry.name not in result[ts]["tools"]:
   201→                result[ts]["tools"].append(entry.name)
   202→            for env in entry.requires_env:
   203→                if env not in result[ts]["env_vars"]:
   204→                    result[ts]["env_vars"].append(env)
   205→        return result
   206→
   207→    def check_tool_availability(self, quiet: bool = False):
   208→        """Return (available_toolsets, unavailable_info) like the old function."""
   209→        available = []
   210→        unavailable = []
   211→        seen = set()
   212→        for entry in self._tools.values():
   213→            ts = entry.toolset
   214→            if ts in seen:

   216→            seen.add(ts)

1→"""
     2→Delivery routing for cron job outputs and agent responses.
     3→
     4→Routes messages to the appropriate destination based on:
     5→- Explicit targets (e.g., "telegram:123456789")
     6→- Platform home channels (e.g., "telegram" → home channel)
     7→- Origin (back to where the job was created)
     8→- Local (always saved to files)
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import logging
    12→from pathlib import Path
    13→from datetime import datetime
    14→from dataclasses import dataclass
    15→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any, Union
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    19→MAX_PLATFORM_OUTPUT = 4000
    20→TRUNCATED_VISIBLE = 3800
