   129→def _build_from_sessions(platform_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
   130→    """Pull known channels/contacts from sessions.json origin data."""
   131→    sessions_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "sessions" / "sessions.json"
   132→    if not sessions_path.exists():
   133→        return []
   134→
   135→    entries = []
   136→    try:
   137→        with open(sessions_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   138→            data = json.load(f)
   139→
   140→        seen_ids = set()
   141→        for _key, session in data.items():
   142→            origin = session.get("origin") or {}
   143→            if origin.get("platform") != platform_name:
   144→                continue
   145→            entry_id = _session_entry_id(origin)
   146→            if not entry_id or entry_id in seen_ids:
   147→                continue
   148→            seen_ids.add(entry_id)
   149→            entries.append({
   150→                "id": entry_id,
   151→                "name": _session_entry_name(origin),
   152→                "type": session.get("chat_type", "dm"),
   153→                "thread_id": origin.get("thread_id"),
   154→            })
   155→    except Exception as e:
   156→        logger.debug("Channel directory: failed to read sessions for %s: %s", platform_name, e)

   158→    return entries

   165→def load_directory() -> Dict[str, Any]:
   166→    """Load the cached channel directory from disk."""
   167→    if not DIRECTORY_PATH.exists():
   168→        return {"updated_at": None, "platforms": {}}
   169→    try:
   170→        with open(DIRECTORY_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   171→            return json.load(f)
   172→    except Exception:
   173→        return {"updated_at": None, "platforms": {}}
   174→
   175→
   176→def resolve_channel_name(platform_name: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
   177→    """
   178→    Resolve a human-friendly channel name to a numeric ID.
   179→
   180→    Matching strategy (case-insensitive, first match wins):
   181→    - Discord: "bot-home", "#bot-home", "GuildName/bot-home"
   182→    - Telegram: display name or group name
   183→    - Slack: "engineering", "#engineering"
   184→    """
   185→    directory = load_directory()
   186→    channels = directory.get("platforms", {}).get(platform_name, [])
   187→    if not channels:
   188→        return None
   189→
   190→    query = name.lstrip("#").lower()
   191→
   192→    # 1. Exact name match
   193→    for ch in channels:
   194→        if ch["name"].lower() == query:
   195→            return ch["id"]
   196→
   197→    # 2. Guild-qualified match for Discord ("GuildName/channel")
   198→    if "/" in query:
   199→        guild_part, ch_part = query.rsplit("/", 1)
   200→        for ch in channels:
   201→            guild = ch.get("guild", "").lower()
   202→            if guild == guild_part and ch["name"].lower() == ch_part:
   203→                return ch["id"]
   204→
   205→    # 3. Partial prefix match (only if unambiguous)
   206→    matches = [ch for ch in channels if ch["name"].lower().startswith(query)]
   207→    if len(matches) == 1:
   208→        return matches[0]["id"]
   209→
   210→    return None
   211→
   212→
   213→def format_directory_for_display() -> str:
   214→    """Format the channel directory as a human-readable list for the model."""
   215→    directory = load_directory()
   216→    platforms = directory.get("platforms", {})
   217→
   218→    if not any(platforms.values()):
   219→        return "No messaging platforms connected or no channels discovered yet."
   220→
   221→    lines = ["Available messaging targets:\n"]
   222→
   223→    for plat_name, channels in sorted(platforms.items()):
   224→        if not channels:
   225→            continue
   226→
   227→        # Group Discord channels by guild
   228→        if plat_name == "discord":
   229→            guilds: Dict[str, List] = {}
   230→            dms: List = []
   231→            for ch in channels:
   232→                guild = ch.get("guild")
   233→                if guild:
   234→                    guilds.setdefault(guild, []).append(ch)
   235→                else:
   236→                    dms.append(ch)
   237→
   238→            for guild_name, guild_channels in sorted(guilds.items()):
   239→                lines.append(f"Discord ({guild_name}):")
   240→                for ch in sorted(guild_channels, key=lambda c: c["name"]):
   241→                    lines.append(f"  discord:#{ch['name']}")
   242→            if dms:
   243→                lines.append("Discord (DMs):")
   244→                for ch in dms:
   245→                    lines.append(f"  discord:{ch['name']}")
   246→            lines.append("")
   247→        else:
   248→            lines.append(f"{plat_name.title()}:")
   249→            for ch in channels:
   250→                type_label = f" ({ch['type']})" if ch.get("type") else ""
   251→                lines.append(f"  {plat_name}:{ch['name']}{type_label}")
   252→            lines.append("")
   253→
   254→    lines.append('Use these as the "target" parameter when sending.')
   255→    lines.append('Bare platform name (e.g. "telegram") sends to home channel.')
   256→
   257→    return "\n".join(lines)
   258→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→Trajectory Compressor
     4→
     5→Post-processes completed agent trajectories to compress them within a target
     6→token budget while preserving training signal quality.
     7→
     8→Compression Strategy:
     9→1. Protect first turns (system, human, first gpt, first tool)
    10→2. Protect last N turns (final actions and conclusions)
    11→3. Compress MIDDLE turns only, starting from 2nd tool response
    12→4. Compress only as much as needed to fit under target
    13→5. Replace compressed region with a single human summary message
    14→6. Keep remaining tool calls intact (model continues working after summary)
    15→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→File Operations Module
     4→
     5→Provides file manipulation capabilities (read, write, patch, search) that work
     6→across all terminal backends (local, docker, singularity, ssh, modal, daytona).
     7→
     8→The key insight is that all file operations can be expressed as shell commands,
     9→so we wrap the terminal backend's execute() interface to provide a unified file API.
    10→
    11→Usage:
    12→    from tools.file_operations import ShellFileOperations
    13→    from tools.terminal_tool import _active_environments
    14→    
    15→    # Get file operations for a terminal environment
    16→    file_ops = ShellFileOperations(terminal_env)
    17→    
    18→    # Read a file
    19→    result = file_ops.read_file("/path/to/file.py")
    20→    
    21→    # Write a file
    22→    result = file_ops.write_file("/path/to/new.py", "print('hello')")
    23→    
    24→    # Search for content
    25→    result = file_ops.search("TODO", path=".", file_glob="*.py")
    26→"""
    27→
    28→import os
    29→import re
    30→import difflib
    31→from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
    32→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    33→from typing import Optional, List, Dict, Any
    34→from pathlib import Path
    35→
    36→
    37→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    38→# Write-path deny list — blocks writes to sensitive system/credential files
    39→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    40→
    41→_HOME = str(Path.home())
    42→
    43→WRITE_DENIED_PATHS = {
    44→    os.path.realpath(p) for p in [
    45→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".ssh", "authorized_keys"),
    46→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".ssh", "id_rsa"),
    47→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".ssh", "id_ed25519"),
    48→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".ssh", "config"),
    49→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".hermes", ".env"),
    50→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".bashrc"),
    51→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".zshrc"),
    52→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".profile"),
    53→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".bash_profile"),
    54→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".zprofile"),
    55→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".netrc"),
    56→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".pgpass"),
    57→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".npmrc"),
    58→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".pypirc"),
    59→        "/etc/sudoers",
    60→        "/etc/passwd",
    61→        "/etc/shadow",
    62→    ]
    63→}
    64→
    65→WRITE_DENIED_PREFIXES = [
    66→    os.path.realpath(p) + os.sep for p in [
    67→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".ssh"),
    68→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".aws"),
    69→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".gnupg"),
    70→        os.path.join(_HOME, ".kube"),
    71→        "/etc/sudoers.d",
    72→        "/etc/systemd",
    73→    ]
    74→]
    75→
    76→
    77→def _is_write_denied(path: str) -> bool:
    78→    """Return True if path is on the write deny list."""
    79→    resolved = os.path.realpath(os.path.expanduser(path))
    80→    if resolved in WRITE_DENIED_PATHS:
    81→        return True
    82→    for prefix in WRITE_DENIED_PREFIXES:
    83→        if resolved.startswith(prefix):
    84→            return True
    85→    return False
    86→
    87→
    88→# =============================================================================
    89→# Result Data Classes
    90→# =============================================================================
    91→
    92→@dataclass
    93→class ReadResult:
    94→    """Result from reading a file."""
    95→    content: str = ""
    96→    total_lines: int = 0
    97→    file_size: int = 0
    98→    truncated: bool = False
    99→    hint: Optional[str] = None
   100→    is_binary: bool = False

  3724→        # Track this agent as running for this session (for interrupt support)

  3760→            loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
  3761→            response = await loop.run_in_executor(None, run_sync)

  3763→            # Check if we were interrupted and have a pending message

  3765→            adapter = self.adapters.get(source.platform)
  3766→

  3768→            # Use session_key (not source.chat_id) to match adapter's storage keys.
  3769→            pending = None
  3770→            if result and result.get("interrupted") and adapter:
  3771→                pending_event = adapter.get_pending_message(session_key) if session_key else None
  3772→                if pending_event:

  3795→                    history=updated_history,
  3796→                    source=source,
  3797→                    session_id=session_id,
  3798→                    session_key=session_key

  3811→            # Wait for cancelled tasks
  3812→            for task in [progress_task, interrupt_monitor, tracking_task]:

  3814→                    try:
  3815→                        await task
  3816→                    except asyncio.CancelledError:
  3817→                        pass

  3819→        return response

   156→    def get_connected_platforms(self) -> List[Platform]:
   157→        """Return list of platforms that are enabled and configured."""
   158→        connected = []
   159→        for platform, config in self.platforms.items():
   160→            if not config.enabled:
   161→                continue
   162→            # Platforms that use token/api_key auth
   163→            if config.token or config.api_key:
   164→                connected.append(platform)
   165→            # WhatsApp uses enabled flag only (bridge handles auth)

   173→                connected.append(platform)

1→"""
     2→Event Hook System
     3→
     4→A lightweight event-driven system that fires handlers at key lifecycle points.
     5→Hooks are discovered from ~/.hermes/hooks/ directories, each containing:
     6→  - HOOK.yaml  (metadata: name, description, events list)
     7→  - handler.py (Python handler with async def handle(event_type, context))
     8→
     9→Events:
    10→  - gateway:startup     -- Gateway process starts
    11→  - session:start       -- New session created
    12→  - session:reset       -- User ran /new or /reset
    13→  - agent:start         -- Agent begins processing a message
    14→  - agent:step          -- Each turn in the tool-calling loop
    15→  - agent:end           -- Agent finishes processing
    16→  - command:*           -- Any slash command executed (wildcard match)
    17→
    18→Errors in hooks are caught and logged but never block the main pipeline.
    19→"""
    20→
    21→import asyncio
    22→import importlib.util
    23→import os
    24→from pathlib import Path
    25→from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
    26→
    27→import yaml
    28→
    29→
    30→HOOKS_DIR = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/hooks"))
    31→
    32→
    33→class HookRegistry:
    34→    """
    35→    Discovers, loads, and fires event hooks.
    36→
    37→    Usage:
    38→        registry = HookRegistry()
    39→        registry.discover_and_load()
    40→        await registry.emit("agent:start", {"platform": "telegram", ...})
    41→    """
    42→
    43→    def __init__(self):
    44→        # event_type -> [handler_fn, ...]
    45→        self._handlers: Dict[str, List[Callable]] = {}
    46→        self._loaded_hooks: List[dict] = []  # metadata for listing
    47→
    48→    @property
    49→    def loaded_hooks(self) -> List[dict]:
    50→        """Return metadata about all loaded hooks."""
    51→        return list(self._loaded_hooks)
    52→
    53→    def discover_and_load(self) -> None:
    54→        """
    55→        Scan the hooks directory for hook directories and load their handlers.
    56→
    57→        Each hook directory must contain:
    58→          - HOOK.yaml with at least 'name' and 'events' keys
    59→          - handler.py with a top-level 'handle' function (sync or async)
    60→        """
    61→        if not HOOKS_DIR.exists():
    62→            return
    63→
    64→        for hook_dir in sorted(HOOKS_DIR.iterdir()):
    65→            if not hook_dir.is_dir():
    66→                continue
    67→
    68→            manifest_path = hook_dir / "HOOK.yaml"
    69→            handler_path = hook_dir / "handler.py"
    70→
    71→            if not manifest_path.exists() or not handler_path.exists():
    72→                continue
    73→
    74→            try:
    75→                manifest = yaml.safe_load(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    76→                if not manifest or not isinstance(manifest, dict):
    77→                    print(f"[hooks] Skipping {hook_dir.name}: invalid HOOK.yaml", flush=True)
    78→                    continue
    79→
    80→                hook_name = manifest.get("name", hook_dir.name)
    81→                events = manifest.get("events", [])
    82→                if not events:
    83→                    print(f"[hooks] Skipping {hook_name}: no events declared", flush=True)
    84→                    continue
    85→
    86→                # Dynamically load the handler module
    87→                spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    88→                    f"hermes_hook_{hook_name}", handler_path
    89→                )
    90→                if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
    91→                    print(f"[hooks] Skipping {hook_name}: could not load handler.py", flush=True)
    92→                    continue
    93→
    94→                module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    95→                spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    96→
    97→                handle_fn = getattr(module, "handle", None)
    98→                if handle_fn is None:
    99→                    print(f"[hooks] Skipping {hook_name}: no 'handle' function found", flush=True)
   100→                    continue
   101→
   102→                # Register the handler for each declared event
   103→                for event in events:
   104→                    self._handlers.setdefault(event, []).append(handle_fn)
   105→
   106→                self._loaded_hooks.append({
   107→                    "name": hook_name,
   108→                    "description": manifest.get("description", ""),
   109→                    "events": events,
   110→                    "path": str(hook_dir),
   111→                })
   112→
   113→                print(f"[hooks] Loaded hook '{hook_name}' for events: {events}", flush=True)
   114→
   115→            except Exception as e:
   116→                print(f"[hooks] Error loading hook {hook_dir.name}: {e}", flush=True)
   117→
   118→    async def emit(self, event_type: str, context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
   119→        """
   120→        Fire all handlers registered for an event.
   121→
   122→        Supports wildcard matching: handlers registered for "command:*" will
   123→        fire for any "command:..." event. Handlers registered for a base type
   124→        like "agent" won't fire for "agent:start" -- only exact matches and
   125→        explicit wildcards.
   126→
   127→        Args:
   128→            event_type: The event identifier (e.g. "agent:start").
   129→            context:    Optional dict with event-specific data.
   130→        """
   131→        if context is None:
   132→            context = {}
   133→
   134→        # Collect handlers: exact match + wildcard match
   135→        handlers = list(self._handlers.get(event_type, []))
   136→
   137→        # Check for wildcard patterns (e.g., "command:*" matches "command:reset")
   138→        if ":" in event_type:
   139→            base = event_type.split(":")[0]
   140→            wildcard_key = f"{base}:*"
   141→            handlers.extend(self._handlers.get(wildcard_key, []))
   142→
   143→        for fn in handlers:
   144→            try:
   145→                result = fn(event_type, context)
   146→                # Support both sync and async handlers
   147→                if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):
   148→                    await result
   149→            except Exception as e:
   150→                print(f"[hooks] Error in handler for '{event_type}': {e}", flush=True)
   151→

   156→    def get_connected_platforms(self) -> List[Platform]:

   261→def load_gateway_config() -> GatewayConfig:
   262→    """
   263→    Load gateway configuration from multiple sources.
   264→    
   265→    Priority (highest to lowest):
   266→    1. Environment variables
   267→    2. ~/.hermes/gateway.json
   268→    3. cli-config.yaml gateway section
   269→    4. Defaults
   270→    """
   271→    config = GatewayConfig()
   272→    
   273→    # Try loading from ~/.hermes/gateway.json
   274→    gateway_config_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "gateway.json"
   275→    if gateway_config_path.exists():
   276→        try:
   277→            with open(gateway_config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   278→                data = json.load(f)
   279→                config = GatewayConfig.from_dict(data)
   280→        except Exception as e:
   281→            print(f"[gateway] Warning: Failed to load {gateway_config_path}: {e}")
   282→    
   283→    # Bridge session_reset from config.yaml (the user-facing config file)
   284→    # into the gateway config. config.yaml takes precedence over gateway.json
   285→    # for session reset policy since that's where hermes setup writes it.
   286→    try:
   287→        import yaml
   288→        config_yaml_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "config.yaml"
   289→        if config_yaml_path.exists():
   290→            with open(config_yaml_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   291→                yaml_cfg = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
   292→            sr = yaml_cfg.get("session_reset")
   293→            if sr and isinstance(sr, dict):
   294→                config.default_reset_policy = SessionResetPolicy.from_dict(sr)
   295→
   296→            # Bridge discord settings from config.yaml to env vars
   297→            # (env vars take precedence — only set if not already defined)
   298→            discord_cfg = yaml_cfg.get("discord", {})
   299→            if isinstance(discord_cfg, dict):
   300→                if "require_mention" in discord_cfg and not os.getenv("DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION"):
   301→                    os.environ["DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION"] = str(discord_cfg["require_mention"]).lower()
   302→                frc = discord_cfg.get("free_response_channels")
   303→                if frc is not None and not os.getenv("DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS"):
   304→                    if isinstance(frc, list):
   305→                        frc = ",".join(str(v) for v in frc)
   306→                    os.environ["DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS"] = str(frc)
   307→    except Exception:
   308→        pass
   309→
   310→    # Override with environment variables
   311→    _apply_env_overrides(config)
   312→    
   313→    # --- Validate loaded values ---
   314→    policy = config.default_reset_policy
   315→
   316→    if not (0 <= policy.at_hour <= 23):
   317→        logger.warning(
   318→            "Invalid at_hour=%s (must be 0-23). Using default 4.", policy.at_hour
   319→        )
   320→        policy.at_hour = 4
   321→
   322→    if policy.idle_minutes is None or policy.idle_minutes <= 0:
   323→        logger.warning(
   324→            "Invalid idle_minutes=%s (must be positive). Using default 1440.",
   325→            policy.idle_minutes,
   326→        )
   327→        policy.idle_minutes = 1440
   328→
   329→    # Warn about empty bot tokens — platforms that loaded an empty string
   330→    # won't connect and the cause can be confusing without a log line.
   331→    _token_env_names = {
   332→        Platform.TELEGRAM: "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN",
   333→        Platform.DISCORD: "DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN",
   334→        Platform.SLACK: "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN",
   335→    }
   336→    for platform, pconfig in config.platforms.items():
   337→        if not pconfig.enabled:
   338→            continue
   339→        env_name = _token_env_names.get(platform)
   340→        if env_name and pconfig.token is not None and not pconfig.token.strip():
   341→            logger.warning(
   342→                "%s is enabled but %s is empty. "
   343→                "The adapter will likely fail to connect.",
   344→                platform.value, env_name,
   345→            )
   346→
   347→    return config

   350→def _apply_env_overrides(config: GatewayConfig) -> None:
   351→    """Apply environment variable overrides to config."""
   352→    
   353→    # Telegram
   354→    telegram_token = os.getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")

   358→        config.platforms[Platform.TELEGRAM].enabled = True

1→"""
     2→Hermes control client — lightweight module for external tools to control
     3→a running Hermes instance (CLI or gateway).
     4→
     5→Usage:
     6→    from gateway.hermes_control_client import HermesControl
     7→
     8→    ctl = HermesControl()  # auto-discovers port from ~/.hermes/control_api.port
     9→
    10→    # Send a message (interrupt mode — stops current work)
    11→    ctl.send_message("Focus on this instead")
    12→
    13→    # Queue a message (processed after current work finishes)
    14→    ctl.send_message("When you're done, also check logs", mode="queue")
    15→
    16→    # Send a slash command
    17→    ctl.send_message("/reset")
    18→    ctl.send_message("/model openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4")
    19→
    20→    # List running sessions
    21→    sessions = ctl.list_sessions()
    22→
    23→    # List available commands
    24→    commands = ctl.list_commands()
    25→
    26→Zero dependencies beyond stdlib (uses urllib, not requests/aiohttp).
    27→"""
    28→
    29→import json
    30→import os
    31→import urllib.request
    32→import urllib.error
    33→from typing import Optional
    34→
    35→DEFAULT_PORT = 47823
    36→PORT_FILE = os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/control_api.port")
    37→
    38→
    39→class HermesControl:
    40→    """Client for the Hermes control API."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: Optional[int] = None):
    43→        if port is None:
    44→            port = self._discover_port()
    45→        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"
    46→
    47→    @staticmethod
    48→    def _discover_port() -> int:
    49→        try:
    50→            with open(PORT_FILE) as f:
    51→                return int(f.read().strip())
    52→        except (OSError, ValueError):
    53→            return DEFAULT_PORT
    54→
    55→    def _request(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict = None) -> dict:
    56→        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
    57→        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None
    58→        req = urllib.request.Request(
    59→            url,
    60→            data=data,
    61→            method=method,
    62→            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"} if data else {},
    63→        )
    64→        try:
    65→            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as resp:
    66→                return json.loads(resp.read())
    67→        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    68→            return json.loads(e.read())
    69→        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
    70→            return {"error": f"Cannot reach Hermes control API: {e.reason}"}
    71→
    72→    # ── Read-only endpoints ────────────────────────────────────────────
    73→
    74→    def health(self) -> dict:
    75→        """Check if the control API is running."""
    76→        return self._request("GET", "/health")
    77→
    78→    def list_sessions(self) -> dict:
    79→        """List all running agent sessions."""
    80→        return self._request("GET", "/sessions")
    81→
    82→    def get_session(self, session_key: str = "_any") -> dict:
    83→        """Get info about a specific session."""
    84→        return self._request("GET", f"/sessions/{session_key}")
    85→
    86→    def list_commands(self) -> dict:
    87→        """List available slash commands."""
    88→        return self._request("GET", "/commands")
    89→
    90→    # ── Message injection ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    91→
    92→    def send_message(
    93→        self,
    94→        text: str,
    95→        session_key: str = "_any",
    96→        mode: str = "interrupt",
    97→    ) -> dict:
    98→        """Send a message (or /command) into a running session.
    99→
   100→        Args:
   101→            text: Message text or slash command (e.g., "hello", "/reset").
   102→            session_key: Session to target. "_any" targets the first running session.
   103→            mode: "interrupt" (default) stops current work; "queue" waits for it to finish.
   104→        """
   105→        return self._request("POST", f"/sessions/{session_key}/message", {
   106→            "text": text,
   107→            "mode": mode,
   108→        })
   109→
   110→    # ── Convenience methods ────────────────────────────────────────────
   111→
   112→    def switch_model(self, provider: str, model: str, **kw) -> dict:
   113→        """Switch model via /model command."""
   114→        return self.send_message(f"/model {provider}:{model}", **kw)
   115→
   116→    def compact_context(self, **kw) -> dict:
   117→        """Trigger context compaction."""
   118→        return self.send_message("/compact", **kw)
   119→
   120→    def reset(self, **kw) -> dict:
   121→        """Reset conversation history."""
   122→        return self.send_message("/reset", **kw)
   123→
   124→    def stop(self, **kw) -> dict:
   125→        """Stop the running agent."""
   126→        return self.send_message("/stop", **kw)
   127→
   128→    def is_autoreply_enabled(self, session_key: str = "_any") -> bool:
   129→        """Check if autoreply is enabled for a session."""
   130→        info = self.get_session(session_key)
   131→        return bool(info.get("autoreply", {}).get("enabled"))
   132→
   133→    def is_available(self) -> bool:
   134→        """Check if a Hermes instance with control API is reachable."""
   135→        try:
   136→            return self.health().get("status") == "ok"
   137→        except Exception:
   138→            return False
   139→

1→"""CLI presentation -- spinner, kawaii faces, tool preview formatting.
     2→
     3→Pure display functions and classes with no AIAgent dependency.
     4→Used by AIAgent._execute_tool_calls for CLI feedback.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import json
     8→import logging
     9→import os
    10→import sys
    11→import threading
    12→import time
    13→
    14→# ANSI escape codes for coloring tool failure indicators
    15→_RED = "\033[31m"
    16→_RESET = "\033[0m"
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→
    21→# =========================================================================
    22→# Skin-aware helpers (lazy import to avoid circular deps)
    23→# =========================================================================
    24→
    25→def _get_skin():
    26→    """Get the active skin config, or None if not available."""
    27→    try:
    28→        from hermes_cli.skin_engine import get_active_skin
    29→        return get_active_skin()
    30→    except Exception:
    31→        return None
    32→
    33→
    34→def get_skin_faces(key: str, default: list) -> list:
    35→    """Get spinner face list from active skin, falling back to default."""
    36→    skin = _get_skin()
    37→    if skin:
    38→        faces = skin.get_spinner_list(key)
    39→        if faces:
    40→            return faces
    41→    return default
    42→
    43→
    44→def get_skin_verbs() -> list:
    45→    """Get thinking verbs from active skin."""
    46→    skin = _get_skin()
    47→    if skin:
    48→        verbs = skin.get_spinner_list("thinking_verbs")
    49→        if verbs:
    50→            return verbs
    51→    return KawaiiSpinner.THINKING_VERBS
    52→
    53→
    54→def get_skin_tool_prefix() -> str:
    55→    """Get tool output prefix character from active skin."""
    56→    skin = _get_skin()
    57→    if skin:
    58→        return skin.tool_prefix
    59→    return "┊"
    60→
    61→
    62→# =========================================================================
    63→# Tool preview (one-line summary of a tool call's primary argument)
    64→# =========================================================================
    65→
    66→def _oneline(text: str) -> str:
    67→    """Collapse whitespace (including newlines) to single spaces."""
    68→    return " ".join(text.split())
    69→
    70→
    71→def build_tool_preview(tool_name: str, args: dict, max_len: int = 40) -> str:
    72→    """Build a short preview of a tool call's primary argument for display."""
    73→    if not args:
    74→        return None
    75→    primary_args = {
    76→        "terminal": "command", "web_search": "query", "web_extract": "urls",
    77→        "read_file": "path", "write_file": "path", "patch": "path",
    78→        "search_files": "pattern", "browser_navigate": "url",
    79→        "browser_click": "ref", "browser_type": "text",
    80→        "image_generate": "prompt", "text_to_speech": "text",
    81→        "vision_analyze": "question", "mixture_of_agents": "user_prompt",
    82→        "skill_view": "name", "skills_list": "category",
    83→        "schedule_cronjob": "name",
    84→        "execute_code": "code", "delegate_task": "goal",
    85→        "clarify": "question", "skill_manage": "name",
    86→    }
    87→
    88→    if tool_name == "process":
    89→        action = args.get("action", "")
    90→        sid = args.get("session_id", "")
    91→        data = args.get("data", "")
    92→        timeout_val = args.get("timeout")
    93→        parts = [action]
    94→        if sid:

    96→        if data:
    97→            parts.append(f'"{_oneline(data[:20])}"')
    98→        if timeout_val and action == "wait":
    99→            parts.append(f"{timeout_val}s")
   100→        return " ".join(parts) if parts else None

   155→async def cache_audio_from_url(url: str, ext: str = ".ogg") -> str:
   156→    """
   157→    Download an audio file from a URL and save it to the local cache.
   158→
   159→    Args:
   160→        url: The HTTP/HTTPS URL to download from.
   161→        ext: File extension including the dot (e.g. ".ogg", ".mp3").
   162→
   163→    Returns:
   164→        Absolute path to the cached audio file as a string.
   165→    """

   168→    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:

   170→            url,
   171→            headers={
   172→                "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; HermesAgent/1.0)",
   173→                "Accept": "audio/*,*/*;q=0.8",
   174→            },
   175→        )
   176→        response.raise_for_status()

   180→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181→# Document cache utilities
   182→#
   183→# Same pattern as image/audio cache -- documents from platforms are downloaded
   184→# here so the agent can reference them by local file path.
   185→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   186→
   187→DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/document_cache"))
   188→
   189→SUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPES = {
   190→    ".pdf": "application/pdf",
   191→    ".md": "text/markdown",
   192→    ".txt": "text/plain",
   193→    ".docx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
   194→    ".xlsx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
   195→    ".pptx": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation",
   196→}
   197→
   198→
   199→def get_document_cache_dir() -> Path:
   200→    """Return the document cache directory, creating it if it doesn't exist."""
   201→    DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   202→    return DOCUMENT_CACHE_DIR
   203→
   204→
   205→def cache_document_from_bytes(data: bytes, filename: str) -> str:
   206→    """
   207→    Save raw document bytes to the cache and return the absolute file path.
   208→
   209→    The cached filename preserves the original human-readable name with a
   210→    unique prefix: ``doc_{uuid12}_{original_filename}``.
   211→
   212→    Args:
   213→        data: Raw document bytes.
   214→        filename: Original filename (e.g. "report.pdf").
   215→
   216→    Returns:
   217→        Absolute path to the cached document file as a string.
   218→
   219→    Raises:
   220→        ValueError: If the sanitized path escapes the cache directory.
   221→    """
   222→    cache_dir = get_document_cache_dir()
   223→    # Sanitize: strip directory components, null bytes, and control characters
   224→    safe_name = Path(filename).name if filename else "document"
   225→    safe_name = safe_name.replace("\x00", "").strip()
   226→    if not safe_name or safe_name in (".", ".."):
   227→        safe_name = "document"
   228→    cached_name = f"doc_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}_{safe_name}"
   229→    filepath = cache_dir / cached_name
   230→    # Final safety check: ensure path stays inside cache dir
   231→    if not filepath.resolve().is_relative_to(cache_dir.resolve()):
   232→        raise ValueError(f"Path traversal rejected: {filename!r}")
   233→    filepath.write_bytes(data)
   234→    return str(filepath)
   235→

   237→def cleanup_document_cache(max_age_hours: int = 24) -> int:
   238→    """
   239→    Delete cached documents older than *max_age_hours*.
   240→
   241→    Returns the number of files removed.
   242→    """
   243→    import time
   244→
   245→    cache_dir = get_document_cache_dir()
   246→    cutoff = time.time() - (max_age_hours * 3600)
   247→    removed = 0
   248→    for f in cache_dir.iterdir():
   249→        if f.is_file() and f.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:
   250→            try:
   251→                f.unlink()
   252→                removed += 1
   253→            except OSError:
   254→                pass
   255→    return removed

   258→class MessageType(Enum):
   259→    """Types of incoming messages."""
   260→    TEXT = "text"
   261→    LOCATION = "location"
   262→    PHOTO = "photo"
   263→    VIDEO = "video"
   264→    AUDIO = "audio"
   265→    VOICE = "voice"

   267→    STICKER = "sticker"
   268→    COMMAND = "command"  # /command style

   271→@dataclass
   272→class MessageEvent:
   273→    """
   274→    Incoming message from a platform.
   275→    
   276→    Normalized representation that all adapters produce.
   277→    """
   278→    # Message content
   279→    text: str
   280→    message_type: MessageType = MessageType.TEXT
   281→    
   282→    # Source information
   283→    source: SessionSource = None
   284→    
   285→    # Original platform data
   286→    raw_message: Any = None
   287→    message_id: Optional[str] = None
   288→    
   289→    # Media attachments
   290→    media_urls: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   291→    media_types: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   292→    
   293→    # Reply context
   294→    reply_to_message_id: Optional[str] = None
   295→    
   296→    # Timestamps
   297→    timestamp: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.now)
   298→    
   299→    def is_command(self) -> bool:
   300→        """Check if this is a command message (e.g., /new, /reset)."""
   301→        return self.text.startswith("/")
   302→    
   303→    def get_command(self) -> Optional[str]:
   304→        """Extract command name if this is a command message."""
   305→        if not self.is_command():
   306→            return None
   307→        # Split on space and get first word, strip the /
   308→        parts = self.text.split(maxsplit=1)
   309→        return parts[0][1:].lower() if parts else None
   310→    
   311→    def get_command_args(self) -> str:
   312→        """Get the arguments after a command."""
   313→        if not self.is_command():
   314→            return self.text
   315→        parts = self.text.split(maxsplit=1)
   316→        return parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""

    21→    """Compresses conversation context when approaching the model's context limit.
    22→
    23→    Algorithm: protect first N + last N turns, summarize everything in between.
    24→    Token tracking uses actual counts from API responses for accuracy.
    25→    """
    26→
    27→    def __init__(
    28→        self,
    29→        model: str,
    30→        threshold_percent: float = 0.50,
    31→        protect_first_n: int = 3,
    32→        protect_last_n: int = 4,
    33→        summary_target_tokens: int = 2500,
    34→        quiet_mode: bool = False,
    35→        summary_model_override: str = None,
    36→        base_url: str = "",
    37→    ):
    38→        self.model = model
    39→        self.base_url = base_url
    40→        self.threshold_percent = threshold_percent
    41→        self.protect_first_n = protect_first_n
    42→        self.protect_last_n = protect_last_n
    43→        self.summary_target_tokens = summary_target_tokens
    44→        self.quiet_mode = quiet_mode
    45→
    46→        self.context_length = get_model_context_length(model, base_url=base_url)
    47→        self.threshold_tokens = int(self.context_length * threshold_percent)
    48→        self.compression_count = 0
    49→        self._context_probed = False  # True after a step-down from context error
    50→
    51→        self.last_prompt_tokens = 0
    52→        self.last_completion_tokens = 0
    53→        self.last_total_tokens = 0
    54→
    55→        self.summary_model = summary_model_override or ""
    56→
    57→    def update_from_response(self, usage: Dict[str, Any]):
    58→        """Update tracked token usage from API response."""
    59→        self.last_prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
    60→        self.last_completion_tokens = usage.get("completion_tokens", 0)
    61→        self.last_total_tokens = usage.get("total_tokens", 0)
    62→
    63→    def should_compress(self, prompt_tokens: int = None) -> bool:
    64→        """Check if context exceeds the compression threshold."""
    65→        tokens = prompt_tokens if prompt_tokens is not None else self.last_prompt_tokens
    66→        return tokens >= self.threshold_tokens
    67→
    68→    def should_compress_preflight(self, messages: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
    69→        """Quick pre-flight check using rough estimate (before API call)."""
    70→        rough_estimate = estimate_messages_tokens_rough(messages)
    71→        return rough_estimate >= self.threshold_tokens
    72→
    73→    def get_status(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    74→        """Get current compression status for display/logging."""
    75→        return {
    76→            "last_prompt_tokens": self.last_prompt_tokens,
    77→            "threshold_tokens": self.threshold_tokens,
    78→            "context_length": self.context_length,
    79→            "usage_percent": (self.last_prompt_tokens / self.context_length * 100) if self.context_length else 0,
    80→            "compression_count": self.compression_count,
    81→        }
    82→
    83→    def _generate_summary(self, turns_to_summarize: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
    84→        """Generate a concise summary of conversation turns.
    85→
    86→        Tries the auxiliary model first, then falls back to the user's main
    87→        model.  Returns None if all attempts fail — the caller should drop
    88→        the middle turns without a summary rather than inject a useless
    89→        placeholder.
    90→        """
    91→        parts = []
    92→        for msg in turns_to_summarize:
    93→            role = msg.get("role", "unknown")
    94→            content = msg.get("content") or ""
    95→            if len(content) > 2000:
    96→                content = content[:1000] + "\n...[truncated]...\n" + content[-500:]
    97→            tool_calls = msg.get("tool_calls", [])
    98→            if tool_calls:
    99→                tool_names = [tc.get("function", {}).get("name", "?") for tc in tool_calls if isinstance(tc, dict)]
   100→                content += f"\n[Tool calls: {', '.join(tool_names)}]"

   300→def get_toolset(name: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   301→    """
   302→    Get a toolset definition by name.
   303→    
   304→    Args:
   305→        name (str): Name of the toolset
   306→        
   307→    Returns:
   308→        Dict: Toolset definition with description, tools, and includes
   309→        None: If toolset not found
   310→    """
   311→    # Return toolset definition
   312→    return TOOLSETS.get(name)
   313→
   314→
   315→def resolve_toolset(name: str, visited: Set[str] = None) -> List[str]:
   316→    """
   317→    Recursively resolve a toolset to get all tool names.
   318→    
   319→    This function handles toolset composition by recursively resolving
   320→    included toolsets and combining all tools.
   321→    
   322→    Args:
   323→        name (str): Name of the toolset to resolve
   324→        visited (Set[str]): Set of already visited toolsets (for cycle detection)
   325→        
   326→    Returns:
   327→        List[str]: List of all tool names in the toolset
   328→    """
   329→    if visited is None:
   330→        visited = set()
   331→    
   332→    # Special aliases that represent all tools across every toolset
   333→    # This ensures future toolsets are automatically included without changes.
   334→    if name in {"all", "*"}:
   335→        all_tools: Set[str] = set()
   336→        for toolset_name in get_toolset_names():
   337→            # Use a fresh visited set per branch to avoid cross-branch contamination
   338→            resolved = resolve_toolset(toolset_name, visited.copy())
   339→            all_tools.update(resolved)
   340→        return list(all_tools)
   341→
   342→    # Check for cycles
   343→    if name in visited:
   344→        print(f"⚠️  Circular dependency detected in toolset '{name}'")
   345→        return []
   346→    
   347→    visited.add(name)
   348→    
   349→    # Get toolset definition
   350→    toolset = TOOLSETS.get(name)
   351→    if not toolset:
   352→        return []
   353→    
   354→    # Collect direct tools
   355→    tools = set(toolset.get("tools", []))
   356→    
   357→    # Recursively resolve included toolsets
   358→    for included_name in toolset.get("includes", []):
   359→        included_tools = resolve_toolset(included_name, visited.copy())
   360→        tools.update(included_tools)
   361→    
   362→    return list(tools)
   363→
   364→
   365→def resolve_multiple_toolsets(toolset_names: List[str]) -> List[str]:
   366→    """
   367→    Resolve multiple toolsets and combine their tools.
   368→    
   369→    Args:
   370→        toolset_names (List[str]): List of toolset names to resolve
   371→        
   372→    Returns:
   373→        List[str]: Combined list of all tool names (deduplicated)
   374→    """
   375→    all_tools = set()
   376→    
   377→    for name in toolset_names:
   378→        tools = resolve_toolset(name)
   379→        all_tools.update(tools)
   380→    
   381→    return list(all_tools)
   382→
   383→
   384→def get_all_toolsets() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
   385→    """
   386→    Get all available toolsets with their definitions.
   387→    
   388→    Returns:
   389→        Dict: All toolset definitions
   390→    """
   391→    return TOOLSETS.copy()
   392→
   393→
   394→def get_toolset_names() -> List[str]:
   395→    """
   396→    Get names of all available toolsets (excluding aliases).
   397→    
   398→    Returns:
   399→        List[str]: List of toolset names
   400→    """
   401→    return list(TOOLSETS.keys())
   402→

   406→def validate_toolset(name: str) -> bool:
   407→    """
   408→    Check if a toolset name is valid.
   409→    
   410→    Args:
   411→        name (str): Toolset name to validate
   412→        
   413→    Returns:
   414→        bool: True if valid, False otherwise
   415→    """
   416→    # Accept special alias names for convenience
   417→    if name in {"all", "*"}:
   418→        return True
   419→    return name in TOOLSETS

   422→def create_custom_toolset(
   423→    name: str,
   424→    description: str,
   425→    tools: List[str] = None,
   426→    includes: List[str] = None
   427→) -> None:
   428→    """
   429→    Create a custom toolset at runtime.
   430→    
   431→    Args:
   432→        name (str): Name for the new toolset
   433→        description (str): Description of the toolset
   434→        tools (List[str]): Direct tools to include
   435→        includes (List[str]): Other toolsets to include
   436→    """
   437→    TOOLSETS[name] = {
   438→        "description": description,
   439→        "tools": tools or [],
   440→        "includes": includes or []
   441→    }
   442→
   443→
   444→
   445→
   446→def get_toolset_info(name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   447→    """
   448→    Get detailed information about a toolset including resolved tools.
   449→    
   450→    Args:
   451→        name (str): Toolset name
   452→        
   453→    Returns:
   454→        Dict: Detailed toolset information
   455→    """
   456→    toolset = get_toolset(name)
   457→    if not toolset:
   458→        return None
   459→    
   460→    resolved_tools = resolve_toolset(name)
   461→    
   462→    return {
   463→        "name": name,
   464→        "description": toolset["description"],
   465→        "direct_tools": toolset["tools"],
   466→        "includes": toolset["includes"],
   467→        "resolved_tools": resolved_tools,
   468→        "tool_count": len(resolved_tools),
   469→        "is_composite": len(toolset["includes"]) > 0
   470→    }
   471→
   472→
   473→def print_toolset_tree(name: str, indent: int = 0) -> None:
   474→    """
   475→    Print a tree view of a toolset and its composition.
   476→    
   477→    Args:
   478→        name (str): Toolset name
   479→        indent (int): Current indentation level
   480→    """
   481→    prefix = "  " * indent
   482→    toolset = get_toolset(name)
   483→    
   484→    if not toolset:
   485→        print(f"{prefix}❌ Unknown toolset: {name}")
   486→        return
   487→    
   488→    # Print toolset name and description
   489→    print(f"{prefix}📦 {name}: {toolset['description']}")
   490→    
   491→    # Print direct tools
   492→    if toolset["tools"]:
   493→        print(f"{prefix}  🔧 Tools: {', '.join(toolset['tools'])}")
   494→    
   495→    # Print included toolsets
   496→    if toolset["includes"]:
   497→        print(f"{prefix}  📂 Includes:")
   498→        for included in toolset["includes"]:
   499→            print_toolset_tree(included, indent + 2)
   500→

   112→class _SafeWriter:
   113→    """Transparent stdout wrapper that catches OSError from broken pipes.
   114→
   115→    When hermes-agent runs as a systemd service, Docker container, or headless
   116→    daemon, the stdout pipe can become unavailable (idle timeout, buffer
   117→    exhaustion, socket reset). Any print() call then raises
   118→    ``OSError: [Errno 5] Input/output error``, which can crash
   119→    run_conversation() — especially via double-fault when the except handler
   120→    also tries to print.
   121→
   122→    This wrapper delegates all writes to the underlying stream and silently
   123→    catches OSError.  It is installed once at the start of run_conversation()
   124→    and is transparent when stdout is healthy (zero overhead on the happy path).
   125→    """
   126→
   127→    __slots__ = ("_inner",)
   128→
   129→    def __init__(self, inner):
   130→        object.__setattr__(self, "_inner", inner)
   131→
   132→    def write(self, data):
   133→        try:
   134→            return self._inner.write(data)
   135→        except OSError:
   136→            return len(data) if isinstance(data, str) else 0
   137→
   138→    def flush(self):
   139→        try:
   140→            self._inner.flush()
   141→        except OSError:
   142→            pass
   143→
   144→    def fileno(self):
   145→        return self._inner.fileno()
   146→
   147→    def isatty(self):

   149→            return self._inner.isatty()

   151→            return False
   152→
   153→    def __getattr__(self, name):

   157→class IterationBudget:
   158→    """Thread-safe shared iteration counter for parent and child agents.
   159→
   160→    Tracks total LLM-call iterations consumed across a parent agent and all
   161→    its subagents.  A single ``IterationBudget`` is created by the parent
   162→    and passed to every child so they share the same cap.
   163→
   164→    ``execute_code`` (programmatic tool calling) iterations are refunded via
   165→    :meth:`refund` so they don't eat into the budget.
   166→    """
   167→
   168→    def __init__(self, max_total: int):
   169→        self.max_total = max_total
   170→        self._used = 0
   171→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
   172→
   173→    def consume(self) -> bool:
   174→        """Try to consume one iteration.  Returns True if allowed."""
   175→        with self._lock:
   176→            if self._used >= self.max_total:
   177→                return False
   178→            self._used += 1
   179→            return True
   180→
   181→    def refund(self) -> None:
   182→        """Give back one iteration (e.g. for execute_code turns)."""
   183→        with self._lock:
   184→            if self._used > 0:
   185→                self._used -= 1
   186→
   187→    @property
   188→    def used(self) -> int:
   189→        return self._used
   190→
   191→    @property
   192→    def remaining(self) -> int:
   193→        with self._lock:
   194→            return max(0, self.max_total - self._used)
   195→

     4→
     5→Usage:
     6→    from gateway.hermes_control_client import HermesControl
     7→
     8→    ctl = HermesControl()  # auto-discovers port from ~/.hermes/control_api.port
     9→
    10→    # Send a message (interrupt mode — stops current work)
    11→    ctl.send_message("Focus on this instead")
    12→
    13→    # Queue a message (processed after current work finishes)
    14→    ctl.send_message("When you're done, also check logs", mode="queue")
    15→
    16→    # Send a slash command
    17→    ctl.send_message("/reset")
    18→    ctl.send_message("/model openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4")
    19→

    21→    sessions = ctl.list_sessions()
    22→
    23→    # List available commands
    24→    commands = ctl.list_commands()
    25→
    26→Zero dependencies beyond stdlib (uses urllib, not requests/aiohttp).
    27→"""
    28→

    31→import urllib.request
    32→import urllib.error

    34→
    35→DEFAULT_PORT = 47823

    38→
    39→class HermesControl:
    40→    """Client for the Hermes control API."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: Optional[int] = None):
    43→        if port is None:
    44→            port = self._discover_port()
    45→        self.base_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"
    46→
    47→    @staticmethod
    48→    def _discover_port() -> int:
    49→        try:
    50→            with open(PORT_FILE) as f:
    51→                return int(f.read().strip())
    52→        except (OSError, ValueError):
    53→            return DEFAULT_PORT
    54→
    55→    def _request(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict = None) -> dict:
    56→        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
    57→        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None
    58→        req = urllib.request.Request(
    59→            url,
    60→            data=data,
    61→            method=method,
    62→            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"} if data else {},
    63→        )
    64→        try:
    65→            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5) as resp:
    66→                return json.loads(resp.read())
    67→        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    68→            return json.loads(e.read())
    69→        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
    70→            return {"error": f"Cannot reach Hermes control API: {e.reason}"}
    71→
    72→    # ── Read-only endpoints ────────────────────────────────────────────
    73→
    74→    def health(self) -> dict:
    75→        """Check if the control API is running."""
    76→        return self._request("GET", "/health")
    77→
    78→    def list_sessions(self) -> dict:
    79→        """List all running agent sessions."""
    80→        return self._request("GET", "/sessions")
    81→
    82→    def get_session(self, session_key: str = "_any") -> dict:
    83→        """Get info about a specific session."""
    84→        return self._request("GET", f"/sessions/{session_key}")
    85→
    86→    def list_commands(self) -> dict:
    87→        """List available slash commands."""
    88→        return self._request("GET", "/commands")
    89→
    90→    # ── Message injection ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    91→
    92→    def send_message(
    93→        self,
    94→        text: str,
    95→        session_key: str = "_any",
    96→        mode: str = "interrupt",
    97→    ) -> dict:
    98→        """Send a message (or /command) into a running session.
    99→
   100→        Args:
   101→            text: Message text or slash command (e.g., "hello", "/reset").
   102→            session_key: Session to target. "_any" targets the first running session.
   103→            mode: "interrupt" (default) stops current work; "queue" waits for it to finish.
   104→        """
   105→        return self._request("POST", f"/sessions/{session_key}/message", {
   106→            "text": text,
   107→            "mode": mode,
   108→        })
   109→
   110→    # ── Convenience methods ────────────────────────────────────────────
   111→
   112→    def switch_model(self, provider: str, model: str, **kw) -> dict:
   113→        """Switch model via /model command."""
   114→        return self.send_message(f"/model {provider}:{model}", **kw)
   115→
   116→    def compact_context(self, **kw) -> dict:
   117→        """Trigger context compaction."""
   118→        return self.send_message("/compact", **kw)
   119→
   120→    def reset(self, **kw) -> dict:
   121→        """Reset conversation history."""
   122→        return self.send_message("/reset", **kw)
   123→
   124→    def stop(self, **kw) -> dict:
   125→        """Stop the running agent."""
   126→        return self.send_message("/stop", **kw)
   127→
   128→    def is_autoreply_enabled(self, session_key: str = "_any") -> bool:
   129→        """Check if autoreply is enabled for a session."""
   130→        info = self.get_session(session_key)
   131→        return bool(info.get("autoreply", {}).get("enabled"))
   132→
   133→    def is_available(self) -> bool:
   134→        """Check if a Hermes instance with control API is reachable."""
   135→        try:
   136→            return self.health().get("status") == "ok"
   137→        except Exception:
   138→            return False

1→"""Central registry for all hermes-agent tools.
     2→
     3→Each tool file calls ``registry.register()`` at module level to declare its
     4→schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check.  ``model_tools.py``
     5→queries the registry instead of maintaining its own parallel data structures.
     6→
     7→Import chain (circular-import safe):
     8→    tools/registry.py  (no imports from model_tools or tool files)
     9→           ^
    10→    tools/*.py  (import from tools.registry at module level)
    11→           ^
    12→    model_tools.py  (imports tools.registry + all tool modules)
    13→           ^
    14→    run_agent.py, cli.py, batch_runner.py, etc.
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set
    20→
    21→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    22→
    23→
    24→class ToolEntry:
    25→    """Metadata for a single registered tool."""
    26→
    27→    __slots__ = (
    28→        "name", "toolset", "schema", "handler", "check_fn",
    29→        "requires_env", "is_async", "description",
    30→    )
    31→
    32→    def __init__(self, name, toolset, schema, handler, check_fn,
    33→                 requires_env, is_async, description):
    34→        self.name = name
    35→        self.toolset = toolset
    36→        self.schema = schema
    37→        self.handler = handler
    38→        self.check_fn = check_fn
    39→        self.requires_env = requires_env
    40→        self.is_async = is_async
    41→        self.description = description
    42→
    43→
    44→class ToolRegistry:
    45→    """Singleton registry that collects tool schemas + handlers from tool files."""
    46→
    47→    def __init__(self):
    48→        self._tools: Dict[str, ToolEntry] = {}
    49→        self._toolset_checks: Dict[str, Callable] = {}
    50→
    51→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    52→    # Registration
    53→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    54→
    55→    def register(
    56→        self,
    57→        name: str,
    58→        toolset: str,
    59→        schema: dict,
    60→        handler: Callable,
    61→        check_fn: Callable = None,
    62→        requires_env: list = None,
    63→        is_async: bool = False,
    64→        description: str = "",
    65→    ):
    66→        """Register a tool.  Called at module-import time by each tool file."""
    67→        self._tools[name] = ToolEntry(
    68→            name=name,
    69→            toolset=toolset,
    70→            schema=schema,
    71→            handler=handler,
    72→            check_fn=check_fn,
    73→            requires_env=requires_env or [],
    74→            is_async=is_async,
    75→            description=description or schema.get("description", ""),
    76→        )
    77→        if check_fn and toolset not in self._toolset_checks:
    78→            self._toolset_checks[toolset] = check_fn
    79→
    80→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    81→    # Schema retrieval
    82→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    83→
    84→    def get_definitions(self, tool_names: Set[str], quiet: bool = False) -> List[dict]:
    85→        """Return OpenAI-format tool schemas for the requested tool names.
    86→
    87→        Only tools whose ``check_fn()`` returns True (or have no check_fn)
    88→        are included.
    89→        """
    90→        result = []
    91→        for name in sorted(tool_names):
    92→            entry = self._tools.get(name)
    93→            if not entry:
    94→                continue
    95→            if entry.check_fn:
    96→                try:
    97→                    if not entry.check_fn():
    98→                        if not quiet:
    99→                            logger.debug("Tool %s unavailable (check failed)", name)
   100→                        continue

     2→"""
     3→SQLite State Store for Hermes Agent.
     4→
     5→Provides persistent session storage with FTS5 full-text search, replacing
     6→the per-session JSONL file approach. Stores session metadata, full message
     7→history, and model configuration for CLI and gateway sessions.
     8→
     9→Key design decisions:
    10→- WAL mode for concurrent readers + one writer (gateway multi-platform)
    11→- FTS5 virtual table for fast text search across all session messages
    12→- Compression-triggered session splitting via parent_session_id chains
    13→- Batch runner and RL trajectories are NOT stored here (separate systems)
    14→- Session source tagging ('cli', 'telegram', 'discord', etc.) for filtering
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→import os
    19→import re
    20→import sqlite3
    21→import threading
    22→import time
    23→from pathlib import Path
    24→from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
    25→
    26→

    32→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (
    33→    version INTEGER NOT NULL
    34→);

    36→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
    37→    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

    43→    parent_session_id TEXT,

    45→    ended_at REAL,
    46→    end_reason TEXT,
    47→    message_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    48→    tool_call_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    49→    input_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    50→    output_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    51→    title TEXT,
    52→    FOREIGN KEY (parent_session_id) REFERENCES sessions(id)
    53→);
    54→
    55→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
    56→    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    57→    session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
    58→    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    59→    content TEXT,
    60→    tool_call_id TEXT,
    61→    tool_calls TEXT,
    62→    tool_name TEXT,
    63→    timestamp REAL NOT NULL,

    66→);
    67→
    68→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_source ON sessions(source);
    69→CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_parent ON sessions(parent_session_id);

    90→def _convert_content_for_responses(content: Any) -> Any:
    91→    """Convert chat.completions content to Responses API format.
    92→
    93→    chat.completions uses:
    94→      {"type": "text", "text": "..."}
    95→      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}}
    96→
    97→    Responses API uses:
    98→      {"type": "input_text", "text": "..."}
    99→      {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}
   100→
   101→    If content is a plain string, it's returned as-is (the Responses API
   102→    accepts strings directly for text-only messages).
   103→    """
   104→    if isinstance(content, str):
   105→        return content
   106→    if not isinstance(content, list):
   107→        return str(content) if content else ""
   108→
   109→    converted: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   110→    for part in content:
   111→        if not isinstance(part, dict):
   112→            continue
   113→        ptype = part.get("type", "")
   114→        if ptype == "text":
   115→            converted.append({"type": "input_text", "text": part.get("text", "")})
   116→        elif ptype == "image_url":
   117→            # chat.completions nests the URL: {"image_url": {"url": "..."}}

   123→            if detail:

   131→            text = part.get("text", "")
   132→            if text:
   133→                converted.append({"type": "input_text", "text": text})
   134→
   135→    return converted or ""

   261→def load_gateway_config() -> GatewayConfig:
   262→    """
   263→    Load gateway configuration from multiple sources.
   264→    
   265→    Priority (highest to lowest):
   266→    1. Environment variables
   267→    2. ~/.hermes/gateway.json
   268→    3. cli-config.yaml gateway section
   269→    4. Defaults
   270→    """
   271→    config = GatewayConfig()
   272→    
   273→    # Try loading from ~/.hermes/gateway.json
   274→    gateway_config_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "gateway.json"
   275→    if gateway_config_path.exists():
   276→        try:
   277→            with open(gateway_config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   278→                data = json.load(f)
   279→                config = GatewayConfig.from_dict(data)
   280→        except Exception as e:
   281→            print(f"[gateway] Warning: Failed to load {gateway_config_path}: {e}")
   282→    
   283→    # Bridge session_reset from config.yaml (the user-facing config file)
   284→    # into the gateway config. config.yaml takes precedence over gateway.json
   285→    # for session reset policy since that's where hermes setup writes it.
   286→    try:
   287→        import yaml
   288→        config_yaml_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "config.yaml"
   289→        if config_yaml_path.exists():
   290→            with open(config_yaml_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   291→                yaml_cfg = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
   292→            sr = yaml_cfg.get("session_reset")
   293→            if sr and isinstance(sr, dict):
   294→                config.default_reset_policy = SessionResetPolicy.from_dict(sr)
   295→
   296→            # Bridge discord settings from config.yaml to env vars
   297→            # (env vars take precedence — only set if not already defined)
   298→            discord_cfg = yaml_cfg.get("discord", {})
   299→            if isinstance(discord_cfg, dict):
   300→                if "require_mention" in discord_cfg and not os.getenv("DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION"):
   301→                    os.environ["DISCORD_REQUIRE_MENTION"] = str(discord_cfg["require_mention"]).lower()
   302→                frc = discord_cfg.get("free_response_channels")
   303→                if frc is not None and not os.getenv("DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS"):
   304→                    if isinstance(frc, list):
   305→                        frc = ",".join(str(v) for v in frc)
   306→                    os.environ["DISCORD_FREE_RESPONSE_CHANNELS"] = str(frc)
   307→    except Exception:
   308→        pass
   309→
   310→    # Override with environment variables
   311→    _apply_env_overrides(config)
   312→    
   313→    # --- Validate loaded values ---
   314→    policy = config.default_reset_policy
   315→
   316→    if not (0 <= policy.at_hour <= 23):
   317→        logger.warning(
   318→            "Invalid at_hour=%s (must be 0-23). Using default 4.", policy.at_hour
   319→        )
   320→        policy.at_hour = 4
   321→
   322→    if policy.idle_minutes is None or policy.idle_minutes <= 0:
   323→        logger.warning(
   324→            "Invalid idle_minutes=%s (must be positive). Using default 1440.",
   325→            policy.idle_minutes,
   326→        )
   327→        policy.idle_minutes = 1440
   328→
   329→    # Warn about empty bot tokens — platforms that loaded an empty string
   330→    # won't connect and the cause can be confusing without a log line.
   331→    _token_env_names = {
   332→        Platform.TELEGRAM: "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN",
   333→        Platform.DISCORD: "DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN",
   334→        Platform.SLACK: "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN",
   335→    }
   336→    for platform, pconfig in config.platforms.items():
   337→        if not pconfig.enabled:
   338→            continue
   339→        env_name = _token_env_names.get(platform)
   340→        if env_name and pconfig.token is not None and not pconfig.token.strip():
   341→            logger.warning(
   342→                "%s is enabled but %s is empty. "
   343→                "The adapter will likely fail to connect.",
   344→                platform.value, env_name,
   345→            )
   346→
   347→    return config

   350→def _apply_env_overrides(config: GatewayConfig) -> None:
   351→    """Apply environment variable overrides to config."""

1→"""Shared auxiliary OpenAI client for cheap/fast side tasks.
     2→
     3→Provides a single resolution chain so every consumer (context compression,
     4→session search, web extraction, vision analysis, browser vision) picks up
     5→the best available backend without duplicating fallback logic.
     6→
     7→Resolution order for text tasks (auto mode):
     8→  1. OpenRouter  (OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
     9→  2. Nous Portal (~/.hermes/auth.json active provider)
    10→  3. Custom endpoint (OPENAI_BASE_URL + OPENAI_API_KEY)
    11→  4. Codex OAuth (Responses API via chatgpt.com with gpt-5.3-codex,
    12→     wrapped to look like a chat.completions client)
    13→  5. Direct API-key providers (z.ai/GLM, Kimi/Moonshot, MiniMax, MiniMax-CN)
    14→     — checked via PROVIDER_REGISTRY entries with auth_type='api_key'
    15→  6. None
    16→
    17→Resolution order for vision/multimodal tasks (auto mode):
    18→  1. OpenRouter
    19→  2. Nous Portal
    20→  3. Codex OAuth (gpt-5.3-codex supports vision via Responses API)
    21→  4. Custom endpoint (for local vision models: Qwen-VL, LLaVA, Pixtral, etc.)
    22→  5. None  (API-key providers like z.ai/Kimi/MiniMax are skipped —
    23→     they may not support multimodal)
    24→
    25→Per-task provider overrides (e.g. AUXILIARY_VISION_PROVIDER,
    26→CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_PROVIDER) can force a specific provider for each task:
    27→"openrouter", "nous", "codex", or "main" (= steps 3-5).
    28→Default "auto" follows the chains above.
    29→
    30→Per-task model overrides (e.g. AUXILIARY_VISION_MODEL,
    31→AUXILIARY_WEB_EXTRACT_MODEL) let callers use a different model slug
    32→than the provider's default.
    33→"""

1→"""Shared utility functions for hermes-agent."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import os
     5→import tempfile
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import Any, Union
     8→
     9→import yaml
    10→
    11→
    12→def atomic_json_write(path: Union[str, Path], data: Any, *, indent: int = 2) -> None:
    13→    """Write JSON data to a file atomically.
    14→
    15→    Uses temp file + fsync + os.replace to ensure the target file is never
    16→    left in a partially-written state.  If the process crashes mid-write,
    17→    the previous version of the file remains intact.
    18→
    19→    Args:
    20→        path: Target file path (will be created or overwritten).
    21→        data: JSON-serializable data to write.
    22→        indent: JSON indentation (default 2).
    23→    """
    24→    path = Path(path)
    25→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    26→
    27→    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
    28→        dir=str(path.parent),
    29→        prefix=f".{path.stem}_",
    30→        suffix=".tmp",
    31→    )
    32→    try:
    33→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    34→            json.dump(data, f, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)
    35→            f.flush()
    36→            os.fsync(f.fileno())
    37→        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    38→    except BaseException:
    39→        try:
    40→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    41→        except OSError:
    42→            pass
    43→        raise
    44→
    45→
    46→def atomic_yaml_write(
    47→    path: Union[str, Path],
    48→    data: Any,
    49→    *,
    50→    default_flow_style: bool = False,
    51→    sort_keys: bool = False,
    52→    extra_content: str | None = None,
    53→) -> None:
    54→    """Write YAML data to a file atomically.
    55→
    56→    Uses temp file + fsync + os.replace to ensure the target file is never
    57→    left in a partially-written state.  If the process crashes mid-write,
    58→    the previous version of the file remains intact.
    59→
    60→    Args:
    61→        path: Target file path (will be created or overwritten).
    62→        data: YAML-serializable data to write.
    63→        default_flow_style: YAML flow style (default False).
    64→        sort_keys: Whether to sort dict keys (default False).
    65→        extra_content: Optional string to append after the YAML dump
    66→            (e.g. commented-out sections for user reference).
    67→    """
    68→    path = Path(path)
    69→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    70→
    71→    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
    72→        dir=str(path.parent),
    73→        prefix=f".{path.stem}_",
    74→        suffix=".tmp",
    75→    )
    76→    try:
    77→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    78→            yaml.dump(data, f, default_flow_style=default_flow_style, sort_keys=sort_keys)
    79→            if extra_content:
    80→                f.write(extra_content)
    81→            f.flush()
    82→            os.fsync(f.fileno())
    83→        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    84→    except BaseException:
    85→        try:
    86→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    87→        except OSError:
    88→            pass
    89→        raise

1→"""
     2→Delivery routing for cron job outputs and agent responses.
     3→
     4→Routes messages to the appropriate destination based on:
     5→- Explicit targets (e.g., "telegram:123456789")
     6→- Platform home channels (e.g., "telegram" → home channel)
     7→- Origin (back to where the job was created)
     8→- Local (always saved to files)
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import logging
    12→from pathlib import Path
    13→from datetime import datetime
    14→from dataclasses import dataclass
    15→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any, Union
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→MAX_PLATFORM_OUTPUT = 4000
    20→TRUNCATED_VISIBLE = 3800
    21→
    22→from .config import Platform, GatewayConfig
    23→from .session import SessionSource
    24→
    25→
    26→@dataclass
    27→class DeliveryTarget:
    28→    """
    29→    A single delivery target.
    30→    
    31→    Represents where a message should be sent:
    32→    - "origin" → back to source
    33→    - "local" → save to local files
    34→    - "telegram" → Telegram home channel
    35→    - "telegram:123456" → specific Telegram chat
    36→    """
    37→    platform: Platform
    38→    chat_id: Optional[str] = None  # None means use home channel
    39→    thread_id: Optional[str] = None
    40→    is_origin: bool = False
    41→    is_explicit: bool = False  # True if chat_id was explicitly specified
    42→    
    43→    @classmethod
    44→    def parse(cls, target: str, origin: Optional[SessionSource] = None) -> "DeliveryTarget":
    45→        """
    46→        Parse a delivery target string.
    47→        
    48→        Formats:
    49→        - "origin" → back to source
    50→        - "local" → local files only
    51→        - "telegram" → Telegram home channel
    52→        - "telegram:123456" → specific Telegram chat
    53→        """
    54→        target = target.strip().lower()
    55→        
    56→        if target == "origin":
    57→            if origin:
    58→                return cls(
    59→                    platform=origin.platform,
    60→                    chat_id=origin.chat_id,
    61→                    thread_id=origin.thread_id,
    62→                    is_origin=True,
    63→                )
    64→            else:
    65→                # Fallback to local if no origin
    66→                return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL, is_origin=True)
    67→        
    68→        if target == "local":
    69→            return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)
    70→        
    71→        # Check for platform:chat_id format
    72→        if ":" in target:
    73→            platform_str, chat_id = target.split(":", 1)
    74→            try:
    75→                platform = Platform(platform_str)
    76→                return cls(platform=platform, chat_id=chat_id, is_explicit=True)
    77→            except ValueError:
    78→                # Unknown platform, treat as local
    79→                return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)
    80→        
    81→        # Just a platform name (use home channel)
    82→        try:
    83→            platform = Platform(target)
    84→            return cls(platform=platform)
    85→        except ValueError:
    86→            # Unknown platform, treat as local
    87→            return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)
    88→    
    89→    def to_string(self) -> str:
    90→        """Convert back to string format."""
    91→        if self.is_origin:
    92→            return "origin"
    93→        if self.platform == Platform.LOCAL:
    94→            return "local"
    95→        if self.chat_id:
    96→            return f"{self.platform.value}:{self.chat_id}"
    97→        return self.platform.value
