   148→def build_session_context_prompt(context: SessionContext) -> str:
   149→    """
   150→    Build the dynamic system prompt section that tells the agent about its context.
   151→    
   152→    This is injected into the system prompt so the agent knows:
   153→    - Where messages are coming from
   154→    - What platforms are connected
   155→    - Where it can deliver scheduled task outputs
   156→    """
   157→    lines = [
   158→        "## Current Session Context",
   159→        "",
   160→    ]
   161→    
   162→    # Source info
   163→    platform_name = context.source.platform.value.title()
   164→    if context.source.platform == Platform.LOCAL:
   165→        lines.append(f"**Source:** {platform_name} (the machine running this agent)")
   166→    else:
   167→        lines.append(f"**Source:** {platform_name} ({context.source.description})")
   168→    
   169→    # Channel topic (if available - provides context about the channel's purpose)
   170→    if context.source.chat_topic:
   171→        lines.append(f"**Channel Topic:** {context.source.chat_topic}")
   172→
   173→    # User identity (especially useful for WhatsApp where multiple people DM)
   174→    if context.source.user_name:
   175→        lines.append(f"**User:** {context.source.user_name}")
   176→    elif context.source.user_id:
   177→        lines.append(f"**User ID:** {context.source.user_id}")
   178→    
   179→    # Connected platforms
   180→    platforms_list = ["local (files on this machine)"]
   181→    for p in context.connected_platforms:
   182→        if p != Platform.LOCAL:
   183→            platforms_list.append(f"{p.value}: Connected ✓")
   184→    
   185→    lines.append(f"**Connected Platforms:** {', '.join(platforms_list)}")
   186→    
   187→    # Home channels
   188→    if context.home_channels:
   189→        lines.append("")
   190→        lines.append("**Home Channels (default destinations):**")
   191→        for platform, home in context.home_channels.items():
   192→            lines.append(f"  - {platform.value}: {home.name} (ID: {home.chat_id})")
   193→    
   194→    # Delivery options for scheduled tasks
   195→    lines.append("")
   196→    lines.append("**Delivery options for scheduled tasks:**")
   197→    
   198→    # Origin delivery
   199→    if context.source.platform == Platform.LOCAL:
   200→        lines.append("- `\"origin\"` → Local output (saved to files)")
   201→    else:
   202→        lines.append(f"- `\"origin\"` → Back to this chat ({context.source.chat_name or context.source.chat_id})")
   203→    
   204→    # Local always available
   205→    lines.append("- `\"local\"` → Save to local files only (~/.hermes/cron/output/)")
   206→    
   207→    # Platform home channels
   208→    for platform, home in context.home_channels.items():
   209→        lines.append(f"- `\"{platform.value}\"` → Home channel ({home.name})")
   210→    
   211→    # Note about explicit targeting
   212→    lines.append("")
   213→    lines.append("*For explicit targeting, use `\"platform:chat_id\"` format if the user provides a specific chat ID.*")
   214→    
   215→    return "\n".join(lines)
   216→
   217→
   218→@dataclass
   219→class SessionEntry:
   220→    """
   221→    Entry in the session store.
   222→    
   223→    Maps a session key to its current session ID and metadata.
   224→    """
   225→    session_key: str
   226→    session_id: str
   227→    created_at: datetime
   228→    updated_at: datetime
   229→    
   230→    # Origin metadata for delivery routing
   231→    origin: Optional[SessionSource] = None
   232→    
   233→    # Display metadata
   234→    display_name: Optional[str] = None
   235→    platform: Optional[Platform] = None
   236→    chat_type: str = "dm"
   237→    
   238→    # Token tracking
   239→    input_tokens: int = 0
   240→    output_tokens: int = 0
   241→    total_tokens: int = 0
   242→    
   243→    # Last API-reported prompt tokens (for accurate compression pre-check)
   244→    last_prompt_tokens: int = 0
   245→    
   246→    # Set when a session was created because the previous one expired;
   247→    # consumed once by the message handler to inject a notice into context
   248→    was_auto_reset: bool = False
   249→    
   250→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   251→        result = {
   252→            "[REDACTED],
   253→            "session_id": self.session_id,
   254→            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
   255→            "updated_at": self.updated_at.isoformat(),
   256→            "display_name": self.display_name,
   257→            "platform": self.platform.value if self.platform else None,
   258→            "chat_type": self.chat_type,
   259→            "input_tokens": self.input_tokens,
   260→            "output_tokens": self.output_tokens,
   261→            "total_tokens": self.total_tokens,
   262→            "last_prompt_tokens": self.last_prompt_tokens,
   263→        }
   264→        if self.origin:
   265→            result["origin"] = self.origin.to_dict()
   266→        return result
   267→    
   268→    @classmethod
   269→    def from_dict(cls, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> "SessionEntry":
   270→        origin = None
   271→        if "origin" in data and data["origin"]:
   272→            origin = SessionSource.from_dict(data["origin"])
   273→        
   274→        platform = None
   275→        if data.get("platform"):
   276→            try:
   277→                platform = Platform(data["platform"])
   278→            except ValueError as e:
   279→                logger.debug("Unknown platform value %r: %s", data["platform"], e)
   280→        
   281→        return cls(
   282→            session_key=data["session_key"],
   283→            session_id=data["session_id"],
   284→            created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(data["created_at"]),
   285→            updated_at=datetime.fromisoformat(data["updated_at"]),
   286→            origin=origin,
   287→            display_name=data.get("display_name"),
   288→            platform=platform,
   289→            chat_type=data.get("chat_type", "dm"),
   290→            input_tokens=data.get("input_tokens", 0),
   291→            output_tokens=data.get("output_tokens", 0),
   292→            total_tokens=data.get("total_tokens", 0),
   293→            last_prompt_tokens=data.get("last_prompt_tokens", 0),
   294→        )
   295→
   296→
   297→def build_session_key(source: SessionSource) -> str:
   298→    """Build a deterministic session key from a message source.
   299→
   300→    This is the single source of truth for session key construction.
   301→
   302→    DM rules:
   303→      - WhatsApp DMs include chat_id (multi-user support).
   304→      - Other DMs include thread_id when present (e.g. Slack threaded DMs),
   305→        so each DM thread gets its own session while top-level DMs share one.
   306→      - Without thread_id or chat_id, all DMs share a single session.
   307→
   308→    Group/channel rules:
   309→      - thread_id differentiates threads within a channel.
   310→      - Without thread_id, all messages in a channel share one session.
   311→    """
   312→    platform = source.platform.value
   313→    if source.chat_type == "dm":
   314→        if source.thread_id:
   315→            return f"agent:main:{platform}:dm:{source.thread_id}"
   316→        if platform == "whatsapp" and source.chat_id:
   317→            return f"agent:main:{platform}:dm:{source.chat_id}"
   318→        return f"agent:main:{platform}:dm"
   319→    if source.thread_id:
   320→        return f"agent:main:{platform}:{source.chat_type}:{source.chat_id}:{source.thread_id}"
   321→    return f"agent:main:{platform}:{source.chat_type}:{source.chat_id}"
   322→
   323→
   324→class SessionStore:
   325→    """
   326→    Manages session storage and retrieval.
   327→    
   328→    Uses SQLite (via SessionDB) for session metadata and message transcripts.
   329→    Falls back to legacy JSONL files if SQLite is unavailable.
   330→    """
   331→    
   332→    def __init__(self, sessions_dir: Path, config: GatewayConfig,
   333→                 has_active_processes_fn=None,
   334→                 on_auto_reset=None):
   335→        self.sessions_dir = sessions_dir
   336→        self.config = config
   337→        self._entries: Dict[str, SessionEntry] = {}
   338→        self._loaded = False
   339→        self._has_active_processes_fn = has_active_processes_fn
   340→        # on_auto_reset is deprecated — memory flush now runs proactively
   341→        # via the background session expiry watcher in GatewayRunner.
   342→        self._pre_flushed_sessions: set = set()  # session_ids already flushed by watcher
   343→        
   344→        # Initialize SQLite session database
   345→        self._db = None
   346→        try:
   347→            from hermes_state import SessionDB
   348→            self._db = SessionDB()
   349→        except Exception as e:
   350→            print(f"[gateway] Warning: SQLite session store unavailable, falling back to JSONL: {e}")
   351→    
   352→    def _ensure_loaded(self) -> None:
   353→        """Load sessions index from disk if not already loaded."""
   354→        if self._loaded:
   355→            return
   356→        
   357→        self.sessions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   358→        sessions_file = self.sessions_dir / "sessions.json"
   359→        
   360→        if sessions_file.exists():
   361→            try:
   362→                with open(sessions_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   363→                    data = json.load(f)
   364→                    for key, entry_data in data.items():
   365→                        self._entries[key] = SessionEntry.from_dict(entry_data)
   366→            except Exception as e:
   367→                print(f"[gateway] Warning: Failed to load sessions: {e}")
   368→        
   369→        self._loaded = True
   370→    
   371→    def _save(self) -> None:
   372→        """Save sessions index to disk (kept for session key -> ID mapping)."""
   373→        import tempfile
   374→        self.sessions_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   375→        sessions_file = self.sessions_dir / "sessions.json"
   376→
   377→        data = {key: entry.to_dict() for key, entry in self._entries.items()}
   378→        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
   379→            dir=str(self.sessions_dir), suffix=".tmp", prefix=".sessions_"
   380→        )
   381→        try:
   382→            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   383→                json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
   384→                f.flush()
   385→                os.fsync(f.fileno())
   386→            os.replace(tmp_path, sessions_file)
   387→        except BaseException:
   388→            try:
   389→                os.unlink(tmp_path)
   390→            except OSError as e:
   391→                logger.debug("Could not remove temp file %s: %s", tmp_path, e)
   392→            raise
   393→    
   394→    def _generate_session_key(self, source: SessionSource) -> str:
   395→        """Generate a session key from a source."""
   396→        return build_session_key(source)
   397→    
   398→    def _is_session_expired(self, entry: SessionEntry) -> bool:
   399→        """Check if a session has expired based on its reset policy.
   400→        
   401→        Works from the entry alone — no SessionSource needed.
   402→        Used by the background expiry watcher to proactively flush memories.
   403→        Sessions with active background processes are never considered expired.
   404→        """
   405→        if self._has_active_processes_fn:
   406→            if self._has_active_processes_fn(entry.session_key):
   407→                return False
   408→
   409→        policy = self.config.get_reset_policy(
   410→            platform=entry.platform,
   411→            session_type=entry.chat_type,
   412→        )
   413→
   414→        if policy.mode == "none":
   415→            return False
   416→
   417→        now = datetime.now()
   418→
   419→        if policy.mode in ("idle", "both"):
   420→            idle_deadline = entry.updated_at + timedelta(minutes=policy.idle_minutes)
   421→            if now > idle_deadline:
   422→                return True
   423→
   424→        if policy.mode in ("daily", "both"):
   425→            today_reset = now.replace(
   426→                hour=policy.at_hour,
   427→                minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0,
   428→            )
   429→            if now.hour < policy.at_hour:
   430→                today_reset -= timedelta(days=1)
   431→            if entry.updated_at < today_reset:
   432→                return True
   433→
   434→        return False
   435→
   436→    def _should_reset(self, entry: SessionEntry, source: SessionSource) -> bool:
   437→        """
   438→        Check if a session should be reset based on policy.
   439→        
   440→        Sessions with active background processes are never reset.
   441→        """
   442→        if self._has_active_processes_fn:
   443→            [REDACTED](source)
   444→            if self._has_active_processes_fn(session_key):
   445→                return False
   446→
   447→        policy = self.config.get_reset_policy(
   448→            platform=source.platform,
   449→            session_type=source.chat_type
   450→        )
   451→        
   452→        if policy.mode == "none":
   453→            return False
   454→        
   455→        now = datetime.now()
   456→        
   457→        if policy.mode in ("idle", "both"):
   458→            idle_deadline = entry.updated_at + timedelta(minutes=policy.idle_minutes)
   459→            if now > idle_deadline:
   460→                return True
   461→        
   462→        if policy.mode in ("daily", "both"):
   463→            today_reset = now.replace(
   464→                hour=policy.at_hour, 
   465→                minute=0, 
   466→                second=0, 
   467→                microsecond=0
   468→            )
   469→            if now.hour < policy.at_hour:
   470→                today_reset -= timedelta(days=1)
   471→            
   472→            if entry.updated_at < today_reset:
   473→                return True
   474→        
   475→        return False
   476→    
   477→    def has_any_sessions(self) -> bool:
   478→        """Check if any sessions have ever been created (across all platforms).
   479→
   480→        Uses the SQLite database as the source of truth because it preserves
   481→        historical session records (ended sessions still count).  The in-memory
   482→        ``_entries`` dict replaces entries on reset, so ``len(_entries)`` would
   483→        stay at 1 for single-platform users — which is the bug this fixes.
   484→
   485→        The current session is already in the DB by the time this is called
   486→        (get_or_create_session runs first), so we check ``> 1``.
   487→        """
   488→        if self._db:
   489→            try:
   490→                return self._db.session_count() > 1
   491→            except Exception:
   492→                pass  # fall through to heuristic
   493→        # Fallback: check if sessions.json was loaded with existing data.
   494→        # This covers the rare case where the DB is unavailable.
   495→        self._ensure_loaded()
   496→        return len(self._entries) > 1
   497→    
   498→    def get_or_create_session(
   499→        self, 
   500→        source: SessionSource,
   501→        force_new: bool = False
   502→    ) -> SessionEntry:
   503→        """
   504→        Get an existing session or create a new one.
   505→        
   506→        Evaluates reset policy to determine if the existing session is stale.
   507→        Creates a session record in SQLite when a new session starts.
   508→        """
   509→        self._ensure_loaded()
   510→        
   511→        [REDACTED](source)
   512→        now = datetime.now()
   513→        
   514→        if session_key in self._entries and not force_new:
   515→            entry = self._entries[session_key]
   516→            
   517→            if not self._should_reset(entry, source):
   518→                entry.updated_at = now
   519→                self._save()
   520→                return entry
   521→            else:
   522→                # Session is being auto-reset.  The background expiry watcher
   523→                # should have already flushed memories proactively; discard
   524→                # the marker so it doesn't accumulate.
   525→                was_auto_reset = True
   526→                self._pre_flushed_sessions.discard(entry.session_id)
   527→                if self._db:
   528→                    try:
   529→                        self._db.end_session(entry.session_id, "session_reset")
   530→                    except Exception as e:
   531→                        logger.debug("Session DB operation failed: %s", e)
   532→        else:
   533→            was_auto_reset = False
   534→        
   535→        # Create new session
   536→        session_id = f"{now.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
   537→        
   538→        entry = SessionEntry(
   539→            session_key=session_key,
   540→            session_id=session_id,
   541→            created_at=now,
   542→            updated_at=now,
   543→            origin=source,
   544→            display_name=source.chat_name,
   545→            platform=source.platform,
   546→            chat_type=source.chat_type,
   547→            was_auto_reset=was_auto_reset,
   548→        )
   549→        
   550→        self._entries[session_key] = entry
   551→        self._save()
   552→        
   553→        # Create session in SQLite
   554→        if self._db:
   555→            try:
   556→                self._db.create_session(
   557→                    session_id=session_id,
   558→                    source=source.platform.value,
   559→                    user_id=source.user_id,
   560→                )
   561→            except Exception as e:
   562→                print(f"[gateway] Warning: Failed to create SQLite session: {e}")
   563→        
   564→        return entry
   565→    
   566→    def update_session(
   567→        self, 
   568→        session_key: str,
   569→        input_tokens: int = 0,
   570→        output_tokens: int = 0,
   571→        last_prompt_tokens: int = None,
   572→    ) -> None:
   573→        """Update a session's metadata after an interaction."""
   574→        self._ensure_loaded()
   575→        
   576→        if session_key in self._entries:
   577→            entry = self._entries[session_key]
   578→            entry.updated_at = datetime.now()
   579→            entry.input_tokens += input_tokens
   580→            entry.output_tokens += output_tokens
   581→            if last_prompt_tokens is not None:
   582→                entry.last_prompt_tokens = last_prompt_tokens
   583→            entry.total_tokens = entry.input_tokens + entry.output_tokens
   584→            self._save()
   585→            
   586→            if self._db:
   587→                try:
   588→                    self._db.update_token_counts(
   589→                        entry.session_id, input_tokens, output_tokens
   590→                    )
   591→                except Exception as e:
   592→                    logger.debug("Session DB operation failed: %s", e)
   593→    
   594→    def reset_session(self, session_key: str) -> Optional[SessionEntry]:
   595→        """Force reset a session, creating a new session ID."""
   596→        self._ensure_loaded()
   597→        
   598→        if session_key not in self._entries:
   599→            return None
   600→        
   601→        old_entry = self._entries[session_key]
   602→        
   603→        # End old session in SQLite
   604→        if self._db:
   605→            try:
   606→                self._db.end_session(old_entry.session_id, "session_reset")
   607→            except Exception as e:
   608→                logger.debug("Session DB operation failed: %s", e)
   609→        
   610→        now = datetime.now()
   611→        session_id = f"{now.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
   612→        
   613→        new_entry = SessionEntry(
   614→            session_key=session_key,
   615→            session_id=session_id,
   616→            created_at=now,
   617→            updated_at=now,
   618→            origin=old_entry.origin,
   619→            display_name=old_entry.display_name,
   620→            platform=old_entry.platform,
   621→            chat_type=old_entry.chat_type,
   622→        )
   623→        
   624→        self._entries[session_key] = new_entry
   625→        self._save()
   626→        
   627→        # Create new session in SQLite
   628→        if self._db:
   629→            try:
   630→                self._db.create_session(
   631→                    session_id=session_id,
   632→                    source=old_entry.platform.value if old_entry.platform else "unknown",
   633→                    user_id=old_entry.origin.user_id if old_entry.origin else None,
   634→                )
   635→            except Exception as e:
   636→                logger.debug("Session DB operation failed: %s", e)
   637→        
   638→        return new_entry
   639→
   640→    def switch_session(self, session_key: str, target_session_id: str) -> Optional[SessionEntry]:
   641→        """Switch a session key to point at an existing session ID.
   642→
   643→        Used by ``/resume`` to restore a previously-named session.
   644→        Ends the current session in SQLite (like reset), but instead of
   645→        generating a fresh session ID, re-uses ``target_session_id`` so the
   646→        old transcript is loaded on the next message.
   647→        """
   648→        self._ensure_loaded()
   649→
   650→        if session_key not in self._entries:
   651→            return None
   652→
   653→        old_entry = self._entries[session_key]
   654→
   655→        # Don't switch if already on that session
   656→        if old_entry.session_id == target_session_id:
   657→            return old_entry
   658→
   659→        # End the current session in SQLite
   660→        if self._db:
   661→            try:
   662→                self._db.end_session(old_entry.session_id, "session_switch")
   663→            except Exception as e:
   664→                logger.debug("Session DB end_session failed: %s", e)
   665→
   666→        now = datetime.now()
   667→        new_entry = SessionEntry(
   668→            session_key=session_key,
   669→            session_id=target_session_id,
   670→            created_at=now,
   671→            updated_at=now,
   672→            origin=old_entry.origin,
   673→            display_name=old_entry.display_name,
   674→            platform=old_entry.platform,
   675→            chat_type=old_entry.chat_type,
   676→        )
   677→
   678→        self._entries[session_key] = new_entry
   679→        self._save()
   680→        return new_entry
   681→
   682→    def list_sessions(self, active_minutes: Optional[int] = None) -> List[SessionEntry]:
   683→        """List all sessions, optionally filtered by activity."""
   684→        self._ensure_loaded()
   685→        
   686→        entries = list(self._entries.values())
   687→        
   688→        if active_minutes is not None:
   689→            cutoff = datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=active_minutes)
   690→            entries = [e for e in entries if e.updated_at >= cutoff]
   691→        
   692→        entries.sort(key=lambda e: e.updated_at, reverse=True)
   693→        
   694→        return entries
   695→    
   696→    def get_transcript_path(self, session_id: str) -> Path:
   697→        """Get the path to a session's legacy transcript file."""
   698→        return self.sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.jsonl"
   699→    
   700→    def append_to_transcript(self, session_id: str, message: Dict[str, Any], skip_db: bool = False) -> None:
   701→        """Append a message to a session's transcript (SQLite + legacy JSONL).
   702→
   703→        Args:
   704→            skip_db: When True, only write to JSONL and skip the SQLite write.
   705→                     Used when the agent already persisted messages to SQLite
   706→                     via its own _flush_messages_to_session_db(), preventing
   707→                     the duplicate-write bug (#860).
   708→        """
   709→        # Write to SQLite (unless the agent already handled it)
   710→        if self._db and not skip_db:
   711→            try:
   712→                self._db.append_message(
   713→                    session_id=session_id,
   714→                    role=message.get("role", "unknown"),
   715→                    content=message.get("content"),
   716→                    tool_name=message.get("tool_name"),
   717→                    tool_calls=message.get("tool_calls"),
   718→                    tool_call_id=message.get("tool_call_id"),
   719→                )
   720→            except Exception as e:
   721→                logger.debug("Session DB operation failed: %s", e)
   722→        
   723→        # Also write legacy JSONL (keeps existing tooling working during transition)
   724→        transcript_path = self.get_transcript_path(session_id)
   725→        with open(transcript_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   726→            f.write(json.dumps(message, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   727→    
   728→    def rewrite_transcript(self, session_id: str, messages: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
   729→        """Replace the entire transcript for a session with new messages.
   730→        
   731→        Used by /retry, /undo, and /compress to persist modified conversation history.
   732→        Rewrites both SQLite and legacy JSONL storage.
   733→        """
   734→        # SQLite: clear old messages and re-insert
   735→        if self._db:
   736→            try:
   737→                self._db.clear_messages(session_id)
   738→                for msg in messages:
   739→                    self._db.append_message(
   740→                        session_id=session_id,
   741→                        role=msg.get("role", "unknown"),
   742→                        content=msg.get("content"),
   743→                        tool_name=msg.get("tool_name"),
   744→                        tool_calls=msg.get("tool_calls"),
   745→                        tool_call_id=msg.get("tool_call_id"),
   746→                    )
   747→            except Exception as e:
   748→                logger.debug("Failed to rewrite transcript in DB: %s", e)
   749→        
   750→        # JSONL: overwrite the file
   751→        transcript_path = self.get_transcript_path(session_id)
   752→        with open(transcript_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   753→            for msg in messages:
   754→                f.write(json.dumps(msg, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   755→
   756→    def load_transcript(self, session_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   757→        """Load all messages from a session's transcript."""
   758→        # Try SQLite first
   759→        if self._db:
   760→            try:
   761→                messages = self._db.get_messages_as_conversation(session_id)
   762→                if messages:
   763→                    return messages
   764→            except Exception as e:
   765→                logger.debug("Could not load messages from DB: %s", e)
   766→        
   767→        # Fall back to legacy JSONL
   768→        transcript_path = self.get_transcript_path(session_id)
   769→        
   770→        if not transcript_path.exists():
   771→            return []
   772→        
   773→        messages = []
   774→        with open(transcript_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   775→            for line in f:
   776→                line = line.strip()
   777→                if line:
   778→                    messages.append(json.loads(line))
   779→        
   780→        return messages
   781→
   782→
   783→def build_session_context(
   784→    source: SessionSource,
   785→    config: GatewayConfig,
   786→    session_entry: Optional[SessionEntry] = None
   787→) -> SessionContext:
   788→    """
   789→    Build a full session context from a source and config.
   790→    
   791→    This is used to inject context into the agent's system prompt.
   792→    """
   793→    connected = config.get_connected_platforms()
   794→    
   795→    home_channels = {}
   796→    for platform in connected:
   797→        home = config.get_home_channel(platform)
   798→        if home:
   799→            home_channels[platform] = home
   800→    
   801→    context = SessionContext(
   802→        source=source,
   803→        connected_platforms=connected,
   804→        home_channels=home_channels,
   805→    )
   806→    
   807→    if session_entry:
   808→        context.[REDACTED]
   809→        context.session_id = session_entry.session_id
   810→        context.created_at = session_entry.created_at
   811→        context.updated_at = session_entry.updated_at
   812→    
   813→    return context
   814→

     2→Delivery routing for cron job outputs and agent responses.

    26→@dataclass
    27→class DeliveryTarget:
    28→    """
    29→    A single delivery target.
    30→    
    31→    Represents where a message should be sent:
    32→    - "origin" → back to source
    33→    - "local" → save to local files

    35→    - "telegram:123456" → specific Telegram chat

    39→    thread_id: Optional[str] = None
    40→    is_origin: bool = False
    41→    is_explicit: bool = False  # True if chat_id was explicitly specified
    42→    
    43→    @classmethod
    44→    def parse(cls, target: str, origin: Optional[SessionSource] = None) -> "DeliveryTarget":
    45→        """
    46→        Parse a delivery target string.
    47→        
    48→        Formats:
    49→        - "origin" → back to source
    50→        - "local" → local files only
    51→        - "telegram" → Telegram home channel
    52→        - "telegram:123456" → specific Telegram chat
    53→        """
    54→        target = target.strip().lower()
    55→        
    56→        if target == "origin":
    57→            if origin:
    58→                return cls(
    59→                    platform=origin.platform,
    60→                    chat_id=origin.chat_id,
    61→                    thread_id=origin.thread_id,
    62→                    is_origin=True,
    63→                )
    64→            else:
    65→                # Fallback to local if no origin
    66→                return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL, is_origin=True)
    67→        
    68→        if target == "local":
    69→            return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)
    70→        
    71→        # Check for platform:chat_id format
    72→        if ":" in target:
    73→            platform_str, chat_id = target.split(":", 1)
    74→            try:
    75→                platform = Platform(platform_str)
    76→                return cls(platform=platform, chat_id=chat_id, is_explicit=True)
    77→            except ValueError:
    78→                # Unknown platform, treat as local
    79→                return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)
    80→        
    81→        # Just a platform name (use home channel)
    82→        try:
    83→            platform = Platform(target)
    84→            return cls(platform=platform)
    85→        except ValueError:
    86→            # Unknown platform, treat as local
    87→            return cls(platform=Platform.LOCAL)

    97→        return self.platform.value

   100→class DeliveryRouter:
   101→    """
   102→    Routes messages to appropriate destinations.
   103→    
   104→    Handles the logic of resolving delivery targets and dispatching
   105→    messages to the right platform adapters.
   106→    """
   107→    
   108→    def __init__(self, config: GatewayConfig, adapters: Dict[Platform, Any] = None):
   109→        """
   110→        Initialize the delivery router.
   111→        
   112→        Args:
   113→            config: Gateway configuration
   114→            adapters: Dict mapping platforms to their adapter instances
   115→        """
   116→        self.config = config
   117→        self.adapters = adapters or {}
   118→        self.output_dir = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "cron" / "output"
   119→    
   120→    def resolve_targets(
   121→        self,
   122→        deliver: Union[str, List[str]],
   123→        origin: Optional[SessionSource] = None
   124→    ) -> List[DeliveryTarget]:
   125→        """
   126→        Resolve delivery specification to concrete targets.
   127→        
   128→        Args:
   129→            deliver: Delivery spec - "origin", "telegram", ["local", "discord"], etc.
   130→            origin: The source where the request originated (for "origin" target)
   131→        
   132→        Returns:
   133→            List of resolved delivery targets
   134→        """
   135→        if isinstance(deliver, str):
   136→            deliver = [deliver]
   137→        
   138→        targets = []
   139→        seen_platforms = set()
   140→        
   141→        for target_str in deliver:
   142→            target = DeliveryTarget.parse(target_str, origin)
   143→            
   144→            # Resolve home channel if needed
   145→            if target.chat_id is None and target.platform != Platform.LOCAL:
   146→                home = self.config.get_home_channel(target.platform)
   147→                if home:
   148→                    target.chat_id = home.chat_id
   149→                else:
   150→                    # No home channel configured, skip this platform
   151→                    continue
   152→            
   153→            # Deduplicate
   154→            key = (target.platform, target.chat_id, target.thread_id)
   155→            if key not in seen_platforms:
   156→                seen_platforms.add(key)
   157→                targets.append(target)
   158→        
   159→        # Always include local if configured
   160→        if self.config.always_log_local:
   161→            local_key = (Platform.LOCAL, None)
   162→            if local_key not in seen_platforms:
   163→                targets.append(DeliveryTarget(platform=Platform.LOCAL))
   164→        
   165→        return targets
   166→    
   167→    async def deliver(
   168→        self,
   169→        content: str,
   170→        targets: List[DeliveryTarget],
   171→        job_id: Optional[str] = None,
   172→        job_name: Optional[str] = None,
   173→        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
   174→    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   175→        """
   176→        Deliver content to all specified targets.
   177→        
   178→        Args:
   179→            content: The message/output to deliver
   180→            targets: List of delivery targets
   181→            job_id: Optional job ID (for cron jobs)
   182→            job_name: Optional job name
   183→            metadata: Additional metadata to include
   184→        
   185→        Returns:
   186→            Dict with delivery results per target
   187→        """
   188→        results = {}
   189→        
   190→        for target in targets:
   191→            try:
   192→                if target.platform == Platform.LOCAL:
   193→                    result = self._deliver_local(content, job_id, job_name, metadata)
   194→                else:
   195→                    result = await self._deliver_to_platform(target, content, metadata)
   196→                
   197→                results[target.to_string()] = {
   198→                    "success": True,
   199→                    "result": result
   200→                }
   201→            except Exception as e:
   202→                results[target.to_string()] = {
   203→                    "success": False,
   204→                    "error": str(e)
   205→                }
   206→        
   207→        return results
   208→    
   209→    def _deliver_local(
   210→        self,
   211→        content: str,
   212→        job_id: Optional[str],
   213→        job_name: Optional[str],
   214→        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
   215→    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   216→        """Save content to local files."""
   217→        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
   218→        
   219→        if job_id:
   220→            output_path = self.output_dir / job_id / f"{timestamp}.md"
   221→        else:
   222→            output_path = self.output_dir / "misc" / f"{timestamp}.md"
   223→        
   224→        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   225→        
   226→        # Build the output document
   227→        lines = []
   228→        if job_name:
   229→            lines.append(f"# {job_name}")
   230→        else:
   231→            lines.append("# Delivery Output")
   232→        
   233→        lines.append("")
   234→        lines.append(f"**Timestamp:** {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
   235→        
   236→        if job_id:
   237→            lines.append(f"**Job ID:** {job_id}")
   238→        
   239→        if metadata:
   240→            for key, value in metadata.items():
   241→                lines.append(f"**{key}:** {value}")
   242→        
   243→        lines.append("")
   244→        lines.append("---")
   245→        lines.append("")
   246→        lines.append(content)
   247→        
   248→        output_path.write_text("\n".join(lines))
   249→        
   250→        return {
   251→            "path": str(output_path),
   252→            "timestamp": timestamp
   253→        }
   254→    
   255→    def _save_full_output(self, content: str, job_id: str) -> Path:
   256→        """Save full cron output to disk and return the file path."""
   257→        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
   258→        out_dir = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "cron" / "output"
   259→        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   260→        path = out_dir / f"{job_id}_{timestamp}.txt"
   261→        path.write_text(content)
   262→        return path
   263→
   264→    async def _deliver_to_platform(
   265→        self,
   266→        target: DeliveryTarget,
   267→        content: str,
   268→        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
   269→    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   270→        """Deliver content to a messaging platform."""
   271→        adapter = self.adapters.get(target.platform)
   272→        
   273→        if not adapter:
   274→            raise ValueError(f"No adapter configured for {target.platform.value}")
   275→        
   276→        if not target.chat_id:
   277→            raise ValueError(f"No chat ID for {target.platform.value} delivery")
   278→        
   279→        # Guard: truncate oversized cron output to stay within platform limits
   280→        if len(content) > MAX_PLATFORM_OUTPUT:
   281→            job_id = (metadata or {}).get("job_id", "unknown")
   282→            saved_path = self._save_full_output(content, job_id)
   283→            logger.info("Cron output truncated (%d chars) — full output: %s", len(content), saved_path)
   284→            content = (
   285→                content[:TRUNCATED_VISIBLE]
   286→                + f"\n\n... [truncated, full output saved to {saved_path}]"
   287→            )
   288→        
   289→        send_metadata = dict(metadata or {})
   290→        if target.thread_id and "thread_id" not in send_metadata:
   291→            send_metadata["thread_id"] = target.thread_id
   292→        return await adapter.send(target.chat_id, content, metadata=send_metadata or None)
   293→

   296→    deliver: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]],

   300→    """
   301→    Normalize a delivery specification.
   302→    
   303→    If None or empty, returns the default.
   304→    """
   305→    if not deliver:
   306→        return default
   307→    return deliver

1→"""
     2→Channel directory -- cached map of reachable channels/contacts per platform.
     3→
     4→Built on gateway startup, refreshed periodically (every 5 min), and saved to
     5→~/.hermes/channel_directory.json.  The send_message tool reads this file for
     6→action="list" and for resolving human-friendly channel names to numeric IDs.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import json
    10→import logging
    11→from datetime import datetime
    12→from pathlib import Path
    13→from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→DIRECTORY_PATH = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "channel_directory.json"
    18→
    19→
    20→def _session_entry_id(origin: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    21→    chat_id = origin.get("chat_id")
    22→    if not chat_id:
    23→        return None
    24→    thread_id = origin.get("thread_id")
    25→    if thread_id:
    26→        return f"{chat_id}:{thread_id}"
    27→    return str(chat_id)
    28→
    29→
    30→def _session_entry_name(origin: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    31→    base_name = origin.get("chat_name") or origin.get("user_name") or str(origin.get("chat_id"))
    32→    thread_id = origin.get("thread_id")
    33→    if not thread_id:
    34→        return base_name
    35→
    36→    topic_label = origin.get("chat_topic") or f"topic {thread_id}"
    37→    return f"{base_name} / {topic_label}"
    38→
    39→
    40→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    41→# Build / refresh
    42→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    43→
    44→def build_channel_directory(adapters: Dict[Any, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    45→    """
    46→    Build a channel directory from connected platform adapters and session data.
    47→
    48→    Returns the directory dict and writes it to DIRECTORY_PATH.
    49→    """
    50→    from gateway.config import Platform
    51→
    52→    platforms: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, str]]] = {}
    53→
    54→    for platform, adapter in adapters.items():
    55→        try:
    56→            if platform == Platform.DISCORD:
    57→                platforms["discord"] = _build_discord(adapter)
    58→            elif platform == Platform.SLACK:
    59→                platforms["slack"] = _build_slack(adapter)
    60→        except Exception as e:
    61→            logger.warning("Channel directory: failed to build %s: %s", platform.value, e)
    62→
    63→    # Telegram, WhatsApp & Signal can't enumerate chats -- pull from session history
    64→    for plat_name in ("telegram", "whatsapp", "signal", "email"):
    65→        if plat_name not in platforms:
    66→            platforms[plat_name] = _build_from_sessions(plat_name)
    67→
    68→    directory = {
    69→        "updated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    70→        "platforms": platforms,
    71→    }
    72→
    73→    try:
    74→        DIRECTORY_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    75→        with open(DIRECTORY_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    76→            json.dump(directory, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    77→    except Exception as e:
    78→        logger.warning("Channel directory: failed to write: %s", e)
    79→
    80→    return directory
    81→
    82→
    83→def _build_discord(adapter) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    84→    """Enumerate all text channels the Discord bot can see."""
    85→    channels = []
    86→    client = getattr(adapter, "_client", None)
    87→    if not client:
    88→        return channels
    89→
    90→    try:
    91→        import discord as _discord
    92→    except ImportError:
    93→        return channels
    94→
    95→    for guild in client.guilds:
    96→        for ch in guild.text_channels:
    97→            channels.append({
    98→                "id": str(ch.id),
    99→                "name": ch.name,
   100→                "guild": guild.name,
   101→                "type": "channel",
   102→            })
   103→        # Also include DM-capable users we've interacted with is not
   104→        # feasible via guild enumeration; those come from sessions.
   105→
   106→    # Merge any DMs from session history
   107→    channels.extend(_build_from_sessions("discord"))
   108→    return channels
   109→
   110→
   111→def _build_slack(adapter) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
   112→    """List Slack channels the bot has joined."""
   113→    channels = []
   114→    # Slack adapter may expose a web client
   115→    client = getattr(adapter, "_app", None) or getattr(adapter, "_client", None)
   116→    if not client:
   117→        return _build_from_sessions("slack")
   118→
   119→    try:
   120→        from tools.send_message_tool import _send_slack  # noqa: F401
   121→        # Use the Slack Web API directly if available
   122→    except Exception:
   123→        pass
   124→
   125→    # Fallback to session data
   126→    return _build_from_sessions("slack")
   127→
   128→
   129→def _build_from_sessions(platform_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
   130→    """Pull known channels/contacts from sessions.json origin data."""
   131→    sessions_path = Path.home() / ".hermes" / "sessions" / "sessions.json"
   132→    if not sessions_path.exists():
   133→        return []
   134→
   135→    entries = []
   136→    try:
   137→        with open(sessions_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   138→            data = json.load(f)
   139→
   140→        seen_ids = set()
   141→        for _key, session in data.items():
   142→            origin = session.get("origin") or {}
   143→            if origin.get("platform") != platform_name:
   144→                continue
   145→            entry_id = _session_entry_id(origin)
   146→            if not entry_id or entry_id in seen_ids:
   147→                continue
   148→            seen_ids.add(entry_id)
   149→            entries.append({
   150→                "id": entry_id,
   151→                "name": _session_entry_name(origin),
   152→                "type": session.get("chat_type", "dm"),
   153→                "thread_id": origin.get("thread_id"),
   154→            })
   155→    except Exception as e:
   156→        logger.debug("Channel directory: failed to read sessions for %s: %s", platform_name, e)
   157→
   158→    return entries
   159→
   160→
   161→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   162→# Read / resolve
   163→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   164→
   165→def load_directory() -> Dict[str, Any]:
   166→    """Load the cached channel directory from disk."""
   167→    if not DIRECTORY_PATH.exists():
   168→        return {"updated_at": None, "platforms": {}}
   169→    try:
   170→        with open(DIRECTORY_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   171→            return json.load(f)
   172→    except Exception:
   173→        return {"updated_at": None, "platforms": {}}
   174→
   175→
   176→def resolve_channel_name(platform_name: str, name: str) -> Optional[str]:
   177→    """
   178→    Resolve a human-friendly channel name to a numeric ID.
   179→
   180→    Matching strategy (case-insensitive, first match wins):
   181→    - Discord: "bot-home", "#bot-home", "GuildName/bot-home"
   182→    - Telegram: display name or group name
   183→    - Slack: "engineering", "#engineering"
   184→    """
   185→    directory = load_directory()
   186→    channels = directory.get("platforms", {}).get(platform_name, [])
   187→    if not channels:
   188→        return None
   189→
   190→    query = name.lstrip("#").lower()
   191→
   192→    # 1. Exact name match
   193→    for ch in channels:
   194→        if ch["name"].lower() == query:
   195→            return ch["id"]
   196→
   197→    # 2. Guild-qualified match for Discord ("GuildName/channel")
   198→    if "/" in query:
   199→        guild_part, ch_part = query.rsplit("/", 1)
   200→        for ch in channels:
   201→            guild = ch.get("guild", "").lower()
   202→            if guild == guild_part and ch["name"].lower() == ch_part:
   203→                return ch["id"]
   204→
   205→    # 3. Partial prefix match (only if unambiguous)
   206→    matches = [ch for ch in channels if ch["name"].lower().startswith(query)]
   207→    if len(matches) == 1:
   208→        return matches[0]["id"]
   209→
   210→    return None
   211→
   212→
   213→def format_directory_for_display() -> str:
   214→    """Format the channel directory as a human-readable list for the model."""
   215→    directory = load_directory()
   216→    platforms = directory.get("platforms", {})
   217→
   218→    if not any(platforms.values()):
   219→        return "No messaging platforms connected or no channels discovered yet."
   220→
   221→    lines = ["Available messaging targets:\n"]
   222→
   223→    for plat_name, channels in sorted(platforms.items()):
   224→        if not channels:
   225→            continue
   226→
   227→        # Group Discord channels by guild
   228→        if plat_name == "discord":
   229→            guilds: Dict[str, List] = {}
   230→            dms: List = []
   231→            for ch in channels:
   232→                guild = ch.get("guild")
   233→                if guild:
   234→                    guilds.setdefault(guild, []).append(ch)
   235→                else:
   236→                    dms.append(ch)
   237→
   238→            for guild_name, guild_channels in sorted(guilds.items()):
   239→                lines.append(f"Discord ({guild_name}):")
   240→                for ch in sorted(guild_channels, key=lambda c: c["name"]):
   241→                    lines.append(f"  discord:#{ch['name']}")
   242→            if dms:
   243→                lines.append("Discord (DMs):")
   244→                for ch in dms:
   245→                    lines.append(f"  discord:{ch['name']}")
   246→            lines.append("")
   247→        else:
   248→            lines.append(f"{plat_name.title()}:")
   249→            for ch in channels:
   250→                type_label = f" ({ch['type']})" if ch.get("type") else ""
   251→                lines.append(f"  {plat_name}:{ch['name']}{type_label}")
   252→            lines.append("")
   253→
   254→    lines.append('Use these as the "target" parameter when sending.')
   255→    lines.append('Bare platform name (e.g. "telegram") sends to home channel.')
   256→
   257→    return "\n".join(lines)
   258→

    34→# =============================================================================
    35→# Async Bridging  (single source of truth -- used by registry.dispatch too)
    36→# =============================================================================
    37→
    38→def _run_async(coro):
    39→    """Run an async coroutine from a sync context.
    40→
    41→    If the current thread already has a running event loop (e.g., inside
    42→    the gateway's async stack or Atropos's event loop), we spin up a
    43→    disposable thread so asyncio.run() can create its own loop without
    44→    conflicting.
    45→
    46→    This is the single source of truth for sync->async bridging in tool
    47→    handlers. The RL paths (agent_loop.py, tool_context.py) also provide
    48→    outer thread-pool wrapping as defense-in-depth, but each handler is
    49→    self-protecting via this function.
    50→    """
    51→    try:
    52→        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    53→    except RuntimeError:
    54→        loop = None
    55→
    56→    if loop and loop.is_running():
    57→        import concurrent.futures
    58→        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
    59→            future = pool.submit(asyncio.run, coro)
    60→            return future.result(timeout=300)
    61→    return asyncio.run(coro)
    62→
    63→

1→"""Central registry for all hermes-agent tools.
     2→
     3→Each tool file calls ``registry.register()`` at module level to declare its
     4→schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check.  ``model_tools.py``
     5→queries the registry instead of maintaining its own parallel data structures.
     6→
     7→Import chain (circular-import safe):
     8→    tools/registry.py  (no imports from model_tools or tool files)
     9→           ^
    10→    tools/*.py  (import from tools.registry at module level)
    11→           ^
    12→    model_tools.py  (imports tools.registry + all tool modules)
    13→           ^
    14→    run_agent.py, cli.py, batch_runner.py, etc.
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import json
    18→import logging
    19→from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Set
    20→
    21→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    22→
    23→
    24→class ToolEntry:
    25→    """Metadata for a single registered tool."""
    26→
    27→    __slots__ = (
    28→        "name", "toolset", "schema", "handler", "check_fn",
    29→        "requires_env", "is_async", "description",
    30→    )
    31→
    32→    def __init__(self, name, toolset, schema, handler, check_fn,
    33→                 requires_env, is_async, description):
    34→        self.name = name
    35→        self.toolset = toolset
    36→        self.schema = schema
    37→        self.handler = handler
    38→        self.check_fn = check_fn
    39→        self.requires_env = requires_env
    40→        self.is_async = is_async
    41→        self.description = description
    42→
    43→
    44→class ToolRegistry:
    45→    """Singleton registry that collects tool schemas + handlers from tool files."""
    46→
    47→    def __init__(self):
    48→        self._tools: Dict[str, ToolEntry] = {}
    49→        self._toolset_checks: Dict[str, Callable] = {}
    50→

     2→"""
     3→V4A Patch Format Parser
     4→
     5→Parses the V4A patch format used by codex, cline, and other coding agents.
     6→
     7→V4A Format:
     8→    *** Begin Patch
     9→    *** Update File: path/to/file.py
    10→    @@ optional context hint @@
    11→     context line (space prefix)
    12→    -removed line (minus prefix)
    13→    +added line (plus prefix)
    14→    *** Add File: path/to/new.py
    15→    +new file content
    16→    +line 2
    17→    *** Delete File: path/to/old.py
    18→    *** Move File: old/path.py -> new/path.py
    19→    *** End Patch
    20→

    22→    from tools.patch_parser import parse_v4a_patch, apply_v4a_operations
    23→    
    24→    operations, error = parse_v4a_patch(patch_content)
    25→    if error:

    49→
    50→

    53→    """A group of changes within a file."""
    54→    context_hint: Optional[str] = None
    55→    lines: List[HunkLine] = field(default_factory=list)
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class PatchOperation:
    60→    """A single operation in a V4A patch."""
    61→    operation: OperationType
    62→    file_path: str

    67→

    91→            end_idx = i

    54→│   ├── run.py            # Main loop, slash commands, message dispatch
    55→│   ├── session.py        # SessionStore — conversation persistence
    56→│   └── platforms/        # Adapters: telegram, discord, slack, whatsapp, homeassistant, signal
    57→├── acp_adapter/          # ACP server (VS Code / Zed / JetBrains integration)

    59→├── environments/         # RL training environments (Atropos)

    74→       ↑

   536→## REFLECT Stage Instructions
   537→
   538→Your task: using the verdicts from observe, design the cluster structure.
   539→
   540→**A strategy is NOT a restatement of observe.** Observe says "here's what I found." Reflect
   541→says "here's what we should DO about it, and here's what we should NOT do, and here's WHY."
   542→
   543→**The Structured Observe Assessments table (provided below) is your primary input.** It contains
   544→a per-issue verdict (genuine/false-positive/exaggerated/over-engineering/not-worth-it) with reasoning. Use
   545→these verdicts as authoritative — do not second-guess observe unless you have specific evidence.
   546→
   547→**Important: Issues with verdict `false-positive` or `exaggerated` have already been auto-skipped
   548→by observe confirmation.** They are NOT in your issue set and do NOT need ledger entries.
   549→
   550→For issues with verdict `over-engineering` or `not-worth-it`: observe flagged these as
   551→questionable, but YOU decide. If you agree they're not worth fixing, skip them. If you disagree
   552→and think the fix has value, cluster them. These are judgment calls, not factual determinations.
   553→
   554→### What you must do:
   555→
   556→1. **Filter:** which issues are genuine (from the observe assessments table)?
   557→2. **Map:** for each genuine issue, what file/directory does it touch?
   558→3. **Group:** which issues share files or directories? These become clusters.
   559→4. **Skip:** which issues should be skipped? Apply YAGNI: if the fix is more complex than the
   560→   problem, skip it. Valid skip reasons:
   561→   - "the fix would add a 50-line abstraction to save 3 lines of duplication"
   562→   - "the current code is clear and simple despite being theoretically suboptimal"
   563→   - "observe verdict: not-worth-it — the improvement is marginal"
   564→   - "fixing this requires touching 8 files for a naming consistency issue nobody notices"
   565→   Invalid: "low priority" (everything is low priority compared to something)
   566→5. **Order:** which clusters depend on others? What's the execution sequence?
   567→6. **Check recurring patterns** — compare current issues against resolved history. If the same
   568→   dimension keeps producing issues, that's a root cause that needs addressing, not just
   569→   another round of fixes.
   570→7. **Consider mechanical backlog** — the backlog section shows auto-clusters
   571→   (pre-grouped detector findings) and unclustered items. For each auto-cluster:
   572→   - **promote**: name it in a `## Backlog Promotions` section. Prefer clusters with
   573→     `[autofix: ...]` hints because they are lower-risk.
   574→   - **leave**: say nothing. Silence means it stays in backlog.
   575→   - **supersede**: absorb the underlying work into a review cluster when the same files
   576→     or root cause already belong together.
   577→   For unclustered items: promote individually or group related ones into a manual cluster.
   578→   Mechanical items are NOT part of the Coverage Ledger — that ledger remains review-issues only.
   579→8. **Account for every issue exactly once** — every open issue hash must appear in exactly one
   580→   cluster line or one skip line. Do not drop hashes, and do not repeat a hash in multiple
   581→   clusters or in both a cluster and a skip.
   582→
   583→### Your report MUST include both a coverage ledger and a concrete cluster blueprint
   584→
   585→This blueprint is what the organize stage will execute. Be specific:
   586→```
   587→## Coverage Ledger
   588→- a5996373 -> cluster "travel-structure-contract-unification"
   589→- fb113678 -> skip "false-positive-current-code"
   590→
   591→## Cluster Blueprint
   592→Cluster "media-lightbox-hooks" (all in src/domains/media-lightbox/)
   593→Cluster "task-typing" (both touch src/types/database.ts)
   594→
   595→## Backlog Promotions
   596→- Promote auto/unused-imports (overlaps with the files in cluster "task-typing")
   597→
   598→## Skip Decisions
   599→Skip "false-positive-current-code" (false positive per observe)
   600→```
   601→
   602→### Hard accounting rule
   603→
   604→- Start your report with a `## Coverage Ledger` section.
   605→- In that section, mention each issue hash **once and only once** on its own ledger line.
   606→- Do **not** mention issue hashes again in cluster rationale paragraphs, recurring-pattern notes,
   607→  or ordering explanations. After the ledger, refer to clusters by name.
   608→- Before finishing, do a self-check: the ledger must cover all open issue hashes exactly once.
   609→
   610→### What a LAZY reflect looks like (will be rejected):
   611→- Restating observe findings in slightly different words
   612→- "We should prioritize high-impact items and defer low-priority ones"
   613→- A bulleted list of dimensions without any strategic thinking
   614→- Ignoring recurring patterns
   615→- No `## Coverage Ledger`
   616→- No cluster blueprint (just vague grouping ideas)
   617→- Missing or duplicated issue hashes
   618→
   619→### What a GOOD reflect looks like:
   620→- "50% false positive rate. Of 34 issues, 17 are genuine. 10 of those are batch-scriptable
   621→  convention fixes (zero risk, 30 min) — cluster 'convention-batch'. The remaining 7 split into
   622→  3 clusters by file proximity: 'media-lightbox-hooks' (issues X,Y,Z — all in src/domains/media-lightbox/),
   623→  'timeline-cleanup' (issues A,B,C — touching Timeline components), 'task-typing' (issues D,E).
   624→  Skip: issue W (false positive), issue V (over-engineering), issue U (not-worth-it:
   625→  adds ErrorBoundary wrapper around 3 components that already handle errors inline —
   626→  technically cleaner but doubles the JSX nesting depth for no behavioral change).
   627→  design_coherence recurs (2 resolved, 5 open) but only 1 of the 5 actually warrants work."
   628→
   629→When done, run:
   630→```
   631→desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "<your strategy with cluster blueprint>" --attestation "<80+ chars mentioning dimensions or recurring patterns>"
   632→```
   633→
   634→
   635→
   636→## CLI Command Reference
   637→
   638→### Stage recording
   639→```
   640→desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "<analysis>"
   641→desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "<strategy>" --attestation "<80+ chars>"
   642→desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "<summary>" --attestation "<80+ chars>"
   643→desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "<enrichment summary>" --attestation "<80+ chars>"
   644→desloppify plan triage --stage sense-check --report "<verification summary>" --attestation "<80+ chars>"
   645→```
   646→
   647→### Cluster management
   648→```
   649→desloppify plan cluster create <name> --description "<what this cluster addresses>"
   650→desloppify plan cluster add <name> <issue-patterns...>
   651→desloppify plan cluster remove <name> <issue-patterns...>
   652→desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "<desc>" --steps "step 1" "step 2"
   653→desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "<title>" --detail "<sub-points>" --effort small --issue-refs <id1> <id2>
   654→desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "<sub-points>" --effort medium --issue-refs <id1>
   655→desloppify plan cluster update <name> --depends-on <other-cluster-name>
   656→desloppify plan cluster delete <name>
   657→desloppify plan cluster show <name>
   658→desloppify plan cluster list --verbose
   659→desloppify plan promote <pattern>
   660→desloppify plan promote <pattern> top
   661→desloppify plan promote <pattern> before -t <target>
   662→```
   663→
   664→### Skip/dismiss
   665→```
   666→desloppify plan skip --permanent <pattern> --note "<reason>" --attest "I have reviewed this triage skip against the code and I am not gaming the score by suppressing a real defect."
   667→```
   668→**Important:** The --attest value MUST contain the words "reviewed" and "not gaming" (exact phrases required by validation).
   669→Every review issue in the active triage run must end up either in a manual cluster or permanently skipped. Leaving issues unassigned is an invalid triage result.
   670→
   671→### Issue investigation
   672→```
   673→desloppify show <issue-id-or-pattern> --no-budget    # full issue detail with suggestion
   674→desloppify show review --status open --no-budget     # all open review issues
   675→desloppify backlog --count 20                        # inspect backlog-only detector work
   676→```
   677→
   678→### Effort tags
   679→Valid values: trivial, small, medium, large. Set on steps via --effort flag.
   680→
   681→
   682→## Validation Requirements
   683→- Stage must be recorded with a 100+ char report
   684→- Report must mention recurring dimension names (if any exist)
   685→- Report must include a `## Coverage Ledger` section
   686→- Report must account for every open review issue exactly once (no missing or duplicate hashes)
   687→- Stage must be confirmed with an 80+ char attestation
   688→
   689→

   317→    Recursively resolve a toolset to get all tool names.
   318→    
   319→    This function handles toolset composition by recursively resolving

   321→    
   322→    Args:
   323→        name (str): Name of the toolset to resolve

   327→        List[str]: List of all tool names in the toolset
   328→    """

   330→        visited = set()
   331→    
   332→    # Special aliases that represent all tools across every toolset
   333→    # This ensures future toolsets are automatically included without changes.
   334→    if name in {"all", "*"}:

   336→        for toolset_name in get_toolset_names():
   337→            # Use a fresh visited set per branch to avoid cross-branch contamination

   339→            all_tools.update(resolved)
   340→        return list(all_tools)

    23→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    24→class ReviewOptions:
    25→    """All user-facing review command options extracted once from argparse."""
    26→
    27→    merge: bool = False
    28→    run_batches: bool = False
    29→    import_run_dir: str | None = None
    30→    external_start: bool = False
    31→    external_submit: bool = False
    32→    import_file: str | None = None
    33→    validate_import_file: str | None = None

    41→    attest: str | None = None
    42→
    43→    @classmethod
    44→    def from_args(cls, args: argparse.Namespace) -> ReviewOptions:
    45→        return cls(
    46→            merge=bool(getattr(args, "merge", False)),
    47→            run_batches=bool(getattr(args, "run_batches", False)),
    48→            import_run_dir=getattr(args, "import_run_dir", None),
    49→            external_start=bool(getattr(args, "external_start", False)),
    50→            external_submit=bool(getattr(args, "external_submit", False)),

    53→            session_id=getattr(args, "session_id", None),
    54→            allow_partial=bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False)),
    55→            scan_after_import=bool(getattr(args, "scan_after_import", False)),
    56→            path=str(getattr(args, "path", ".") or "."),
    57→            dry_run=bool(getattr(args, "dry_run", False)),

    64→def _enable_live_review_output() -> None:
    65→    """Best-effort: force line-buffered review output for non-TTY runners."""
    66→    for stream_name in ("stdout", "stderr"):
    67→        stream = getattr(sys, stream_name, None)
    68→        reconfigure = getattr(stream, "reconfigure", None)
    69→        if not callable(reconfigure):
    70→            continue
    71→        try:
    72→            reconfigure(line_buffering=True, write_through=True)
    73→        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    74→            _ = exc

    83→def _mode_flags(opts: ReviewOptions) -> list[bool]:
    84→    import_mode = bool(opts.import_file) and not opts.external_submit
    85→    return [

    88→        bool(opts.import_run_dir),

    96→def _validate_mode_selection(
    97→    opts: ReviewOptions,

   102→        raise CommandError(

   162→        do_external_start(
   163→            args,
   164→            state,
   165→            lang,
   166→            config=runtime.config,
   167→        )
   168→        return
   169→    if opts.external_submit:

   190→                attested_external=opts.attested_external,
   191→                manual_attest=opts.attest,
   192→            ),
   193→        )
   194→        return
   195→
   196→    if opts.import_file:
   197→        do_import(

   207→                manual_attest=opts.attest,

   210→        )
   211→        return

   213→    do_prepare(args, state, lang, state_file, config=runtime.config)

   216→def cmd_review(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   217→    """Prepare or import subjective code review issues."""
   218→    _enable_live_review_output()

   232→    # Default prepare and --run-batches need real scan-backed context rather

   235→        if not require_scan_metrics(state):

   206→def _prepared_packet_contract_mismatch_reason(
   207→    packet: dict[str, object],
   208→    expected_contract: dict[str, object],
   209→) -> str | None:
   210→    """Return mismatch reason for prepared packet reuse, else ``None``."""
   211→    raw_contract = packet.get(_PREPARED_PACKET_CONTRACT_KEY)
   212→    if not isinstance(raw_contract, dict):
   213→        return "missing prepared packet contract metadata"
   214→
   215→    for key in (
   216→        "path",
   217→        "state_path",
   218→        "dimensions",
   219→        "retrospective",
   220→        "retrospective_max_issues",
   221→        "retrospective_max_batch_items",
   222→        "config_hash",
   223→    ):
   224→        if raw_contract.get(key) != expected_contract.get(key):
   225→            return f"contract field '{key}' differs"
   226→    return None

   229→def _try_load_prepared_packet(
   230→    *,
   231→    expected_contract: dict[str, object],
   232→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
   233→    """Load prepared packet from query.json when shape and contract match."""
   234→    try:
   235→        qf = query_file_path()
   236→        if not qf.exists():
   237→            return None, None
   238→        data = json.loads(qf.read_text())
   239→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, RuntimeError):
   240→        return None, "query.json is missing or invalid JSON"
   241→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
   242→        return None, "prepared packet payload is not an object"
   243→    if "investigation_batches" not in data:

   245→    batches = data["investigation_batches"]
   246→    if not isinstance(batches, list) or not batches:
   247→        return None, "prepared packet has no investigation batches"
   248→
   249→    mismatch_reason = _prepared_packet_contract_mismatch_reason(
   250→        data,
   251→        expected_contract,
   252→    )
   253→    if mismatch_reason is not None:
   254→        return None, mismatch_reason
   255→    return data, None

   260→    normalized_results: list[BatchResultPayload] = []

   424→    try:
   425→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   426→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   427→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading run summary: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   428→
   429→    selected = summary.get("selected_batches", [])
   430→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   431→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   432→
   433→    if not selected:
   434→        raise CommandError("no selected batches in run summary.", exit_code=1)
   435→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   436→        raise PacketValidationError(f"blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", exit_code=1)
   437→
   438→    try:
   439→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   440→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   441→        raise PacketValidationError(f"Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   442→
   443→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   444→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path

   446→
   447→def do_import_run(
   448→    run_dir_path: str,
   449→    state: dict,
   450→    lang,
   451→    state_file: str,
   452→    *,
   453→    config: dict | None = None,
   454→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   455→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   456→    scan_path: str = ".",
   457→    dry_run: bool = False,
   458→) -> None:
   459→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   460→
   461→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   462→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   463→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   464→    """
   465→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   466→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   467→
   468→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   469→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   470→    selected = summary.get("selected_batches", [])
   471→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   472→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   473→
   474→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   475→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   476→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in selected]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   477→    output_files = {
   478→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   479→        for idx in selected_indexes
   480→    }
   481→
   482→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   483→    if missing:
   484→        if not results_dir.exists():
   485→            hint = (
   486→                f"Results directory does not exist: {results_dir}\n"
   487→                "  Did you run --run-batches or launch subagents to produce results first?"
   488→            )
   489→        elif len(missing) == len(selected):
   490→            hint = (
   491→                f"No result files found in {results_dir}\n"
   492→                "  Each subagent must write its output to results/batch-N.raw.txt.\n"
   493→                "  Run --run-batches first, or launch subagents on the prompts/ files manually."
   494→            )
   495→        else:
   496→            hint = (
   497→                f"Missing result files in {results_dir}: batches {missing}\n"
   498→                "  Re-run the failed batches or use --allow-partial to import what succeeded."
   499→            )
   500→        raise CommandError(hint, exit_code=1)
   501→
   502→    batch_results, failures = collect_batch_results(
   503→        request=review_batches_mod.CollectBatchResultsRequest(
   504→            selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   505→            failures=[],
   506→            output_files=output_files,
   507→            allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   508→        ),
   509→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   510→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: normalize_batch_result(
   511→            payload,
   512→            dims,
   513→            max_batch_issues=max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   514→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   515→        ),
   516→    )
   517→
   518→    if not batch_results:
   519→        raise CommandError("no valid batch results could be parsed.", exit_code=1)
   520→
   521→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   522→    if failures:
   523→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   524→
   525→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   526→
   527→    # Reuse the canonical merge+metadata boundary from normal batch execution.
   528→    raw_batches = packet.get("investigation_batches", [])
   529→    raw_dim_prompts = packet.get("dimension_prompts")
   530→    batches = explode_to_single_dimension(
   531→        raw_batches if isinstance(raw_batches, list) else [],
   532→        dimension_prompts=raw_dim_prompts if isinstance(raw_dim_prompts, dict) else None,
   533→    )
   534→    packet_dimensions = normalize_dimension_list(packet.get("dimensions", []))
   535→    lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   536→    scored_dimensions = scored_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name) if lang_name else []
   537→    merged_path, missing_after_import = _merge_and_write_results(
   538→        merge_batch_results_fn=_merge_batch_results,
   539→        build_import_provenance_fn=build_batch_import_provenance,
   540→        batch_results=batch_results,
   541→        batches=batches,
   542→        successful_indexes=successful_indexes,
   543→        packet=packet,
   544→        packet_dimensions=packet_dimensions,
   545→        scored_dimensions=scored_dimensions,
   546→        scan_path=scan_path,
   547→        runner=runner,
   548→        prompt_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   549→        stamp=stamp,
   550→        run_dir=run_dir,
   551→        safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text,
   552→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   553→    )
   554→    _enforce_import_coverage(
   555→        missing_after_import=missing_after_import,
   556→        packet_dimensions=packet_dimensions,
   557→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   558→        scan_path=scan_path,
   559→        colorize_fn=colorize,
   560→    )
   561→
   562→    # -- import with trusted source --
   563→    _do_import(
   564→        str(merged_path),
   565→        state,
   566→        lang,
   567→        state_file,
   568→        import_config=ReviewImportConfig(
   569→            config=config,
   570→            allow_partial=allow_partial,
   571→            trusted_assessment_source=True,
   572→            trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   573→        ),
   574→        dry_run=dry_run,
   575→    )
   576→
   577→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   578→    if scan_after_import and not dry_run:
   579→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   580→        if lang_name:
   581→            run_followup_scan(
   582→                lang_name=lang_name,
   583→                scan_path=scan_path,
   584→                deps=FollowupScanDeps(

   587→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   588→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   589→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   590→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   591→                ),
   592→            )
