```
   140→def _build_cluster_meta(
   141→    cluster_name: str, members: list[WorkQueueItem], cluster_data: dict[str, Any]
   142→) -> WorkQueueItem:

   145→    action_type = infer_cluster_action_type(cluster_data, detector=detector)
   146→
   147→    stored_desc = cluster_data.get("description") or ""
   148→    total_in_cluster = len(cluster_issue_ids(cluster_data))
   149→    if stored_desc and total_in_cluster != len(members):
   150→        summary = stored_desc.replace(str(total_in_cluster), str(len(members)))
   151→    else:
   152→        summary = stored_desc or f"{len(members)} issues"
   153→
   154→    action = cluster_data.get("action") or ""
   155→    autofix_hint = cluster_autofix_hint(cluster_data, detector=detector)
   156→    if autofix_hint:
   157→        primary_command = f"desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10"
   158→    else:
   159→        primary_command = action or f"desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10"
   160→
   161→    estimated_impact = max(
   162→        (m.get("estimated_impact", 0.0) for m in members), default=0.0
   163→    )

   180→        ),
   181→        "execution_status": cluster_data.get("execution_status", "review"),
   182→        "confidence": "high",
   183→        "detector": detector,
   184→        "file": "",
   185→        "estimated_impact": estimated_impact,
   186→        "action_steps": cluster_data.get("action_steps") or [],
   187→    }
   188→
   189→
   190→def collapse_clusters(items: list[WorkQueueItem], plan: dict) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   191→    """Replace cluster member items with single cluster meta-items.
   192→
   193→    Both auto-clusters and manual (triage) clusters are collapsed.  Manual
   194→    clusters are inserted at the front in plan order so triage-prioritised
   195→    work appears before auto-clustered mechanical items.
   196→    """
   197→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   198→    if not clusters:
   199→        return items
   200→
   201→    fid_to_cluster: dict[str, str] = {}
   202→    for name, cluster in clusters.items():
   203→        for issue_id in cluster_issue_ids(cluster):
   204→            # Manual clusters take priority when an issue is in both
   205→            if issue_id not in fid_to_cluster or not cluster.get("auto"):
   206→                fid_to_cluster[issue_id] = name
   207→
   208→    if not fid_to_cluster:
   209→        return items
   210→
   211→    # Collect members per cluster (preserving encounter order)
   212→    cluster_members: dict[str, list[WorkQueueItem]] = {}
   213→    for item in items:
   214→        cname = fid_to_cluster.get(item.get("id", ""))
   215→        if cname:
   216→            cluster_members.setdefault(cname, []).append(item)
   217→
   218→    # Build meta-items only for clusters with 2+ members in the queue
   219→    meta_items: dict[str, WorkQueueItem] = {}
   220→    for cname, members in cluster_members.items():
   221→        if len(members) < 2:
   222→            continue
   223→        meta_items[cname] = _build_cluster_meta(
   224→            cname, members, clusters.get(cname, {})
   225→        )
   226→
   227→    # Collect manual cluster names in plan order (for front-insertion)
   228→    manual_names = [
   229→        name for name in clusters
   230→        if not clusters[name].get("auto") and name in meta_items
   231→    ]
   232→
   233→    # Walk in order: replace first auto-cluster member with meta-item,
   234→    # skip subsequent members.  Manual cluster members are always skipped
   235→    # (they'll be inserted at the front).
   236→    seen_clusters: set[str] = set()
   237→    rest: list[WorkQueueItem] = []
   238→    for item in items:
   239→        cname = fid_to_cluster.get(item.get("id", ""))
   240→        if cname and cname in meta_items:
   241→            if cname not in seen_clusters:
   242→                seen_clusters.add(cname)
   243→                # Auto-clusters collapse in-place; manual clusters go to front
   244→                if clusters.get(cname, {}).get("auto"):
   245→                    rest.append(meta_items[cname])
   246→            # skip individual member
   247→        else:
   248→            rest.append(item)
   249→
   250→    # Manual clusters at the front in plan order, then everything else
   251→    manual_result = [meta_items[name] for name in manual_names if name in seen_clusters]
   252→    return manual_result + rest
   253→
   254→

   261→    "stamp_plan_sort_keys",
   262→    "stamp_positions",
   263→]
```

```
    29→def _require_reflect_stage_for_organize(stages: dict) -> bool:

    31→        stages,
    32→        flow="organize",
    33→        messages={
    34→            "observe": (

    36→                '  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."',
    37→            ),
    38→            "reflect": (

    44→
    45→
    46→def _enforce_cluster_activity_for_organize(
    47→    *,
    48→    plan: dict,
    49→    stages: dict,
    50→    manual_clusters: list[str],
    51→    open_review_ids: set[str],
    52→    is_reuse: bool,
    53→    attestation: str | None,
    54→) -> bool:
    55→    """Require enough cluster operations after reflect unless explicitly attested."""
    56→    if not open_review_ids:
    57→        return True
    58→    reflect_ts = stages.get("reflect", {}).get("timestamp", "")
    59→    if not reflect_ts or is_reuse:
    60→        return True
    61→    activity = count_log_activity_since(plan, reflect_ts)
    62→    cluster_ops = sum(
    63→        activity.get(key, 0)
    64→        for key in ("cluster_create", "cluster_add", "cluster_update", "cluster_remove")
    65→    )
    66→    min_ops = max(3, len(manual_clusters))
    67→    if cluster_ops >= min_ops:
    68→        return True
    69→    if attestation and len(attestation.strip()) >= 40:
    70→        print(
    71→            colorize(
    72→                f"  Note: only {cluster_ops} cluster op(s) logged (expected {min_ops}+). "
    73→                "Proceeding with attestation override.",
    74→                "yellow",
    75→            )
    76→        )
    77→        return True
    78→    print(
    79→        colorize(
    80→            f"  Cannot organize: only {cluster_ops} cluster operation(s) logged "
    81→            f"since reflect (need {min_ops}+).",
    82→            "red",
    83→        )
    84→    )
    85→    print(
    86→        colorize(
    87→            "  Cluster operations (create/add/update/remove) are logged automatically\n"
    88→            "  when you use the CLI. Did you create clusters, add issues, and enrich them?",
    89→            "dim",
    90→        )
    91→    )
    92→    print(

    95→            "dim",
    96→        )
    97→    )
```

```
   114→def _upsert_triage_clusters(
   115→    *,
   116→    clusters: dict[str, Cluster],
   117→    triage: TriageResult,
   118→    now: str,
   119→    version: int,
   120→) -> tuple[int, int]:

   127→        if existing and existing.get("thesis"):
   128→            _update_existing_epic_cluster(existing, epic_data, now=now, version=version)
   129→            updated += 1
   130→            continue
   131→        clusters[epic_name] = _create_epic_cluster(
   132→            epic_name=epic_name,
   133→            epic_data=epic_data,
   134→            now=now,

   136→        )
   137→        created += 1

   141→def _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   142→    *,
   143→    order: list[str],
   144→    triage: TriageResult,
   145→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   146→) -> None:
   147→    epic_issue_ids: set[str] = set()
   148→    epic_ordered_ids: list[str] = []
   149→    dismissed_set = set(dismissed_ids)
   150→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   151→        for fid in epic_data["issue_ids"]:
   152→            if fid in epic_issue_ids or fid in dismissed_set:
   153→                continue
   154→            epic_issue_ids.add(fid)
   155→            epic_ordered_ids.append(fid)
   156→
   157→    non_epic_items = [fid for fid in order if fid not in epic_issue_ids]
   158→    order.clear()
   159→    order.extend(epic_ordered_ids)
   160→    order.extend(non_epic_items)

   163→def _set_triage_meta(
   164→    *,
   165→    plan: PlanModel,

   174→    open_review_ids = sorted(
```

```
   278→    if isinstance(epic_triage_meta, dict):
   279→        epic_triage_meta.pop("triage_force_visible", None)
   280→
   281→
   282→def triage_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   283→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   284→    return {
   285→        name: cluster
   286→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   287→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   288→    }
   289→
   290→
   291→def live_planned_queue_ids(plan: dict[str, Any] | None) -> set[str]:
   292→    """Return substantive live queue IDs sourced only from ``queue_order``.
   293→
   294→    Overrides and clusters are ownership metadata — they must never expand
   295→    the live queue.  Only explicit ``queue_order`` entries count.
   296→    """
   297→    if not isinstance(plan, dict):
   298→        return set()
   299→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   300→    return {
   301→        str(issue_id)
   302→        for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   303→        if isinstance(issue_id, str)
   304→        and issue_id
   305→        and issue_id not in skipped_ids
   306→        and not any(issue_id.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES)
   307→    }
   308→
   309→
   310→def executable_objective_ids(
   311→    all_objective_ids: set[str],
   312→    plan: dict[str, Any] | None,
   313→) -> set[str]:
   314→    """Return objective IDs eligible for execution.
   315→
   316→    Before the plan tracks any queue work at all, all objective IDs are
   317→    implicitly executable. Once *any* queue items exist — including synthetic
   318→    review/workflow/triage items — execution becomes queue-driven and only
   319→    objective IDs explicitly present in ``plan["queue_order"]`` remain
   320→    eligible for ``next``.
   321→    """
   322→    if not isinstance(plan, dict):
   323→        return set(all_objective_ids)
   324→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   325→    queued_ids = {
   326→        issue_id
   327→        for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   328→        if isinstance(issue_id, str)
   329→        and issue_id
   330→        and issue_id not in skipped_ids
   331→    }
   332→    live_queue_ids = live_planned_queue_ids(plan)
   333→    queued_objective_ids = all_objective_ids & live_queue_ids
   334→    if queued_objective_ids:
   335→        return queued_objective_ids
   336→    if not queued_ids:
   337→        return set(all_objective_ids) - skipped_ids
   338→    return set()
   339→
   340→
   341→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   342→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   343→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   344→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   345→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   346→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   347→
   348→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   349→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   350→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
```

## Summary: Desloppify Execution Queue and Triage Flow

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete flow of how items enter the execution queue and how triage decides what to process:

---

### 1. **How `desloppify next` Builds Its Queue**

**Source of Truth:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py` and `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/selection.py`

**Queue Building Process:**
- `build_execution_queue()` (in `queue_policy.py:56-72`) calls `_build_work_queue_with_visibility()` with `visibility=QueueVisibility.EXECUTION`
- This invokes `build_queue_snapshot()` which creates a canonical queue snapshot partitioning all items into execution vs backlog
- The snapshot selects items based on **phases** (EXECUTE, TRIAGE, REVIEW, SCAN, WORKFLOW, ASSESSMENT)

**Order Determination - The Critical Path:**

1. **`plan.queue_order` is the primary ordering mechanism** (`schema/__init__.py:220, 291-307`)
   - It's a flat list of issue IDs in priority order
   - Only entries in `queue_order` that are NOT in `plan.skipped` count as "live"
   - This is checked via `live_planned_queue_ids(plan)` which respects the explicit ordering

2. **How items get positions in queue_order:**
   - **Automatic objective issues** come first (when no explicit queue exists)
   - **Promoted items** (`promoted_ids` list) track user-promoted backlog work
   - **Cluster members** get positioned together via triage reorganization (`_reorder_queue_by_dependency()`)
   - **New items** are ranked by natural sort key after planned items (`stamp_plan_sort_keys()` in `plan_order.py:60-83`)

3. **Auto-clusters entry mechanism:**
   - Auto-clusters don't automatically enter the execution queue
   - They exist in `plan.clusters` with `"auto": True` but their member issues stay in **backlog** until explicitly promoted
   - When promoted via `desloppify plan promote auto/<name>`, the `add_promoted_ids()` function (in `promoted_ids.py:17-25`) adds all member IDs to `promoted_ids` and then to `queue_order`
   - They appear in the execution queue only when their constituent issue IDs are in `queue_order`

**Visibility Partitions:**
- **EXECUTION_ITEMS:** Items in `queue_order` (live planned work)
- **BACKLOG_ITEMS:** All objective items NOT in execution (unplanned objective backlog + unclustered mechanical items)

---

### 2. **In the Triage Prompt Generation** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py`)

**`_split_open_issue_buckets()` (lines 159-171):**
```python
def _split_open_issue_buckets(issues):
    open_review: dict = {}
    open_mechanical: dict = {}
    for issue_id, issue in issues.items():
        if issue.get("status") != "open":
            continue
        if is_triage_finding(issue):  # Review findings (review/concerns)
            open_review[issue_id] = issue
            continue
        open_mechanical[issue_id] = issue  # All other open issues
    return open_review, open_mechanical
```

This splits ALL open issues into:
- **`open_review`** → `review_issues` (items where `is_triage_finding()` returns True)
  - Only REVIEW_DEFECT and REVIEW_CONCERN items appear here
  - These are the ones triage sees as "high priority for human review"
- **`open_mechanical`** → `objective_backlog_issues` (MECHANICAL_DEFECT items)
  - Detector-created findings that don't require review judgment
  - These go to the **mechanical backlog** section of the triage prompt

**What the Triager Sees:**

The `build_triage_prompt()` function (lines 562-588) constructs the prompt with these sections:

1. **Existing clusters** (`_append_existing_clusters_section`, lines 292-306)
   - Shows all manual and auto clusters with counts and issue summaries

2. **New issues since last triage** (lines 566-571)
   - Only review issues (`si.review_issues`)

3. **Resolved since last triage** (lines 572-576)
   - Just IDs, for context

4. **Resolved issue context** (lines 577)
   - Snapshot of recently resolved issues to understand patterns

5. **Completed clusters** (lines 578)
   - Completed work for feedback

6. **Recurring dimensions** (lines 579)
   - Issues where same dimension has been resolved before

7. **All open review issues** (lines 580)
   - **Full detailed list** of every review issue with confidence, file, dimension, suggestion
   - This is what triager actually prioritizes and clusters

8. **Dimension scores** (lines 581)
   - Context on strict/overall/objective scores per dimension

9. **MECHANICAL BACKLOG SECTION** (lines 582-586)
   - **This is the key section for your use case**
   - Shows auto-clusters with member counts
   - Auto-clusters are listed as units with descriptions
   - Unclustered mechanical items listed separately

10. **Previously dismissed** (lines 587)

**Key Finding on Mechanical Backlog** (`_append_mechanical_backlog_section`, lines 426-529):

The triager DOES see mechanical/auto-cluster items, but organized as:
- **Auto-clusters section**: Shows top 15 auto-clusters by member count with summaries and autofix hints
- **Unclustered items section**: Shows individual mechanical findings that don't fit any auto-cluster
- The triager is explicitly told: "These detector-created items stay in backlog unless you explicitly promote them into the active queue"
- Instructions show: `` `desloppify plan promote auto/<name>` ``

**Current State:** Auto-clusters ARE already visible but as a **sidebar**, not as triage priorities.

**What Needs to Change for Full Integration:**

The auto-clusters currently live in a separate "Mechanical Backlog" section and are **never grouped into the triage LLM's output clusters**. To make them truly part of triage decision-making:

1. **Option A: Promote them to the prompt's "open issues" context**

   - The triager would see them as "implicit issue groupings already available for promotion"
   - Current code: `auto_clusters` are passed separately (line 214) but not integrated into review_issues logic

2. **Option B: Let triager output explicit promotion instructions**

   - Currently, the schema only accepts clusters the triager creates/updates (lines 262-280)
   - The prompt says triage CAN use `desloppify plan promote` (line 244) but the LLM has no structured way to express this decision

3. **Option C: Pre-populate triage with auto-cluster visibility**
   - Enhance `_append_mechanical_backlog_section()` to show more context about how auto-clusters relate to review issues
   - For example, show that "auto/security has 423 bandit findings" and some might conflict with review decisions

**The Core Issue:** The triager doesn't SEE that promoting `auto/security` would resolve certain mechanical findings, nor does it have a structured way to recommend promotions in its JSON output.

### 4. **How `plan promote` Works**

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/reorder_handlers.py:85-117`

```python
def cmd_plan_promote(args):
    # 1. Resolve patterns to actual issue IDs
    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
    
    # 2. Move items to queue (to "bottom" by default)
    count = move_items(plan, issue_ids, position, target=target)
    
    # 3. CRITICAL: Add to promoted_ids tracking
    add_promoted_ids(plan, issue_ids)  # <-- Key line
    
    # 4. Log and save
    save_plan(plan)
```

**How it Handles Auto-Clusters:**
- When user runs `desloppify plan promote auto/security`
- The pattern resolver (`resolve_ids_from_patterns()`) expands `auto/security` to all its member issue IDs
- Each member ID gets added to both `queue_order` AND `promoted_ids` tracking
- `promoted_ids` is used by `promoted_insertion_index()` to track "where promoted items ended up" for UI/status

**The Organize Agent:**
- The organize stage (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stages/organize.py`) records manual cluster creation
- It does NOT directly promote auto-clusters; that's the user's or downstream agent's responsibility
- Organize just validates that clusters are enriched and consistent

**Location:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:159-171, 426-529`

**Current Usage:**

1. **Split and Partition** (line 196):

2. **Passed to TriageInput** (line 213):

3. **Used in Mechanical Backlog Section** (lines 426-529):
   - Clustered by auto-cluster membership

**Key Insight:** `open_mechanical` is completely **invisible to the LLM**. The triage prompt tells the human triager they exist and can be promoted, but the LLM never has to make decisions about them. This is intentional—mechanical findings are supposed to flow automatically unless triaged out.

```
   125→def _issue_dimension(issue: dict) -> str:
   126→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   127→    if isinstance(detail, dict):
   128→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
   129→        if isinstance(dimension, str):
   130→            return dimension
   131→    return ""

   134→def _recurring_dimensions(
   135→    review_issues: dict[str, dict],
   136→    resolved_issues: dict[str, dict],
   137→) -> dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]:
   138→    open_by_dim: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   139→    for issue_id, issue in review_issues.items():
   140→        dimension = _issue_dimension(issue)
   141→        if dimension:
   142→            open_by_dim.setdefault(dimension, []).append(issue_id)
   143→
   144→    resolved_by_dim: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   145→    for issue_id, issue in resolved_issues.items():
   146→        dimension = _issue_dimension(issue)
   147→        if dimension:
   148→            resolved_by_dim.setdefault(dimension, []).append(issue_id)
   149→
   150→    recurring: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
   151→    for dimension in sorted(set(open_by_dim) & set(resolved_by_dim)):
   152→        recurring[dimension] = {
   153→            "open": sorted(open_by_dim[dimension]),
   154→            "resolved": sorted(resolved_by_dim[dimension]),
   155→        }
   156→    return recurring

   159→def _split_open_issue_buckets(
   160→    issues: dict[str, dict],
   161→) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], dict[str, dict]]:
   162→    open_review: dict[str, dict] = {}
   163→    open_mechanical: dict[str, dict] = {}
   164→    for issue_id, issue in issues.items():
   165→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
   166→            continue
   167→        if is_triage_finding(issue):
   168→            open_review[issue_id] = issue
   169→            continue
   170→        open_mechanical[issue_id] = issue
   171→    return open_review, open_mechanical

   174→def _recent_completed_clusters(meta: dict, plan: PlanModel) -> list[dict]:
   175→    last_completed = meta.get("last_completed_at", "")
   176→    all_completed: list[dict] = plan.get("completed_clusters", [])
   177→    if not last_completed:
   178→        return list(all_completed)
   179→    return [
   180→        cluster for cluster in all_completed
   181→        if cluster.get("completed_at", "") > last_completed
   182→    ]

   185→def collect_triage_input(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> TriageInput:
   186→    """Gather all data needed for the triage LLM prompt."""
   187→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   188→    issues = (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {}))
   189→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   190→    epics = triage_clusters(plan)
   191→    auto_clusters = {
   192→        name: cluster
   193→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   194→        if cluster.get("auto") and not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   195→    }
   196→    open_review, open_mechanical = _split_open_issue_buckets(issues)
   197→    snapshot = build_triage_snapshot(plan, state)
   198→
   199→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   200→    current_review_ids = set(open_review.keys())
   201→    new_since = set(snapshot.new_since_triage_ids)
   202→    resolved_since = triaged_ids - current_review_ids
   203→    previously_dismissed = list(meta.get("dismissed_ids", []))
   204→    version = int(meta.get("version", 0)) + 1
   205→
   206→    # Resolved issue objects (for REFLECT stage)
   207→    resolved_issue_objs = {
   208→        fid: issues[fid] for fid in resolved_since if fid in issues
   209→    }
   210→
   211→    return TriageInput(
   212→        review_issues=open_review,
   213→        objective_backlog_issues=open_mechanical,
   214→        auto_clusters=auto_clusters,
   215→        existing_clusters=dict(epics),
   216→        dimension_scores=state.get("dimension_scores", {}),
   217→        new_since_last=new_since,
   218→        resolved_since_last=resolved_since,
   219→        previously_dismissed=previously_dismissed,
   220→        triage_version=version,
   221→        resolved_issues=resolved_issue_objs,
   222→        completed_clusters=_recent_completed_clusters(meta, plan),
   223→    )

   477→        if member_count <= 0:
   478→            continue
   479→        rendered_clusters.append((name, cluster, member_count))
   480→
   481→    if rendered_clusters:
   482→        parts.append("### Auto-clusters")
   483→        parts.append(
   484→            "These are pre-grouped detector findings. Promote whole clusters with "
   485→            "`desloppify plan promote auto/<name>`."
   486→        )
   487→        rendered_clusters.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[2], item[0]))
   488→        visible_clusters = rendered_clusters[:15]
   489→        for name, cluster, member_count in visible_clusters:
   490→            autofix_hint = _cluster_autofix_hint(cluster)
   491→            hint_suffix = f" [autofix: {autofix_hint}]" if autofix_hint else ""
   492→            summary = _cluster_backlog_summary(name, cluster, member_count)
   493→            parts.append(f"- {name} ({member_count} items){hint_suffix}")
   494→            parts.append(f"  {summary}")
   495→        if len(rendered_clusters) > len(visible_clusters):
   496→            remaining = rendered_clusters[len(visible_clusters):]
   497→            remaining_issues = sum(item[2] for item in remaining)
   498→            parts.append(
   499→                f"- ... and {len(remaining)} more clusters ({remaining_issues} issues)"
   500→            )
   501→
   502→    if unclustered:
   503→        parts.append(
   504→            f"### Unclustered items ({len(unclustered)} items — needs human judgment or isolated findings)"
   505→        )
   506→        parts.append(
   507→            "Promote individually with `desloppify plan promote <issue-id>`, or group related items into a manual cluster."
   508→        )
   509→        sample_ids = sorted(
   510→            unclustered,
   511→            key=lambda issue_id: (
   512→                _confidence_sort_key(unclustered[issue_id]),
   513→                issue_id,
   514→            ),
   515→        )[:10]
   516→        for issue_id in sample_ids:
   517→            issue = unclustered[issue_id]
   518→            confidence = str(issue.get("confidence", "medium"))
   519→            summary = str(issue.get("summary", "(no summary)"))
   520→            parts.append(f"- [{confidence}] {issue_id} — {summary}")
   521→        if len(unclustered) > len(sample_ids):
   522→            parts.append(
   523→                f"- ... and {len(unclustered) - len(sample_ids)} more unclustered items"
   524→            )
   525→
   526→    parts.append("Browse full backlog: `desloppify backlog`")
   527→    parts.append("Inspect a cluster: `desloppify plan cluster show auto/<name>`")
   528→    parts.append("Inspect an issue: `desloppify show <issue-id>`")
   529→    parts.append("")
   530→
   531→
   532→def _cluster_autofix_hint(cluster: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   533→    return cluster_autofix_hint(cluster) or ""
   534→
   535→
   536→def _cluster_backlog_summary(name: str, cluster: dict[str, Any], member_count: int) -> str:
   537→    description = str(cluster.get("description") or "").strip()
   538→    if description:
   539→        return description
   540→    title = name.removeprefix("auto/").replace("-", " ")
   541→    if title:
   542→        return f"Address {member_count} {title} findings"
   543→    return f"Address {member_count} detector findings"
   544→
   545→
   546→def _confidence_sort_key(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
   547→    confidence = str(issue.get("confidence", "medium")).lower()
   548→    order = {"high": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2}
   549→    return order.get(confidence, 1)
   550→
   551→
   552→def _append_previously_dismissed_section(parts: list[str], dismissed_ids: list[str]) -> None:
   553→    if not dismissed_ids:
   554→        return
   555→    parts.append(f"## Previously dismissed ({len(dismissed_ids)})")
   556→    parts.append("Maintain unless contradicted by new evidence.")
   557→    for issue_id in dismissed_ids:
   558→        parts.append(f"- {issue_id}")
   559→    parts.append("")
   560→
   561→
   562→def build_triage_prompt(si: TriageInput) -> str:
   563→    """Build the user-facing prompt content with all issue data."""
   564→    parts: list[str] = []
   565→    _append_existing_clusters_section(parts, si.existing_clusters)
   566→    _append_changed_issue_section(
   567→        parts,
   568→        title="New issues since last triage",
   569→        issue_ids=si.new_since_last,
   570→        issues=si.review_issues,
   571→    )
   572→    _append_changed_issue_section(
   573→        parts,
   574→        title="Resolved since last triage",
   575→        issue_ids=si.resolved_since_last,
   576→    )
   577→    _append_resolved_issue_context(parts, si.resolved_issues)
   578→    _append_completed_clusters_section(parts, si.completed_clusters)
   579→    _append_recurring_dimensions_section(parts, si.review_issues, si.resolved_issues)
   580→    _append_open_review_issues_section(parts, si.review_issues)
   581→    _append_dimension_scores_section(parts, si.dimension_scores)
   582→    _append_mechanical_backlog_section(
   583→        parts,
   584→        si.objective_backlog_issues,
   585→        si.auto_clusters,
   586→    )
   587→    _append_previously_dismissed_section(parts, si.previously_dismissed)
   588→    return "\n".join(parts)
   589→
   590→__all__ = [
   591→    "_TRIAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT",
   592→    "ContradictionNote",
   593→    "DismissedIssue",
   594→    "TriageInput",
   595→    "TriageResult",
   596→    "build_triage_prompt",
```

```
   128→            _update_existing_epic_cluster(existing, epic_data, now=now, version=version)
   129→            updated += 1

   132→            epic_name=epic_name,

   141→def _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   142→    *,
   143→    order: list[str],
   144→    triage: TriageResult,
   145→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   146→) -> None:
   147→    epic_issue_ids: set[str] = set()
   148→    epic_ordered_ids: list[str] = []

   150→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   151→        for fid in epic_data["issue_ids"]:
   152→            if fid in epic_issue_ids or fid in dismissed_set:
   153→                continue
   154→            epic_issue_ids.add(fid)
   155→            epic_ordered_ids.append(fid)
   156→
   157→    non_epic_items = [fid for fid in order if fid not in epic_issue_ids]
   158→    order.clear()
   159→    order.extend(epic_ordered_ids)
   160→    order.extend(non_epic_items)

   192→def apply_triage_to_plan(
   193→    plan: PlanModel,
   194→    state: StateModel,
   195→    triage: TriageResult,
   196→    *,
   197→    trigger: str = "manual",
   198→) -> TriageMutationResult:
   199→    """Apply parsed triage result to the living plan.
   200→
   201→    1. Creates/updates triage clusters in plan["clusters"]
   202→    2. Marks dismissed issues as triaged_out skips
   203→    3. Reorders queue_order to group cluster members by dependency_order
   204→    4. Updates epic_triage_meta with snapshot hash
   205→    """
   206→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   207→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   208→    now = utc_now()
   209→    result = TriageMutationResult()
   210→    result.strategy_summary = triage.strategy_summary
   211→
   212→    clusters = plan["clusters"]
   213→    skipped: dict = plan["skipped"]
   214→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   215→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   216→    version = int(meta.get("version", 0)) + 1
   217→    result.triage_version = version
   218→
   219→    created, updated = _upsert_triage_clusters(
   220→        clusters=clusters,
   221→        triage=triage,
   222→        now=now,
   223→        version=version,
   224→    )
   225→    result.epics_created += created
   226→    result.epics_updated += updated
   227→
   228→    dismissed_ids, dismiss_count = dismiss_triage_issues(
   229→        triage=triage,
   230→        order=order,
   231→        skipped=skipped,
   232→        now=now,
   233→        version=version,
   234→        scan_count=int(state.get("scan_count", 0)),
   235→    )
   236→    result.issues_dismissed += dismiss_count
   237→
   238→    # Sync state status for dismissed issues so state is authoritative.
   239→    issues = (state.get("work_items") or state.get("issues", {}))
   240→    triaged_out_status = skip_kind_state_status("triaged_out")
   241→    for fid in dismissed_ids:
   242→        issue = issues.get(fid)
   243→        if issue and issue.get("status") == "open" and triaged_out_status:
   244→            issue["status"] = triaged_out_status
   245→            issue["note"] = f"Triaged out by epic triage v{version}"
   246→
   247→    _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   248→        order=order,
   249→        triage=triage,
   250→        dismissed_ids=dismissed_ids,
   251→    )

   253→    _set_triage_meta(

   257→        now=now,
   258→        version=version,
   259→        dismissed_ids=dismissed_ids,
   260→        trigger=trigger,
   261→    )
   262→    plan["updated"] = now
   263→
   264→    return result
   265→
```

```
1→"""Helpers for tracking user-promoted queue IDs."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from typing import Any
     6→
     7→
     8→def _promoted_ids(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
     9→    promoted = plan.get("promoted_ids")
    10→    if isinstance(promoted, list):
    11→        return promoted
    12→    promoted = []
    13→    plan["promoted_ids"] = promoted
    14→    return promoted
    15→
    16→
    17→def add_promoted_ids(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_ids: list[str]) -> None:
    18→    """Append issue IDs to promoted_ids preserving existing order."""
    19→    promoted = _promoted_ids(plan)
    20→    existing = set(promoted)
    21→    for issue_id in issue_ids:
    22→        if issue_id in existing:
    23→            continue
    24→        promoted.append(issue_id)
    25→        existing.add(issue_id)
    26→
    27→
    28→def prune_promoted_ids(plan: dict[str, Any], issue_ids: set[str] | list[str]) -> None:
    29→    """Remove issue IDs from promoted_ids if present."""
    30→    remove_set = set(issue_ids)
    31→    if not remove_set:
    32→        return
    33→    promoted = _promoted_ids(plan)
    34→    plan["promoted_ids"] = [issue_id for issue_id in promoted if issue_id not in remove_set]
    35→
    36→
    37→def promoted_insertion_index(order: list[str], plan: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    38→    """Return insertion index immediately after the last promoted item."""
    39→    promoted = set(_promoted_ids(plan))
    40→    if not promoted:
    41→        return 0
    42→    last_idx = -1
    43→    for idx, issue_id in enumerate(order):
    44→        if issue_id in promoted:
    45→            last_idx = idx
    46→    return last_idx + 1 if last_idx >= 0 else 0
    47→
    48→
    49→__all__ = [
    50→    "add_promoted_ids",
    51→    "promoted_insertion_index",
    52→    "prune_promoted_ids",
    53→]
    54→
```

```
    18→def _state_with_review_issues(*ids: str) -> dict:
    19→    """Build minimal state with open review issues."""
    20→    issues = {}
    21→    for fid in ids:
    22→        issues[fid] = {
    23→            "status": "open",
    24→            "detector": "review",
    25→            "file": "test.py",
    26→            "summary": f"Review issue {fid}",
    27→            "confidence": "medium",
    28→            "tier": 2,
    29→            "detail": {"dimension": "abstraction_fitness"},
    30→        }
    31→    return {"issues": issues, "scan_count": 5, "dimension_scores": {}}
    32→
    33→
    34→def _state_empty() -> dict:
    35→    return {"issues": {}, "scan_count": 1, "dimension_scores": {}}
    36→
    37→
    38→def _triage_with_epics(*epics: dict) -> TriageResult:
    39→    """Build a TriageResult with the given epics and no dismissals."""
    40→    return TriageResult(
    41→        strategy_summary="Test strategy",
    42→        epics=list(epics),
    43→    )
    44→
    45→
    46→def _epic(
    47→    name: str,
    48→    issue_ids: list[str],
    49→    dependency_order: int = 1,
    50→    *,
    51→    direction: str = "delete",
    52→    dismissed: list[str] | None = None,
    53→    agent_safe: bool = False,
    54→    status: str = "pending",
    55→    action_steps: list[str] | None = None,
    56→) -> dict:
    57→    """Build a minimal epic dict for TriageResult."""
    58→    return {
    59→        "name": name,
    60→        "thesis": f"Thesis for {name}",
    61→        "direction": direction,
    62→        "root_cause": f"Root cause for {name}",
    63→        "issue_ids": issue_ids,
    64→        "dismissed": dismissed or [],
    65→        "agent_safe": agent_safe,
    66→        "dependency_order": dependency_order,
    67→        "action_steps": action_steps or [],
    68→        "status": status,
    69→    }
```

```json
  "old_string": "def apply_triage_to_plan(",
  "new_string": "def _apply_auto_cluster_decisions(\n    *,\n    plan: PlanModel,\n    decisions: list[AutoClusterDecision],\n    order: list[str],\n    now: str,\n    version: int,\n    result: TriageMutationResult,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Process auto_cluster_decisions from the triage result.\n\n    - promote: add cluster issue IDs to queue_order\n    - skip: mark the cluster as skipped in the plan\n    - break_up: record the decision for downstream processing\n    \"\"\"\n    clusters = plan[\"clusters\"]\n\n    for decision in decisions:\n        cluster_name = decision.cluster\n        cluster = clusters.get(cluster_name)\n        if cluster is None:\n            continue\n\n        action = decision.action\n\n        if action == \"promote\":\n            issue_ids = cluster.get(\"issue_ids\", [])\n            existing_in_order = set(order)\n            new_ids = [\n                fid for fid in issue_ids\n                if isinstance(fid, str) and fid not in existing_in_order\n            ]\n            # Determine insertion position based on priority hint\n            priority = (decision.priority or \"\").lower().strip()\n            if priority == \"first\":\n                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):\n                    order.insert(i, fid)\n            elif priority.startswith(\"after \"):\n                target = priority[len(\"after \"):]\n                insert_idx = len(order)\n                for idx, item in enumerate(order):\n                    if target in item:\n                        insert_idx = idx + 1\n                        break\n                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):\n                    order.insert(insert_idx + i, fid)\n            elif priority.startswith(\"before \"):\n                target = priority[len(\"before \"):]\n                insert_idx = len(order)\n                for idx, item in enumerate(order):\n                    if target in item:\n                        insert_idx = idx\n                        break\n                for i, fid in enumerate(new_ids):\n                    order.insert(insert_idx + i, fid)\n            else:\n                # \"last\" or unrecognized: append to end\n                order.extend(new_ids)\n\n            cluster[\"execution_status\"] = EXECUTION_STATUS_ACTIVE\n            cluster[\"updated_at\"] = now\n            cluster[\"triage_version\"] = version\n            result.auto_clusters_promoted += 1\n\n        elif action == \"skip\":\n            cluster[\"triage_skip\"] = {\n                \"reason\": decision.reason,\n                \"skipped_at\": now,\n                \"triage_version\": version,\n            }\n            cluster[\"updated_at\"] = now\n            result.auto_clusters_skipped += 1\n\n        elif action == \"break_up\":\n            cluster[\"triage_break_up\"] = {\n                \"reason\": decision.reason,\n                \"sub_clusters\": decision.sub_clusters,\n                \"decided_at\": now,\n                \"triage_version\": version,\n            }\n            cluster[\"updated_at\"] = now\n            result.auto_clusters_broken_up += 1\n\n\ndef apply_triage_to_plan("
}
```

Fix the staged triage pipeline in /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify so that auto-clusters get mandatory treatment at each stage, similar to review issues.

## Current Problem

The staged triage pipeline (observe → reflect → organize → enrich → sense-check → complete) treats auto-clusters as optional. The reflect stage says "silence means it stays in backlog" and no stage validates that auto-cluster decisions were made. Review issues get a mandatory coverage ledger but auto-clusters have no equivalent.

## What Needs to Change

### 1. Reflect stage instructions (`desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_instruction_blocks.py`)

Around lines 137-144, change step 7 from "silence means leave in backlog" to requiring an explicit decision for each auto-cluster. The triager must include a `## Backlog Decisions` section in their reflect report listing every auto-cluster with a decision: promote, skip (with reason), or supersede (absorb into a review cluster). This should be mandatory like the Coverage Ledger is for review issues.

Change:
```
   - **leave**: say nothing. Silence means it stays in backlog.
```
To require explicit decisions. Something like:
```
   - **skip**: explicitly skip with a reason (e.g., "mostly test noise", "low value").
   You MUST make an explicit decision for every auto-cluster. Include a `## Backlog Decisions` 
   section listing each auto-cluster with: promote, skip (with reason), or supersede.
```

### 2. Organize stage instructions (same file, around line 218-220)

The organize stage already mentions promoting backlog items. Make it clear that the organize stage must execute ALL the backlog decisions from reflect — not just the promotions, but also the skips.

### 3. Reflect stage validation (`desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/reflect_accounting.py`)

Check if there's validation that the reflect report covers auto-clusters. If not, add validation that warns when auto-clusters exist but no backlog decisions section is found in the reflect report.

### 4. Organize stage validation (`desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/organize_policy.py`)  

Check if there's validation for organize. If auto-clusters were mentioned in reflect with "promote" decisions, validate that the organize stage actually promoted them.

### 5. The completion flow (`desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/completion_flow.py` or `stages/completion.py`)

Make sure the `auto_cluster_decisions` from the prompt.py schema is also processed when completing via the staged pipeline, not just the single-shot path.

## Important Constraints

- Read the existing code carefully before making changes — understand the validation framework
- Don't break existing tests — run `python -m pytest desloppify/tests/ -q --tb=short` after
- Keep backward compatibility — warn but don't fail if backlog decisions are missing
- The key insight: auto-clusters should be REQUIRED in the reflect stage's output, just like the coverage ledger is required for review issues
- Keep changes minimal and focused

Create a commit when done. Do NOT push.

   127→   problem, skip it. Valid skip reasons:

   129→   - "the current code is clear and simple despite being theoretically suboptimal"

   287→
   288→def _enrich_instructions(mode: PromptMode = "self_record") -> str:
   289→    subagent_block = """\
   290→**USE SUBAGENTS — one per cluster.** Each subagent MUST:
   291→
   292→1. Run `desloppify plan cluster show <name>` to get steps, members, and reviewer suggestions

   300→    tail = """\

   306→    if mode == "output_only":
   307→        subagent_block = """\
   308→**USE SUBAGENTS — one per cluster.** Each subagent MUST:

   310→1. Inspect the cluster definition provided in the prompt context

   321→    return f"""\
   322→## ENRICH Stage Instructions
   323→
   324→Your task: make EVERY step executor-ready. The test: could a developer who has never seen
   325→this codebase read your step detail and make the change without asking a single question?
   326→
   327→If the answer is "they'd need to figure out which file" or "they'd need to understand the
   328→context" — your step is not ready. Be specific enough that the work is mechanical.
   329→Use the organize report included above as the authoritative cluster plan; do not re-derive
   330→strategy from old triage runs unless you find a concrete mismatch you need to explain.
   331→
   332→### Requirements (ALL BLOCKING — confirmation will reject if not met)
   333→
   334→1. Every step MUST have `--detail` with 80+ chars INCLUDING at least one file path (src/... or supabase/...)
   335→2. Every step MUST have `--issue-refs` linking it to specific review issue hash(es)
   336→3. Every step MUST have `--effort` tag (trivial/small/medium/large) — set INDIVIDUALLY, not bulk
   337→4. File paths in detail MUST exist on disk (validator checks this)
   338→5. No step may reference a skipped/wontfixed issue in its issue_refs
   339→
   340→### How to enrich
   341→
   342→{subagent_block}
   343→
   344→### Common lazy patterns to avoid
   345→
   346→**Copying the issue description as step detail.** The issue says "useGenerationsPaneController
   347→returns 60+ values mixing concerns." That's a PROBLEM description. The step detail should say
   348→"In src/shared/components/GenerationsPane/hooks/useGenerationsPaneController.ts (283 lines),
   349→extract lines 45-89 (filter state: activeFilter, setActiveFilter, filterOptions, applyFilter)
   350→into a new useGenerationFilters hook. The controller imports and spreads the sub-hook's return."
   351→
   352→**Vague action verbs.** "Refactor", "clean up", "improve", "fix" are not actions.
   353→"Extract lines 45-89 into useGenerationFilters", "delete lines 12-18", "rename the file
   354→from X to Y and update the 3 imports in A.tsx, B.tsx, C.tsx" are actions.
   355→
   356→**Guessing file paths.** If you write `src/shared/lib/jsonNarrowing.ts` and it doesn't exist,
   357→confirmation will block. READ the file system. Only reference files you've verified exist.
   358→
   359→**Bulk effort tags.** Don't mark everything "small". A file rename with 2 imports is "trivial".
   360→Decomposing a 400-line hook into 3 sub-hooks is "medium" or "large". Think about each one.
   361→
   362→**Over-engineering the fix.** KISS: the fix should be simpler than the problem. If you're
   363→adding interfaces, registries, factory methods, or configuration to fix a code smell, the
   364→cure is worse than the disease. Prefer: delete code > inline code > extract a function >
   365→add an abstraction. If the simplest fix is "delete these 10 lines," say that — don't
   366→propose a refactoring framework.
   367→
   368→### Examples
   369→
   370→**GOOD step detail:**

   373→to capture previous queryClient state before optimistic update. In onError callback, restore
   374→previous state and change showToast from false to true."
   375→--issue-refs 79baeebf --effort small

   381→--detail "Decompose god-hooks"  # What file? What hooks? Into what?
   382→--detail "Address the issues identified in the observe stage"  # This says nothing
   383→```
   384→
   385→### Do NOT mark steps as done
   386→
   387→Use `--update-step N` to add detail, effort, and issue-refs.
   388→Do NOT use `--done-step` — steps are only marked done when actual code changes are made.
   389→
   390→### File path rules
   391→
   392→Only reference files that exist RIGHT NOW. Do not reference files that a step will create
   393→(e.g., a new shared module) or rename targets (the new filename after a rename). Reference
   394→the current source file and describe what will change. The path validator will block
   395→confirmation if paths don't exist on disk.
   396→
   397→{tail}

   405→    structure_fix_block = """\

   409→    value_commands = """\

   412→- `desloppify plan cluster show <name>` to inspect cluster members and steps
   413→- `desloppify show <issue-id-or-hash> --no-budget` to re-read the underlying finding
   414→- `desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --update-step N --detail "..." --effort small`

   440→    investigation_hint = (

   443→        if mode == "self_record"

   445→    )
   446→    constraints = render_constraints(header="   Also flag steps that:", bullet="   - ")
   447→    return f"""\
   448→## SENSE-CHECK Stage Instructions
   449→
   450→This stage is handled by three subagents. If you are being run as a
   451→single-subprocess fallback, perform ALL three checks below.
   452→
   453→Execution order: content batches (parallel) → structure batch → value batch (sequential).
   454→Value runs last because it needs the corrected plan state from content and structure.
   455→
   456→### Content Check (per cluster)
   457→{investigation_hint}For EVERY step in every cluster, read the actual source file and verify:
   458→1. OVER-ENGINEERING (check FIRST — if the fix fails this, skip the rest):
   459→   Would this change make the codebase *worse*? Flag steps that:
   460→   - Add abstractions, wrappers, or indirection for a one-time operation
   461→   - Introduce unnecessary config/feature-flags/generalization
   462→   - Make simple code harder to read for marginal benefit
   463→   - Gold-plate beyond what the issue actually requires
   464→   - Trade one smell for a worse one (e.g. fix duplication by adding a fragile base class)
   465→   - Add more lines of code than they remove (net complexity increase)
   466→{constraints}
   467→   Remove or simplify over-engineered steps. If the whole cluster is net-negative,
   468→   recommend removing it entirely — don't just flag it, say "skip this cluster."
   469→2. STALENESS: Is the problem still present, or already fixed?
   470→3. LINE NUMBERS: Does the code at the claimed lines match the step description?
   471→4. NAMES: Do function/variable/type names in the step exist in the file?
   472→5. COUNTS: Are counts ("update the 3 imports") accurate?
   473→6. VAGUENESS: Could a developer with zero context execute this step?
   474→7. EFFORT TAGS: Does the tag match actual scope?
   475→8. DUPLICATES: Flag steps that duplicate work in another cluster.
   476→
   477→{content_fix_block}
   478→
   479→### Structure Check (global)
   480→Build a file-touch graph and check:
   481→1. SHARED FILES: Two clusters touching same file without --depends-on → add dependency
   482→2. MISSING CASCADE: Rename/remove without importer updates → add cascade step
   483→3. CIRCULAR DEPS: Flag cycles, don't add them
   484→
   485→{structure_fix_block}
   486→
   487→### Value Check (global — YAGNI/KISS pass)
   488→
   489→Walk the CURRENT planned work item by item and make the final judgment about value.
   490→Ask: does doing this make the codebase genuinely better? Beauty is a valid reason to keep work,
   491→but not if it buys that beauty with new indirection, wrappers, abstraction layers, or confusion.
   492→
   493→For EVERY live queue target, choose exactly one:
   494→1. `keep` — clearly improves correctness, clarity, cohesion, simplicity, or elegance
   495→2. `tighten` — worth doing, but the plan must be simplified or made more concrete first
   496→3. `skip` — the fix would add churn, indirection, coordination, or abstraction for too little gain
   497→
   498→What should usually be skipped:
   499→- facade pruning that just spreads imports
   500→- abstraction-for-abstraction's-sake
   501→- tiny theoretical cleanups that make the code harder to follow
   502→- fixes whose implementation is more complicated than the current code
   503→
   504→What can still be worth keeping:
   505→- simplifications that delete layers or reduce branching
   506→- aesthetic cleanups that genuinely improve readability without adding machinery
   507→- focused unifications that make naming or flow more coherent with less confusion
   508→
   509→{value_commands}
   510→
   511→Required process:
   512→1. Re-read the actual code behind each queue target.
   513→2. Apply the rubric above, not the raw issue title.
   514→3. Tighten any keeper whose steps are too vague, too broad, or too complicated.
   515→4. Permanently skip anything that fails the value test.
   516→5. Delete dead clusters after skipping all their members.
   517→
   518→Required report structure — include a Decision Ledger section:
   519→```
   520→## Decision Ledger
   521→- cluster-or-id -> keep
   522→- cluster-or-id -> tighten
   523→- cluster-or-id -> skip
   524→```
   525→
   526→{tail}
   527→"""

```
   269→            short_id_usage=short_id_usage,

   271→        if not issue_id:
   272→            continue
   273→        hits[issue_id] += 1
   274→        _append_disposition_if_supported(
   275→            dispositions,
   276→            issue_id=issue_id,
   277→            decision=decision,
   278→            target=target,
   279→        )
   280→
   281→    return _LedgerParseResult(
   282→        hits=hits,
   283→        dispositions=dispositions,
   284→        found_section=found_section,
   285→    )
   286→
   287→
   288→def parse_reflect_dispositions(
   289→    report: str,
   290→    valid_ids: set[str],
   291→) -> list[ReflectDisposition]:
   292→    """Parse structured dispositions from the Coverage Ledger section."""
   293→    return _walk_coverage_ledger(report, valid_ids).dispositions
   294→
   295→
   296→def analyze_reflect_issue_accounting(
   297→    *,
   298→    report: str,
   299→    valid_ids: set[str],
   300→) -> tuple[set[str], list[str], list[str]]:
   301→    """Return cited, missing, and duplicate issue IDs referenced by reflect."""
   302→    result = _walk_coverage_ledger(report, valid_ids)
   303→    if result.found_section and result.hits:
   304→        cited = set(result.hits)
   305→        duplicates = sorted(issue_id for issue_id, count in result.hits.items() if count > 1)
   306→        missing = sorted(valid_ids - cited)
   307→        return cited, missing, duplicates
   308→
   309→    maps = _build_id_resolution_maps(valid_ids)
   310→    cited = extract_issue_citations(report, valid_ids)
   311→    for issue_id in valid_ids:
   312→        if issue_id in report:
   313→            cited.add(issue_id)
   314→
   315→    short_hits = _collect_legacy_short_hex_hits(report, maps)
   316→    cited.update(short_hits)
   317→
   318→    duplicates = sorted(issue_id for issue_id, count in short_hits.items() if count > 1)
   319→    missing = sorted(valid_ids - cited)
   320→    return cited, missing, duplicates
   321→
   322→
   323→def _collect_legacy_short_hex_hits(
   324→    report: str,
   325→    maps: _IdResolutionMaps,
   326→) -> Counter[str]:
   327→    short_hits: Counter[str] = Counter()
   328→    for token in re.findall(r"[0-9a-f]{8,}", report):
   329→        resolved = maps.short_hex_map.get(token)
   330→        if resolved:
   331→            short_hits[resolved] += 1
   332→    return short_hits
   333→
   334→
   335→def validate_reflect_accounting(
   336→    *,
   337→    report: str,
   338→    valid_ids: set[str],
   339→) -> tuple[bool, set[str], list[str], list[str]]:
   340→    """Require the reflect report to account for each open issue exactly once."""
   341→    cited, missing, duplicates = analyze_reflect_issue_accounting(
   342→        report=report,
   343→        valid_ids=valid_ids,
   344→    )
   345→    if not missing and not duplicates:
   346→        return True, cited, missing, duplicates
   347→
   348→    print(
   349→        colorize(
   350→            "  Reflect report must account for every open review issue exactly once.",
   351→            "red",
   352→        )
   353→    )
   354→    if missing:
   355→        missing_short = ", ".join(issue_id.rsplit("::", 1)[-1] for issue_id in missing[:10])
   356→        print(colorize(f"    Missing: {missing_short}", "yellow"))
   357→    if duplicates:
   358→        duplicate_short = ", ".join(issue_id.rsplit("::", 1)[-1] for issue_id in duplicates[:10])
   359→        print(colorize(f"    Duplicated: {duplicate_short}", "yellow"))
   360→    print(colorize("  Fix the reflect blueprint before running organize.", "dim"))
   361→    if missing:
   362→        print(colorize("  Expected format — include a ## Coverage Ledger section:", "dim"))
   363→        print(colorize('    - <hash> -> cluster "cluster-name"', "dim"))
   364→        print(colorize('    - <hash> -> skip "reason"', "dim"))
   365→        print(colorize("  Also accepted: bare hashes, colon-separated, comma-separated.", "dim"))
   366→    return False, cited, missing, duplicates
   367→
   368→

   371→    "analyze_reflect_issue_accounting",
   372→    "parse_reflect_dispositions",
```

```
   142→def _build_actual_disposition_index(plan: dict) -> dict[str, ActualDisposition]:
   143→    """Build a lookup from issue ID to its actual disposition in plan state."""
   144→    index: dict[str, ActualDisposition] = {}
   145→

   147→        if cluster.get("auto"):

   149→        for fid in cluster_issue_ids(cluster):

   151→
   152→    for fid in (plan.get("skipped", {}) or {}):
   153→        if isinstance(fid, str):

   159→def _disposition_matches(intended: ReflectDisposition, actual: ActualDisposition) -> bool:
   160→    """True when the actual plan state satisfies the intended disposition."""
   161→    if intended.decision == "permanent_skip":
   162→        return actual.kind == "skipped"
   163→    if intended.decision == "cluster":
   164→        return actual.kind == "clustered" and actual.cluster_name == intended.target

   168→def validate_organize_against_dispositions(
   169→    *,

   172→    """Check that plan mutations match the unified issue_dispositions map.
   173→
   174→    Preferred over ``validate_organize_against_reflect_ledger`` when the
   175→    disposition map exists.  Only checks entries with a ``decision`` field
   176→    (i.e. entries that have been through observe auto-skip or reflect).
   177→    """
   178→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   179→    dispositions = meta.get("issue_dispositions", {})
   180→    if not dispositions:
   181→        return []
   182→
   183→    # Only validate entries that have a decision
   184→    decided = [
   185→        (issue_id, disp)
   186→        for issue_id, disp in dispositions.items()
   187→        if disp.get("decision")
   188→    ]
   189→    if not decided:
   190→        return []
   191→
   192→    actuals = _build_actual_disposition_index(plan)
   193→    unplaced = ActualDisposition(kind="unplaced")
   194→    mismatches: list[LedgerMismatch] = []
   195→
   196→    for issue_id, disp in decided:
   197→        decision = disp["decision"]
   198→        target = disp.get("target", "")
   199→        # Normalize to ReflectDisposition for the mismatch report
   200→        reflect_decision = "permanent_skip" if decision == "skip" else decision
   201→        intended = ReflectDisposition(
   202→            issue_id=issue_id,
   203→            decision=reflect_decision,
   204→            target=target,
   205→        )
   206→        actual = actuals.get(issue_id, unplaced)
   207→        if not _disposition_matches(intended, actual):
   208→            mismatches.append(LedgerMismatch(intended=intended, actual=actual))
   209→
   210→    return mismatches

   213→def validate_organize_against_reflect_ledger(
   214→    *,
   215→    plan: dict,
   216→    stages: dict,
   217→) -> list[LedgerMismatch]:
   218→    """Check that plan mutations match the reflect disposition ledger."""
   219→    raw_ledger = stages.get("reflect", {}).get("disposition_ledger")
   220→    if not raw_ledger:
   221→        return []
   222→
   223→    ledger = [ReflectDisposition.from_dict(d) for d in raw_ledger]
   224→    actuals = _build_actual_disposition_index(plan)
   225→    unplaced = ActualDisposition(kind="unplaced")
   226→
   227→    return [
   228→        LedgerMismatch(intended=d, actual=actuals.get(d.issue_id, unplaced))
   229→        for d in ledger
   230→        if not _disposition_matches(d, actuals.get(d.issue_id, unplaced))
   231→    ]
   232→
   233→
   234→def _validate_organize_against_ledger_or_error(

   240→    # Prefer unified disposition map when available

   242→    if not mismatches:
```

```
   162→
   163→    Organize/enrich can legitimately use plan skip commands on live review IDs.
   164→    Those commands clear the postflight-scan marker because they mutate queue
   165→    coverage for real issues. Triage completion is still operating on the same
   166→    scan snapshot, so leaving the marker cleared incorrectly bounces `next`
   167→    back to `workflow::run-scan` instead of the freshly triaged review work.
   168→    """
   169→    if not state.get("last_scan"):
   170→        return
   171→    mark_postflight_scan_completed(
   172→        plan,
   173→        scan_count=int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0),
   174→    )
   175→
   176→
   177→def apply_completion(
   178→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   179→    plan: PlanModel,
   180→    strategy: str,
   181→    *,
   182→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   183→    completion_mode: str = "manual_triage",
   184→    completion_note: str = "",
   185→) -> None:
   186→    """Shared completion logic: update meta, remove triage stage IDs, save."""
   187→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   188→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   189→    state = runtime.state
   190→
   191→    coverage_ids = coverage_open_ids(plan, state)
   192→    organized, total, clusters = triage_coverage(plan, open_review_ids=coverage_ids)
   193→
   194→    purge_ids(
   195→        plan,
   196→        [*TRIAGE_IDS, WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID],
   197→    )
   198→    existing_strategy = _normalize_summary_text(
   199→        ensure_triage_meta(plan).get("strategy_summary", "")
   200→    )
   201→    meta, effective_strategy_summary = _sync_completion_meta(
   202→        plan=plan,
   203→        state=state,
   204→        strategy=strategy,
   205→        completion_mode=completion_mode,
   206→        completion_note=completion_note,
   207→        coverage_ids=coverage_ids,
   208→    )
   209→    _archive_and_clear_triage_stages(
   210→        meta,
   211→        effective_strategy_summary=effective_strategy_summary,
   212→        existing_strategy=existing_strategy,
   213→        completion_mode=completion_mode,
   214→        completion_note=completion_note,
   215→    )
   216→    _restore_postflight_scan_completion_for_current_scan(
   217→        plan=plan,
   218→        state=state,
   219→    )
   220→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   221→    _print_completion_summary(
   222→        clusters=clusters,
   223→        organized=organized,
   224→        total=total,
   225→        completion_mode=completion_mode,
   226→        effective_strategy_summary=effective_strategy_summary,
   227→    )
   228→
   229→
   230→def count_log_activity_since(plan: PlanModel, since: str) -> dict[str, int]:
   231→    """Count execution-log activity by action since a timestamp string."""
   232→    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   233→    for raw_entry in ensure_execution_log(plan):
   234→        if "timestamp" not in raw_entry or "action" not in raw_entry:
   235→            continue
   236→        timestamp = raw_entry["timestamp"]
   237→        action = raw_entry["action"]
   238→        if not isinstance(timestamp, str) or not isinstance(action, str):
   239→            continue
   240→        if timestamp >= since:
   241→            counts[action] += 1
   242→    return dict(counts)
   243→
   244→
   245→__all__ = [
   246→    "apply_completion",
   247→    "count_log_activity_since",
   248→]
   249→
```

```
   107→        report=report,
   108→        valid_ids=accounting_ids,
   109→    )
   110→    if not accounting_ok:
   111→        return None
   112→
   113→    from .evidence_parsing import (
   114→        format_evidence_failures,
   115→        validate_reflect_skip_evidence,
   116→    )
   117→
   118→    blocking_skips = [
   119→        failure
   120→        for failure in validate_reflect_skip_evidence(report)
   121→        if failure.blocking
   122→    ]
   123→    if blocking_skips:
   124→        print(colorize(format_evidence_failures(blocking_skips, stage_label="reflect"), "red"))
   125→        return None
   126→
   127→    # Parse structured disposition ledger from Coverage Ledger section
   128→    disposition_ledger = parse_reflect_dispositions(report, valid_ids)
   129→
   130→    return (
   131→        triage_input,
   132→        issue_count,
   133→        recurring,
   134→        recurring_dims,
   135→        cited_ids,
   136→        missing_ids,
   137→        duplicate_ids,
   138→        disposition_ledger,
   139→    )
   140→
   141→
   142→def _persist_reflect_stage(
   143→    *,
   144→    plan: dict,
   145→    meta: dict,
   146→    stages: dict,
   147→    report: str,
   148→    issue_count: int,
   149→    cited_ids: set[str],
   150→    missing_ids: list[str],
   151→    duplicate_ids: list[str],
   152→    recurring_dims: list[str],
   153→    disposition_ledger: list[ReflectDisposition],
   154→    existing_stage: dict | None,
   155→    is_reuse: bool,
   156→    services: TriageServices,
   157→) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
   158→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   159→
   160→    # On fresh reflect run, cascade-clear reflect decisions from dispositions
   161→    if not is_reuse:
   162→        cascade_clear_dispositions(meta, "reflect")
   163→
   164→    reflect_stage: dict = {
   165→        "stage": "reflect",
   166→        "report": report,
   167→        "cited_ids": sorted(cited_ids),
   168→        "timestamp": utc_now(),
   169→        "issue_count": issue_count,
   170→        "missing_issue_ids": missing_ids,
   171→        "duplicate_issue_ids": duplicate_ids,
   172→        "recurring_dims": recurring_dims,
   173→    }
   174→    if disposition_ledger:
   175→        reflect_stage["disposition_ledger"] = [d.to_dict() for d in disposition_ledger]
   176→        # Write reflect decisions to the disposition map
   177→        dispositions = meta.setdefault("issue_dispositions", {})
   178→        for d in disposition_ledger:
   179→            entry = dispositions.setdefault(d.issue_id, {})
   180→            decision = "skip" if d.decision == "permanent_skip" else d.decision
   181→            entry["decision"] = decision
   182→            entry["target"] = d.target
   183→            entry["decision_source"] = "reflect"
   184→
   185→    stages["reflect"] = reflect_stage
   186→    if is_reuse and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("confirmed_at"):
   187→        reflect_stage["confirmed_at"] = existing_stage["confirmed_at"]
   188→        reflect_stage["confirmed_text"] = existing_stage.get("confirmed_text", "")
   189→    cleared = cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages, "reflect")
   190→
   191→    services.save_plan(plan)
   192→    services.append_log_entry(
   193→        plan,
   194→        "triage_reflect",
   195→        actor="user",
   196→        detail={"issue_count": issue_count, "reuse": is_reuse, "recurring_dims": recurring_dims},
   197→    )
   198→    services.save_plan(plan)
   199→    return reflect_stage, cleared
   200→
   201→
   202→def _cmd_stage_reflect(
   203→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   204→    *,
   205→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   206→) -> None:
   207→    """Record the REFLECT stage: compare current issues against completed work."""
   208→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   209→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   210→
   211→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   212→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   213→    state = runtime.state
   214→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   215→
   216→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   217→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to reflect on.", "yellow"))
   218→        return
   219→
   220→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   221→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   222→    existing_stage = stages.get("reflect")
   223→
   224→    report, is_reuse = resolve_reusable_report(report, existing_stage)
   225→    if not report:
   226→        _print_reflect_report_requirement()
   227→        return
   228→
   229→    submission = _validate_reflect_submission(
   230→        report=report,
   231→        plan=plan,
   232→        state=state,
   233→        stages=stages,
   234→        attestation=attestation,
   235→        services=resolved_services,
   236→    )
   237→    if submission is None:
   238→        return
   239→    (
   240→        triage_input, issue_count, recurring, recurring_dims,
   241→        cited_ids, missing_ids, duplicate_ids, disposition_ledger,
   242→    ) = submission
   243→    reflect_stage, cleared = _persist_reflect_stage(
   244→        plan=plan,
   245→        meta=meta,
   246→        stages=stages,
   247→        report=report,
   248→        issue_count=issue_count,
   249→        cited_ids=cited_ids,
   250→        missing_ids=missing_ids,
   251→        duplicate_ids=duplicate_ids,
   252→        recurring_dims=recurring_dims,
   253→        disposition_ledger=disposition_ledger,
   254→        existing_stage=existing_stage,
   255→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   256→        services=resolved_services,
   257→    )
   258→
   259→    print_reflect_result(
   260→        issue_count=issue_count,
   261→        recurring_dims=recurring_dims,
   262→        recurring=recurring,
   263→        report=report,
   264→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   265→        cleared=cleared,
   266→        stages=stages,
   267→    )
   268→
   269→
   270→def cmd_stage_reflect(
   271→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   272→    *,
   273→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   274→) -> None:
   275→    """Public entrypoint for reflect stage recording."""
   276→    _cmd_stage_reflect(args, services=services)
   277→
   278→
   279→__all__ = ["_cmd_stage_reflect", "cmd_stage_reflect"]
```

```
    37→    auto_clusters_broken_up: int = 0
    38→
    39→    @property
    40→    def clusters_created(self) -> int:
    41→        return self.epics_created
    42→
    43→    @property
    44→    def clusters_updated(self) -> int:
    45→        return self.epics_updated

    47→    @property
```
